 */
object CloudflareSolver {
    private const val TAG = "CloudflareSolver"
    private const val VAULT_PREFS = "cloudflare_clearance_vault"
    private const val DEFAULT_TIMEOUT_MS = 30_000L
    private const val VAULT_TTL_MS = 12 * 60 * 60 * 1000L // 12 hours

    private val BACKGROUND_TAGS = setOf("verify", "trending", "warmup", "hls-estimate", "background")

    @Volatile
    var isAppInForeground: Boolean = false

    @Volatile
    var isHostActive: Boolean = true

    @Volatile
    private var appContext: Context? = null

    data class ChallengeRequest(
        val targetUrl: String,
        val host: String,
        val referer: String?,
        val deferred: CompletableDeferred<Boolean>,
        val staleClearance: String?
    )

    private val _challengeState = MutableStateFlow<ChallengeRequest?>(null)
    val challengeState: StateFlow<ChallengeRequest?> = _challengeState.asStateFlow()

    private val solverMutex = Mutex()
    private val inFlightByHost = ConcurrentHashMap<String, CompletableDeferred<Boolean>>()

    fun init(context: Context) {
        appContext = context.applicationContext
        try {
            val defaultUa = WebSettings.getDefaultUserAgent(context)
            val cleanUa = defaultUa.replace("; wv", "")
            HttpClient.DEFAULT_UA = cleanUa
            Log.d(TAG, "Aligned HttpClient.DEFAULT_UA with native Android Chrome: $cleanUa")
        } catch (e: Exception) {
            Log.w(TAG, "Could not fetch default user agent: ${e.message}")
        }

        try {
            val prefs = context.getSharedPreferences(VAULT_PREFS, Context.MODE_PRIVATE)
            val now = System.currentTimeMillis()
            val all = prefs.all
            val cookieManager = CookieManager.getInstance()
            val editor = prefs.edit()
            var modified = false

            for ((domain, raw) in all) {
                val str = raw as? String ?: continue
                try {
                    val obj = JSONObject(str)
                    val token = obj.getString("token")
                    val ua = obj.getString("ua")
                    val expiresAtMs = obj.getLong("expiresAtMs")

                    if (expiresAtMs <= now || ua != HttpClient.DEFAULT_UA) {
                        editor.remove(domain)
                        modified = true
                        continue
                    }

                    val tokenName = obj.optString("tokenName", "cf_clearance")
                    val remainingSec = (expiresAtMs - now) / 1000L
                    if (remainingSec > 0) {
                        HttpClient.storeCookie(tokenName, token, domain, "/", remainingSec)
                        try {
                            cookieManager.setCookie("https://$domain", "$tokenName=$token; Domain=.$domain; Path=/")
                        } catch (_: Exception) {}
                        Log.d(TAG, "Seeded valid clearance token ($tokenName) for domain: $domain ($remainingSec sec remaining)")
                    }
                } catch (_: Exception) {
                    editor.remove(domain)
                    modified = true
                }
            }
            if (modified) editor.apply()
            try { cookieManager.flush() } catch (_: Exception) {}
        } catch (e: Exception) {
            Log.w(TAG, "Clearance vault init error: ${e.message}")
        }
    }

    fun canAttemptSolve(tag: String?): Boolean {
        if (!isHostActive || !isAppInForeground) return false
        if (tag != null && tag in BACKGROUND_TAGS) return false
        return true
    }

    /**
     * Evaluates whether a subresource requested by the challenge WebView should be allowed.
     * Always returns true for non-HTTP(S) schemes (blob:, data:, about:blank) required by Turnstile workers.
     * Drops heavy media, stylesheets, and tracking domains on non-Cloudflare origins.
     */
    fun shouldAllowSubresource(reqUrl: String, targetHost: String): Boolean {
        if (!reqUrl.startsWith("http://", ignoreCase = true) && !reqUrl.startsWith("https://", ignoreCase = true)) {
            return true
        }
        val httpUrl = reqUrl.toHttpUrlOrNull() ?: return true
        val host = httpUrl.host.lowercase()
        if (host == "challenges.cloudflare.com" ||
            host.endsWith(".cloudflare.com") ||
            host.endsWith(".turnstile.com") ||
            host.endsWith(".cloudflareinsights.com")
        ) {
            return true
        }
        val blockedDomains = listOf(
            "google-analytics.com", "googletagmanager.com", "doubleclick.net",
            "adservice.google.com", "yandex.ru", "mc.yandex.ru"
        )
        if (blockedDomains.any { host.contains(it) }) return false

        val path = httpUrl.encodedPath.lowercase()
        val blockedExtensions = listOf(
            ".png", ".jpg", ".jpeg", ".gif", ".webp", ".svg", ".ico",
            ".mp4", ".mkv", ".m3u8", ".ts",
            ".woff", ".woff2", ".ttf", ".otf",
            ".css"
        )
        if (blockedExtensions.any { path.endsWith(it) }) {
            return false
        }

        return true
    }

    fun rootDomain(hostOrUrl: String): String {
        val h = if (hostOrUrl.contains("://")) {
            try {
                hostOrUrl.toHttpUrlOrNull()?.host ?: URI(hostOrUrl).host ?: hostOrUrl
            } catch (_: Exception) {
                hostOrUrl
            }
        } else {
            hostOrUrl
        }.lowercase().trim().removePrefix("www.")

        val httpUrl = try {
            HttpUrl.Builder().scheme("https").host(h).build()
        } catch (_: Exception) {
            null
        }
        return httpUrl?.topPrivateDomain() ?: h
    }

    fun resolveChallengeTargetUrl(reqUrl: String, referer: String?): String {
        return try {
            val uri = URI(reqUrl)
            val path = uri.path?.lowercase() ?: ""
            val isEndpoint = path.contains("/wp-admin/") ||
                path.contains("/api/") ||
                path.contains("/wp-json/") ||
                path.endsWith(".php") ||
                path.endsWith(".json")
            if (isEndpoint) {
                if (!referer.isNullOrBlank() && referer.startsWith("http")) {
                    referer
                } else {
                    "${uri.scheme ?: "https"}://${uri.host}/"
                }
            } else {
                reqUrl
            }
        } catch (_: Exception) {
            reqUrl
        }
    }

    fun solveSync(url: String, referer: String? = null, tag: String? = null): Boolean {
        check(Looper.myLooper() != Looper.getMainLooper()) {
            "CloudflareSolver.solveSync must never be called on the Main looper"
        }
        if (!canAttemptSolve(tag)) return false
        return runBlocking(Dispatchers.IO) {
            solve(url, referer, tag)
        }
    }

    suspend fun solve(url: String, referer: String? = null, tag: String? = null): Boolean {
        if (!canAttemptSolve(tag)) return false
        val targetUrl = resolveChallengeTargetUrl(url, referer)
        val host = try {
            URI(targetUrl).host?.lowercase() ?: ""
        } catch (_: Exception) { "" }
        if (host.isBlank()) return false
        val root = rootDomain(host)

        // Capture the stale token BEFORE waiting on any lock
        val staleClearance = HttpClient.cookieValue("cf_clearance", root)
            ?: HttpClient.cookieValue("hvp", root)
            ?: extractToken(try { CookieManager.getInstance().getCookie(targetUrl) } catch (_: Throwable) { null })?.second

        // 1. Per-host single-flight coalescing OUTSIDE solverMutex
        val existing = inFlightByHost[root]
        if (existing != null) {
            return try {
                existing.await()
            } catch (ce: CancellationException) {
                throw ce
            } catch (_: Exception) {
                false
            }
        }
        val myDeferred = CompletableDeferred<Boolean>()
        val prev = inFlightByHost.putIfAbsent(root, myDeferred)
        if (prev != null) {
            return try {
                prev.await()
            } catch (ce: CancellationException) {
                throw ce
            } catch (_: Exception) {
                false
            }
        }

        // 2. Global 1-WebView cap across all hosts
        return try {
            solverMutex.withLock {
                if (!canAttemptSolve(tag)) {
                    myDeferred.complete(false)
                    return@withLock false
                }

                // Check if a fresh token was already minted while waiting for solverMutex
                val currentToken = HttpClient.cookieValue("cf_clearance", root)
                    ?: HttpClient.cookieValue("hvp", root)
                if (!currentToken.isNullOrBlank() && currentToken != staleClearance) {
                    myDeferred.complete(true)
                    return@withLock true
                }

                // Purge the rejected stale cookie from both HttpClient and CookieManager
                HttpClient.purgeCookie("cf_clearance", root)
                HttpClient.purgeCookie("hvp", root)
                try {
                    val cm = CookieManager.getInstance()
                    cm.setCookie(targetUrl, "cf_clearance=; Max-Age=0; Path=/")
                    cm.setCookie("https://$root", "cf_clearance=; Domain=.$root; Max-Age=0; Path=/")
                    cm.setCookie(targetUrl, "hvp=; Max-Age=0; Path=/")
                    cm.setCookie("https://$root", "hvp=; Domain=.$root; Max-Age=0; Path=/")
                    cm.flush()
                } catch (_: Throwable) {}

                val req = ChallengeRequest(
                    targetUrl = targetUrl,
                    host = root,
                    referer = referer,
                    deferred = myDeferred,
                    staleClearance = staleClearance
                )

                _challengeState.value = req

                try {
                    withTimeoutOrNull(DEFAULT_TIMEOUT_MS) {
                        myDeferred.await()
                    } ?: false
                } catch (e: CancellationException) {
                    myDeferred.complete(false)
                    false
                } finally {
                    if (!myDeferred.isCompleted) {
                        myDeferred.complete(false)
                    }
                    if (_challengeState.value === req) {
                        _challengeState.value = null
                    }
                }
            }
        } finally {
            if (!myDeferred.isCompleted) {
                myDeferred.complete(false)
            }
            inFlightByHost.remove(root, myDeferred)
        }
    }

    fun resolve(request: ChallengeRequest, success: Boolean, clearanceToken: String? = null, tokenName: String = "cf_clearance") {
        if (success && !clearanceToken.isNullOrBlank()) {
            val ttlSec = VAULT_TTL_MS / 1000L
            HttpClient.storeCookie(tokenName, clearanceToken, request.host, "/", ttlSec)
            // Also sync companion cookies (__cf_bm, _cfuvid, hv*) set during the WebView challenge
            try {
                val cm = CookieManager.getInstance()
                cm.flush()
                val rawCookies = cm.getCookie(request.targetUrl).orEmpty()
                for (part in rawCookies.split(";")) {
                    val eq = part.indexOf('=')
                    if (eq <= 0) continue
                    val k = part.substring(0, eq).trim()
                    val v = part.substring(eq + 1).trim()
                    if (k.isNotBlank() && v.isNotBlank()) {
                        HttpClient.storeCookie(k, v, request.host, "/", ttlSec)
                    }
                }
            } catch (_: Throwable) {}
            appContext?.let { ctx ->
                persistClearance(ctx, request.host, clearanceToken, HttpClient.DEFAULT_UA, tokenName)
            }
        }
        request.deferred.complete(success)
        if (_challengeState.value === request) {
            _challengeState.value = null
        }
    }

    fun persistClearance(context: Context, host: String, token: String, ua: String, tokenName: String = "cf_clearance") {
        val root = rootDomain(host)
        val now = System.currentTimeMillis()
        val expiresAt = now + VAULT_TTL_MS
        try {
            val json = JSONObject().apply {
                put("token", token)
                put("tokenName", tokenName)
                put("ua", ua)
                put("expiresAtMs", expiresAt)
            }
            context.getSharedPreferences(VAULT_PREFS, Context.MODE_PRIVATE)
                .edit()
                .putString(root, json.toString())
                .apply()
        } catch (e: Exception) {
            Log.w(TAG, "Failed to persist clearance for $root: ${e.message}")
        }
    }

    fun extractToken(cookieString: String?): Pair<String, String>? {
        if (cookieString.isNullOrBlank()) return null
        val cfRegex = Regex("""cf_clearance=([a-zA-Z0-9_.~-]+)""")
        val cfMatch = cfRegex.find(cookieString)
        if (cfMatch != null) {
            return Pair("cf_clearance", cfMatch.groupValues[1])
        }
        val hvpRegex = Regex("""hvp=([a-zA-Z0-9_.~-]+)""")
        val hvpMatch = hvpRegex.find(cookieString)
        if (hvpMatch != null) {
            return Pair("hvp", hvpMatch.groupValues[1])
        }
        return null
    }
}

            when (event) {
                Lifecycle.Event.ON_RESUME -> CloudflareSolver.isHostActive = true
                Lifecycle.Event.ON_PAUSE, Lifecycle.Event.ON_STOP, Lifecycle.Event.ON_DESTROY -> CloudflareSolver.isHostActive = false

/**
 * Skeleton Subresource Firewall rule evaluator.
 *
 * Blocks heavy non-critical assets (images, media, fonts, stylesheets on non-Cloudflare hosts)
 * returning HTTP 204 No Content, while whitelisting Cloudflare challenge engines.
 */
internal fun shouldBlockSubresource(uri: Uri): Boolean {
    return !CloudflareSolver.shouldAllowSubresource(uri.toString(), "")
}

internal fun shouldBlockSubresource(scheme: String, host: String, path: String): Boolean {
    val fullUrl = if (scheme.isBlank()) host else "$scheme://$host$path"
    return !CloudflareSolver.shouldAllowSubresource(fullUrl, host)
}

        body: String = "",
        url: String = "https://example.com/page"

        val builder = Response.Builder()
            .request(req)
            .protocol(Protocol.HTTP_1_1)
            .code(code)
            .message("Status $code")
            .body(body.toResponseBody())

        headers.forEach { (k, v) -> builder.header(k, v) }
        return builder.build()
    }

    fun isCloudflareChallenge_normal403OnCloudflareDoesNotTrigger() {

                "Server" to "cloudflare",
                "cf-ray" to "8d94bc72a1-DFW",
                "Content-Type" to "video/mp4"

            body = "Access Denied"

        assertFalse(HttpClient.isCloudflareChallenge(res))

                "cf-ray" to "8d94bc72a1-DFW"

        )
        assertTrue(HttpClient.isCloudflareChallenge(res))

    @Test
    fun isCloudflareChallenge_htmlJustAMomentTriggers() {

        val res = mockResponse(
            code = 403,
            headers = mapOf(
                "Server" to "cloudflare",
                "Content-Type" to "text/html; charset=UTF-8"

            body = html
        )

        val res = mockResponse(

                    "WARM ${safeUrl(url)} FAILED ${e.javaClass.simpleName}: ${e.message}"
                )
                return false
            } finally {
                inFlightCalls.remove(call)
            }
        } finally {
            if (admitted) OriginLoadScheduler.release(url, cls)
        }
    }

    /** Tests only: the scheduler class warm-up traffic takes (must be
     *  DOWNLOAD, i.e. never the SEARCH budget). */
    internal fun warmupRequestClassForTest(): OriginRequestClass = requestClass(WARMUP_TAG)

    /**
     * Hybrid Smart-DNS:
     * 1. Primary: System DNS (fast, geo-routes CDN IPs for max video speeds).
     *    Capped at 3 s — on some Nigerian ISPs the carrier DNS server goes
     *    unresponsive (not NXDOMAIN, just silent), blocking getaddrinfo for up
     *    to 75 s before timing out. Three seconds is enough for a healthy
     *    system DNS; anything slower falls through to DoH immediately.
     * 2. Fallback: Google Public DNS over HTTPS (bypasses ISP DNS poisoning /
     *    censorship on blocked scraper sites).
     */
    private val hybridDns = object : okhttp3.Dns {
        override fun lookup(hostname: String): List<java.net.InetAddress> {
            dohCache[hostname]?.let { return it }
            // Bounded system-DNS race: fixed workers + bounded queue, DoH on
            // timeout/saturation/interrupt (see BoundedDnsScheduler).
            return dnsScheduler.lookup(hostname)
        }
    }

    private fun dohFallback(hostname: String): List<java.net.InetAddress> {
        return try {
            val encoded = java.net.URLEncoder.encode(hostname, "UTF-8")
            val dohUrl = "https://dns.google/resolve?name=$encoded&type=A"
            val req = Request.Builder()
                .url(dohUrl)
                .header("User-Agent", DEFAULT_UA)
                .build()
            bootstrapDohClient.newCall(req).execute().use { res ->
                if (!res.isSuccessful) throw java.net.UnknownHostException(hostname)
                val body = res.body?.string() ?: throw java.net.UnknownHostException(hostname)
                val json = org.json.JSONObject(body)
                val answers = json.optJSONArray("Answer") ?: throw java.net.UnknownHostException(hostname)
                val addrs = mutableListOf<java.net.InetAddress>()
                for (i in 0 until answers.length()) {
                    val ans = answers.getJSONObject(i)
                    val type = ans.optInt("type")
                    val data = ans.optString("data")
                    // type 1 = A (IPv4): parse literal octets directly to prevent getByName
                    // from triggering native getaddrinfo on CNAME domain names when ISP DNS is dead.
                    if (type == 1 && data.isNotBlank() && !data.contains(":")) {
                        val parts = data.split('.').mapNotNull { it.toIntOrNull() }
                        if (parts.size == 4 && parts.all { it in 0..255 }) {
                            val bytes = ByteArray(4) { parts[it].toByte() }
                            addrs.add(java.net.InetAddress.getByAddress(hostname, bytes))
                        }
                    }
                }
                if (addrs.isEmpty()) throw java.net.UnknownHostException(hostname)
                dohCache[hostname] = addrs
                addrs
            }
        } catch (e: java.net.UnknownHostException) {
            throw e
        } catch (_: Exception) {
            throw java.net.UnknownHostException(hostname)
        }
    }


    /**
     * Tests only: replace the whole DNS pipeline (system race + DoH + SSRF
     * floor) so MockWebServer's loopback origins can exercise the REAL request
     * paths. Production leaves this null. A test that sets it MUST reset it in
     * @After — the SSRF floor is a security boundary, not a preference.
     */
    internal var dnsForTest: okhttp3.Dns? = null

    /**
     * SSRF floor for every PAGE/RESOLVER fetch: after the hybrid resolver, drop
     * any address that points into private/loopback/link-local/metadata space.
     * A hostile or compromised page we merely fetch can declare a URL that names
     * the user's router (192.168.x), the LAN, or a cloud metadata endpoint
     * (169.254.169.254); making DNS refuse those targets is the one check that
     * cannot be bypassed by redirect chains (OkHttp re-consults Dns per connect)
     * or by odd IP spellings (they all resolve to the same InetAddress).
     * If EVERY address is private the host is unresolvable to us by design.
     */
    private val safeDns = object : okhttp3.Dns {
        override fun lookup(hostname: String): List<java.net.InetAddress> {
            dnsForTest?.let { return it.lookup(hostname) }
            val resolved = hybridDns.lookup(hostname)
            val safe = resolved.filterNot { isBlockedAddress(it) }
            if (safe.isEmpty()) {
                throw java.net.UnknownHostException(
                    "$hostname resolves only to private/link-local addresses — refused (SSRF guard)"
                )
            }
            return rotateRoutes(hostname, safe)
        }
    }

    private val trustAllCerts = arrayOf<javax.net.ssl.TrustManager>(object : javax.net.ssl.X509TrustManager {
        override fun checkClientTrusted(chain: Array<out java.security.cert.X509Certificate>?, authType: String?) {}
        override fun checkServerTrusted(chain: Array<out java.security.cert.X509Certificate>?, authType: String?) {}
        override fun getAcceptedIssuers(): Array<java.security.cert.X509Certificate> = arrayOf()
    })

    private val sslSocketFactory: javax.net.ssl.SSLSocketFactory by lazy {
        val sslContext = javax.net.ssl.SSLContext.getInstance("TLS")
        sslContext.init(null, trustAllCerts, java.security.SecureRandom())
        sslContext.socketFactory
    }

    val shared: OkHttpClient = OkHttpClient.Builder()
        .dns(safeDns)
        .connectionPool(pool)
        .dispatcher(dispatcher)
        .cookieJar(sessionCookieJar)
        .connectTimeout(10, TimeUnit.SECONDS)
        .readTimeout(15, TimeUnit.SECONDS)
        .writeTimeout(10, TimeUnit.SECONDS)
        .followRedirects(true)
        .followSslRedirects(true)
        .retryOnConnectionFailure(true)
        .build()

    val downloadClient: OkHttpClient = shared.newBuilder()
        // The DOWNLOAD plane deliberately keeps the raw hybrid DNS: a download
        // URL is user-chosen (a shared/pasted link, a picked episode), not
        // page-injected, and users legitimately pull files from a LAN server.
        // The SSRF floor guards the page/redirect-following plane, where hosts
        // are chosen by remote content. permissiveClient derives from shared
        // and keeps safeDns — it serves resolver traffic (broken-TLS lockers).
        .dns(hybridDns)
        // HTTP/1.1 only: with the default HTTP_2 ALPN, OkHttp coalesces every
        // concurrent Range request to one host onto a SINGLE TCP connection —
        // silently defeating Turbo's multi-socket throttle bypass and making
        // the whole transfer ramp on one connection's slow start (part of the
        // user-visible 100KB → 3MB crawl). N sockets must mean N real
        // connections; aria2c behaves the same (no h2). Page/resolver traffic
        // on [shared] keeps HTTP/2.
        .protocols(listOf(Protocol.HTTP_1_1))
        .connectTimeout(15, TimeUnit.SECONDS)
        .readTimeout(30, TimeUnit.SECONDS)
        .writeTimeout(15, TimeUnit.SECONDS)
        .build()

    /**
     * Trust-all SSL client for locker hosts with broken TLS chains
     * (wetafiles.com omits its intermediate, kissorgrab.com serves an
     * invalid cert). Used ONLY by DownloadwellaResolver (downloadwella
     * family) and the permissive probe fallback — the shared client stays
     * strict because trust-all must never apply to every request the app
     * makes.
     */
    val permissiveClient: OkHttpClient by lazy {
        shared.newBuilder()
            .sslSocketFactory(sslSocketFactory, trustAllCerts[0] as javax.net.ssl.X509TrustManager)
            .hostnameVerifier { _, _ -> true }
            .build()
    }

    /**
     * Trust-all variant of [downloadClient] (longer streaming timeouts) for
     * the download path: when a strict probe proves the chain is broken, the
     * whole turbo job must run trust-all — mixing a permissive probe with
     * strict sockets would just re-trigger the same handshake failure on all
     * 16 segments. Only reached after [isTlsChainFailure] matched.
     */
    val permissiveDownloadClient: OkHttpClient by lazy {
        downloadClient.newBuilder()
            .sslSocketFactory(sslSocketFactory, trustAllCerts[0] as javax.net.ssl.X509TrustManager)
            .hostnameVerifier { _, _ -> true }
            .build()
    }

    /**
     * Execute a one-off probe call under the same cancellation registry as
     * [get] — pausing/cancelling a task must also kill the StreamValidator /
     * turbo probe so no straggler socket keeps draining data (v3.0.4 showed
     * traffic continuing seconds after a cancel).
     */
    fun executeRegistered(call: okhttp3.Call): okhttp3.Response {
        inFlightCalls.add(call)
        try {
            return call.execute()
        } catch (e: Exception) {
            if (call.isCanceled()) {
                throw kotlinx.coroutines.CancellationException("HTTP call canceled").apply { initCause(e) }
            }
            throw e
        } finally {
            inFlightCalls.remove(call)
        }
    }

    fun safeResolveUri(base: String, relative: String): String {
        if (relative.startsWith("http://", ignoreCase = true) || relative.startsWith("https://", ignoreCase = true) || relative.startsWith("magnet:", ignoreCase = true)) {
            return relative
        }
        return try {
            val safeBase = safeUrl(base)
            val safeRel = relative.replace(" ", "%20").replace("[", "%5B").replace("]", "%5D")
            java.net.URI(safeBase).resolve(safeRel).toString()
        } catch (_: Exception) {
            if (relative.startsWith("/")) {
                val root = base.substringBefore("://") + "://" + base.substringAfter("://").substringBefore("/")
                root + relative
            } else {
                base.trimEnd('/') + "/" + relative.trimStart('/')
            }
        }
    }

    fun safeHost(url: String, defaultHost: String = ""): String {
        return try {
            val clean = url.substringBefore('?').substringBefore('#')
            val afterProto = if (clean.contains("://")) clean.substringAfter("://") else clean
            afterProto.substringBefore('/').substringBefore(':').ifBlank { defaultHost }
        } catch (_: Exception) {
            defaultHost
        }
    }

    /**
     * The TRUE host of [url] per okhttp3.HttpUrl — the same parser that decides
     * which server a request actually connects to. [safeHost] is a lenient
     * string-split with legacy callers and MUST NOT be used for security
     * decisions: HttpUrl.kt 4.12.0 ends the host at `@ / \ ? #` and strips
     * userinfo, so "https://vikingfile.com:443@evil.com/f" really fetches
     * evil.com while safeHost() cheerfully answers "vikingfile.com". Any
     * allowlist gate must compare against THIS function (fact-checked
     * 2026-09-12 against parent-4.12.0 HttpUrl.kt parse(), authority loop).
     * Null for anything HttpUrl itself refuses.
     */
    fun parsedHost(url: String): String? {
        return try {
            parseHttpUrl(safeUrl(url))?.host?.lowercase()
        } catch (_: Exception) {
            null
        }
    }

    /**
     * Single chokepoint for okhttp URL parsing in the security gates.
     * HttpUrl.parse is DEPRECATION-ERROR level against okhttp 4.12.0 (an
     * @Suppress("DEPRECATION") does not silence it), and the recommended
     * String.toHttpUrlOrNull extension does not resolve from this CI's Kotlin
     * setup — so we route through Request.Builder.url(), which delegates to
     * the SAME non-lenient HttpUrl parser (same userinfo/host canonicalization
     * the safety comment above relies on) and is not deprecated anywhere.
     * Malformed input throws IllegalArgumentException where parse would
     * return null; identical net semantics. Do not add raw HttpUrl.parse
     * call sites.
     */
    internal fun parseHttpUrl(url: String): okhttp3.HttpUrl? = try {
        okhttp3.Request.Builder().url(url).build().url
    } catch (_: IllegalArgumentException) {
        null
    }

    internal fun parseMediaType(mediaType: String): okhttp3.MediaType? = try {
        mediaType.toMediaTypeOrNull()
    } catch (_: IllegalArgumentException) {
        null
    }

    fun safeUrl(url: String): String {
        if (url.isBlank()) return url
        val parts = url.split("?", limit = 2)
        val base = encodeBaseKeepingIpv6Literal(parts[0])
        return if (parts.size > 1) "$base?${parts[1].replace(" ", "%20")}" else base
    }

    /** Encode stray `[`/`]` and spaces, but PRESERVE a well-formed IPv6 host
     *  literal (`scheme://[v6]:port/path`). The old blanket encode broke every
     *  IPv6 URL into `%5Bfd00::5%5D`, which HttpUrl.parse then refused — so the
     *  v6 branch of [isSafeTarget] was dead and LAN/NAS targets written as v6
     *  literals were unreachable. OkHttp parses the bracketed form and returns
     *  a bare `fd00::5` host, which then flows through isBlockedAddress. */
    private fun encodeBaseKeepingIpv6Literal(base: String): String {
        val schemeEnd = base.indexOf("://")
        if (schemeEnd < 0) return base.replace("[", "%5B").replace("]", "%5D").replace(" ", "%20")
        val afterScheme = schemeEnd + 3
        if (afterScheme < base.length && base[afterScheme] == '[') {
            val close = base.indexOf(']', afterScheme)
            if (close > afterScheme) {
                val literal = base.substring(0, close + 1)          // "http://[fd00::5]"
                val rest = base.substring(close + 1)
                return literal + rest.replace("[", "%5B").replace("]", "%5D").replace(" ", "%20")
            }
        }
        return base.replace("[", "%5B").replace("]", "%5D").replace(" ", "%20")
    }

    /**
     * Cheap, DNS-free pre-filter for a target URL before any fetch. This is a
     * FAST path, not the security boundary — [safeDns] is the real gate (it
     * catches every odd IP spelling and every DNS rebind at connect time).
     * What it guards here: non-http(s) schemes, service ports that no locker
     * host uses (ssh/smtp/db/admin), and IP-literal hosts that are already
     * obviously private (so we never even attempt the connect).
     * HttpUrl.parse canonicalizes userinfo ("http://evil@127.0.0.1/") out of
     * the host — asserted by HttpClientSafetyTest; do not hand string-split.
     */
    private val SERVICE_PORTS = setOf(
        21, 22, 23, 25, 53, 110, 135, 137, 139, 143, 445, 1433, 2049, 3306,
        3389, 5432, 5984, 6379, 9200, 11211, 27017
    )

    fun isSafeTarget(url: String): Boolean {
        val parsed = parseHttpUrl(safeUrl(url)) ?: return false
        if (parsed.scheme != "http" && parsed.scheme != "https") return false
        if (parsed.port in SERVICE_PORTS) return false
        val host = parsed.host
        if (host.isBlank()) return false
        // IP-literal hosts (v4 quad, decimal/hex single-token, or any v6 form)
        // get the full address check WITHOUT touching the network; plain
        // hostnames are deferred to safeDns, which is the real boundary.
        val bare = if (host.startsWith("[")) host.removeSurrounding("[", "]") else host
        val looksLikeIp = bare.indexOf(':') >= 0 ||
            (bare.isNotEmpty() && bare[0].isDigit() && !bare.any { it.isLetter() || it == '-' })
        if (looksLikeIp) {
            val addr = try { java.net.InetAddress.getByName(bare) } catch (_: Exception) {
                return false // unparseable "numeric" host: refuse it
            }
            if (isBlockedAddress(addr)) return false
        }
        return true
    }

    /** get()/postForm()/getText() entry guard: throw (their existing failure
     *  channels already log throws) instead of silently connecting. */
    private fun refuseUnsafeTarget(url: String) {
        if (!isSafeTarget(url)) {
            lastFailure = "unsafe target refused: ${url.take(120)}"
            throw java.io.IOException("Refused unsafe target: ${url.take(160)}")
        }
    }

    fun get(url: String, referer: String? = null, headers: Map<String, String> = emptyMap(), tag: String? = null, permissive: Boolean = false): Response =
        executeGet(url, referer, headers, tag, permissive) { it }

    // Raw get() still transfers response ownership to its caller. getText() instead
    // consumes inside this scope, retaining cancellation registration during reads.
    private fun <T> executeGet(url: String, referer: String?, headers: Map<String, String>, tag: String?, permissive: Boolean, client: OkHttpClient = if (permissive) permissiveClient else shared, consume: (Response) -> T): T {
        // Cooldown + metering: the class comes from the existing tag, so a
        // download fan-out's 429 can no longer park SEARCH on the same origin
        // and the per-origin scheduler keeps search ahead of verify/fan-out.
        admitRequest(url, tag)
        val cls = requestClass(tag)
        val admitted = OriginLoadScheduler.acquire(url, cls)
        try {
            return executeGetInner(url, referer, headers, tag, permissive, client, consume)
        } finally {
            if (admitted) OriginLoadScheduler.release(url, cls)
        }
    }

    private fun <T> executeGetInner(url: String, referer: String?, headers: Map<String, String>, tag: String?, permissive: Boolean, client: OkHttpClient = if (permissive) permissiveClient else shared, consume: (Response) -> T): T {
        // SSRF floor, page plane. safeDns filters DNS-resolved hosts, but OkHttp
        // SKIPS the custom Dns for IP-literal hosts (RouteSelector:
        // canParseAsIpAddress -> raw getByName; fact-checked against 4.12.0
        // source). isSafeTarget closes that gap + service ports pre-flight.
        refuseUnsafeTarget(url)
        val reqBuilder = Request.Builder()
            .url(safeUrl(url))
            .header("User-Agent", DEFAULT_UA)
            .header("Accept", "text/html,application/xhtml+xml,application/xml;q=0.9,image/avif,image/webp,*/*;q=0.8")
            .header("Accept-Language", "en-US,en;q=0.9")

        val isXhrOrJson = headers["X-Requested-With"]?.equals("XMLHttpRequest", ignoreCase = true) == true ||
            headers["Accept"].orEmpty().contains("json", ignoreCase = true)
        if (!isXhrOrJson) {
            reqBuilder.header("Sec-Fetch-Dest", "document")
            reqBuilder.header("Sec-Fetch-Mode", "navigate")
            reqBuilder.header("Sec-Fetch-Site", if (referer.isNullOrBlank()) "none" else "same-origin")
            reqBuilder.header("Sec-Fetch-User", "?1")
            reqBuilder.header("Upgrade-Insecure-Requests", "1")
        } else {
            reqBuilder.header("Sec-Fetch-Dest", "empty")
            reqBuilder.header("Sec-Fetch-Mode", "cors")
            reqBuilder.header("Sec-Fetch-Site", "same-origin")
        }

        if (!referer.isNullOrBlank()) {
            reqBuilder.header("Referer", referer)
        }
        headers.forEach { (k, v) -> reqBuilder.header(k, v) }

        fun register(c: okhttp3.Call) {
            inFlightCalls.add(c)
            if (tag != null) {
                taggedCalls.computeIfAbsent(tag) { java.util.concurrent.CopyOnWriteArrayList() }.add(c)
            }
        }
        fun unregister(c: okhttp3.Call) {
            inFlightCalls.remove(c)
            if (tag != null) taggedCalls[tag]?.remove(c)
        }

        var call = client.newCall(reqBuilder.build())
        register(call)
        var attempt = 0
        val started = System.currentTimeMillis()
        return try {
            var res = try {
                call.execute()
            } catch (e: Exception) {
                if (call.isCanceled()) {
                    throw kotlinx.coroutines.CancellationException("HTTP call canceled").apply { initCause(e) }
                }
                throw e
            }
            com.anonrode.downloader.util.DebugLog.net(
                "GET ${safeUrl(url)} -> ${res.code} in ${System.currentTimeMillis() - started}ms"
            )
            if (res.code == 451 && attempt == 0) {
                // ONE same-request retry: a legal-block page served by one
                // anycast edge must not mask the healthy sibling address.
                noteHttp451(url, res)
                res.close()
                try { client.connectionPool.evictAll() } catch (_: Exception) {}
                unregister(call)
                attempt++
                call = client.newCall(reqBuilder.build())
                register(call)
                res = try {
                    call.execute()
                } catch (e: Exception) {
                    if (call.isCanceled()) {
                        throw kotlinx.coroutines.CancellationException("HTTP call canceled").apply { initCause(e) }
                    }
                    throw e
                }
                com.anonrode.downloader.util.DebugLog.net(
                    "GET ${safeUrl(url)} retry-after-451 -> ${res.code} in ${System.currentTimeMillis() - started}ms"
                )
            }

            if (android.os.Looper.myLooper() != android.os.Looper.getMainLooper() &&
                CloudflareSolver.canAttemptSolve(tag) &&
                isCloudflareChallenge(res) &&
                attempt == 0) {
                val priorReq = res.request
                val priorProtocol = res.protocol
                val priorCode = res.code
                val priorMessage = res.message
                val priorHeaders = res.headers
                val challengeUrl = priorReq.url.toString()

                res.close()
                unregister(call)

                val solved = CloudflareSolver.solveSync(challengeUrl, referer, tag)
                if (solved) {
                    com.anonrode.downloader.pipeline.HostHealth.clearIfAlive(challengeUrl)
                    reqBuilder.header("User-Agent", DEFAULT_UA)
                    attempt++
                    call = client.newCall(reqBuilder.build())
                    register(call)
                    res = try {
                        call.execute()
                    } catch (e: Exception) {
                        if (call.isCanceled()) {
                            throw kotlinx.coroutines.CancellationException("HTTP call canceled").apply { initCause(e) }
                        }
                        throw e
                    }
                    com.anonrode.downloader.util.DebugLog.net(
                        "GET ${safeUrl(url)} retry-after-challenge -> ${res.code} in ${System.currentTimeMillis() - started}ms"
                    )
                } else {
                    res = Response.Builder()
                        .request(priorReq)
                        .protocol(priorProtocol)
                        .code(priorCode)
                        .message(priorMessage)
                        .headers(priorHeaders)
                        .body(okhttp3.ResponseBody.create(null, ByteArray(0)))
                        .build()
                }
            }
            consume(res)
        } catch (cancelled: kotlinx.coroutines.CancellationException) {
            throw cancelled
        } catch (e: Exception) {
            com.anonrode.downloader.util.DebugLog.net(
                "GET ${safeUrl(url)} FAILED ${e.javaClass.simpleName}: ${e.message} after ${System.currentTimeMillis() - started}ms"
            )
            throw e
        } finally {
            unregister(call)
        }
    }

    /**
     * In-flight resolver/probe calls. pause()/cancel() cancel these so a hung
     * connect or a slow header phase cannot outlive the task that started it.
     * Body reads are separately bounded by [MAX_TEXT_BYTES] — the actual data
     * drain guard: a resolver misdirected onto a direct file URL can no longer
     * stream the whole video into memory.
     */
    private val inFlightCalls = java.util.concurrent.CopyOnWriteArrayList<okhttp3.Call>()

    /**
     * Calls registered under a tag (e.g. "search") can be cancelled as a group
     * when a newer call of the same kind supersedes them. A cancelled search's
     * coroutine dies instantly, but its blocking OkHttp calls keep running
     * until they finish — on mobile that meant every keystroke left ~10 stale
     * requests draining data for seconds after the next search started.
     */
    private val taggedCalls = java.util.concurrent.ConcurrentHashMap<String, java.util.concurrent.CopyOnWriteArrayList<okhttp3.Call>>()

    /** Cancel every in-flight resolver/probe HTTP call (user paused/cancelled). */
    fun cancelInFlight() {
        // A user pause/cancel must not kill their live search: search calls are
        // tagged separately and get cancelled only when a newer search supersedes
        // them (cancelTagged). The log showed pausing one download aborting
        // unrelated in-flight searches mid-keystroke.
        val searchCalls = taggedCalls["search"]
        val strategyCalls = taggedCalls["search-strategy"]
        val trendingCalls = taggedCalls["trending"]
        val browseCalls = taggedCalls["browse"]
        val otaCalls = taggedCalls["ota_rules"]
        inFlightCalls.removeIf { c ->
            val keep = searchCalls?.contains(c) == true ||
                strategyCalls?.contains(c) == true ||
                trendingCalls?.contains(c) == true ||
                browseCalls?.contains(c) == true ||
                otaCalls?.contains(c) == true
            if (!keep) {
                try { c.cancel() } catch (_: Exception) {}
            }
            !keep
        }
    }

    /** Cancel only the calls tagged [tag] (a superseded search, etc.). */
    fun cancelTagged(tag: String) {
        taggedCalls[tag]?.let { calls ->
            for (c in calls) {
                try { c.cancel() } catch (_: Exception) {}
            }
        }
        taggedCalls.remove(tag)
    }

    /**
     * Registration covers headers AND body reads; the response cannot escape this scope.
     * Synchronous: registry cancellation only, NOT automatically bound to a coroutine Job.
     * Callers needing Job cancellation must supply a per-call bridge; never cancel globally.
     */
    internal inline fun <T> executeCancellable(client: OkHttpClient, req: Request, tag: String? = null, block: (Response) -> T): T {
        val permitUrl = req.url.toString()
        val permitClass = when (requestScope(tag)) {
            RetryAfterCooldown.SCOPE_SEARCH -> OriginRequestClass.SEARCH
            RetryAfterCooldown.SCOPE_VERIFY -> OriginRequestClass.VERIFY
            else -> OriginRequestClass.DOWNLOAD
        }
        val admitted = OriginLoadScheduler.acquire(permitUrl, permitClass)
        try {
            val call = registerResolverCall(client, req, tag)
            try {
                return executeResolverCall(call, tag).use(block)
            } finally {
                unregisterResolverCall(call, tag)
            }
        } finally {
            if (admitted) OriginLoadScheduler.release(permitUrl, permitClass)
        }
    }

    @PublishedApi
    internal fun registerResolverCall(client: OkHttpClient, req: Request, tag: String? = null): okhttp3.Call {
        refuseUnsafeTarget(req.url.toString())
        admitRequest(req.url.toString())
        val call = client.newCall(req)
        inFlightCalls.add(call)
        if (tag != null) {
            taggedCalls.computeIfAbsent(tag) { java.util.concurrent.CopyOnWriteArrayList() }.add(call)
        }
        return call
    }

    @PublishedApi
    internal fun executeResolverCall(call: okhttp3.Call, tag: String? = null): Response {
        val response = try {
            call.execute()
        } catch (e: Exception) {
            if (call.isCanceled()) {
                throw kotlinx.coroutines.CancellationException("HTTP call canceled").apply { initCause(e) }
            }
            throw e
        }
        recordCooldown(response, tag)
        if (response.code == 429 || response.code == 503) {
            val url = response.request.url.toString()
            response.close()
            throw OriginCooldownException(url)
        }
        return response
    }

    @PublishedApi
    internal fun unregisterResolverCall(call: okhttp3.Call, tag: String? = null) {
        inFlightCalls.remove(call)
        if (tag != null) {
            taggedCalls[tag]?.remove(call)
        }
    }

    /** Remaining per-origin cooldown ms (0 = usable). */
    fun remainingCooldownMs(url: String, scope: String = RetryAfterCooldown.SCOPE_DOWNLOAD): Long =
        retryAfterCooldown.remainingMs(safeUrl(url), scope = scope)

    /**
     * Hard cap on any body read through [cappedText]/[cappedBytes]. Resolver
     * responses are HTML/JSON/wasm — kilobytes. A response larger than this
     * is by definition not a page (a misdirected file fetch), and reading it
     * would burn the user's mobile data for nothing.
     */
    const val MAX_TEXT_BYTES = 3L * 1024 * 1024
    const val MAX_BIN_BYTES = 5L * 1024 * 1024

    /**
     * Bounded body drain shared by [cappedText]/[cappedBytes]. Okio's
     * `request(n)` blocks until n bytes or EOF; a server trickling one byte
     * every 14 s therefore held the calling thread (and the task's
     * cancellation point) open essentially forever — [budgetMs] is now a hard
     * wall, checked between 64 KiB chunks, on top of the 15 s socket read
     * timeout. Returns the bytes obtained (size vs the caller's cap decides
     * truncation semantics); EOF or budget expiry stops the drain.
     */
    private const val DRAIN_STEP = 64L * 1024
    /** Overall budget for one page/blob body read. Generous for real pages
     *  (kilobytes) yet a hard wall against trickling servers. */
    const val DEFAULT_BODY_BUDGET_MS = 90_000L
    private fun drainCapped(source: okio.BufferedSource, maxBytes: Long, budgetMs: Long, propagateFailure: Boolean = false): ByteArray {
        val want = java.lang.Long.min(maxBytes + 1, Int.MAX_VALUE.toLong())
        val deadline = System.currentTimeMillis() + budgetMs
        var have = 0L
        while (have < want) {
            val target = minOf(have + DRAIN_STEP, want)
            val ok = try {
                source.request(target)
            } catch (e: kotlinx.coroutines.CancellationException) {
                throw e
            } catch (e: Exception) {
                if (propagateFailure) throw e
                false
            }
            have = source.buffer.size
            if (!ok || have >= want || System.currentTimeMillis() > deadline) break
        }
        return source.buffer.readByteArray()
    }

    /** Read at most [maxBytes] of the response body as UTF-8 text. */
    fun cappedText(res: Response, maxBytes: Long = MAX_TEXT_BYTES, budgetMs: Long = DEFAULT_BODY_BUDGET_MS): String? =
        readCappedText(res, maxBytes, budgetMs, propagateFailure = false)

    private fun readCappedText(res: Response, maxBytes: Long, budgetMs: Long = DEFAULT_BODY_BUDGET_MS, propagateFailure: Boolean): String? {
        val body = res.body ?: return null
        val bytes = drainCapped(body.source(), maxBytes, budgetMs, propagateFailure)
        val truncated = bytes.size > maxBytes
        val text = String(if (truncated) bytes.copyOf(maxBytes.toInt()) else bytes, Charsets.UTF_8)
        if (truncated) {
            com.anonrode.downloader.util.DebugLog.net(
                "body from ${res.request.url.host} truncated at $maxBytes bytes (not a page — likely a misdirected file fetch)"
            )
        }
        return text
    }

    /** Read at most [maxBytes] of the response body as bytes.
     *  An oversize body is REJECTED (null), never truncated-and-returned: the
     *  callers are byte consumers (ffmpeg inputs, wasm blobs) and a clipped
     *  file is corrupt garbage that still "succeeds" — strictly worse than a
     *  clean null that routes to the normal failure path. When the server
     *  announces the length we refuse before reading a single byte (data cap). */
    fun cappedBytes(res: Response, maxBytes: Long = MAX_BIN_BYTES, budgetMs: Long = DEFAULT_BODY_BUDGET_MS): ByteArray? {
        val body = res.body ?: return null
        val announced = body.contentLength()
        if (announced > maxBytes) {
            com.anonrode.downloader.util.DebugLog.net(
                "binary body from ${res.request.url.host} is $announced bytes > cap $maxBytes — refused unread"
            )
            return null
        }
        val bytes = drainCapped(body.source(), maxBytes, budgetMs)
        if (bytes.size > maxBytes) {
            com.anonrode.downloader.util.DebugLog.net(
                "binary body from ${res.request.url.host} exceeds $maxBytes bytes — refused (not truncated)"
            )
            return null
        }
        return bytes
    }

    /** Request-local evidence; never infer resolver outcomes from [lastFailure]. */
    fun interface FailureListener {
        fun onFailure(url: String, error: Throwable)
    }

    /** Legacy nullable API retained; the overload adds opt-in local failure evidence. */
    fun getText(url: String, referer: String? = null, headers: Map<String, String> = emptyMap(), acceptStatus: Set<Int> = emptySet(), tag: String? = null, permissive: Boolean = false, maxBytes: Long = MAX_TEXT_BYTES): String? =
        getText(url, referer, headers, acceptStatus, tag, permissive, maxBytes, null)

    /**
     * Listener runs at most once on the caller's thread; listener exceptions propagate.
     * Opting in also reports body-read failures instead of returning partial text.
     */
    fun getText(url: String, referer: String? = null, headers: Map<String, String> = emptyMap(), acceptStatus: Set<Int> = emptySet(), tag: String? = null, permissive: Boolean = false, maxBytes: Long = MAX_TEXT_BYTES, onFailure: FailureListener?): String? =
        getTextWithClient(if (permissive) permissiveClient else shared, url, referer, headers, acceptStatus, tag, maxBytes, onFailure)

    /**
     * getText with a HARD per-call budget (connect + read). The default
     * client's 30s read timeout lets a wedged HTTP/2 edge hold the calling
     * thread for the full half-minute while delivering nothing — asianc's
     * api/a=search stalled exactly this way twice on 2026-10-20 ("Required
     * SETTINGS preface not received after 30978ms" / "Read timed out after
     * 30529ms"), and the day's FIRST search call shadows the cold-start
     * UI. Search/category callers pass ~10s and may retry once on a fresh
     * connection: a wedged pooled edge is bypassed, a slow origin is
     * answered within budget, and the failure journaling/probe semantics
     * are identical to [getTextWithClient].
     */
    fun getTextWithTimeout(url: String, timeoutMs: Long, referer: String? = null, headers: Map<String, String> = emptyMap(), acceptStatus: Set<Int> = emptySet(), tag: String? = null, maxBytes: Long = MAX_TEXT_BYTES): String? {
        val bounded = shared.newBuilder()
            .connectTimeout(timeoutMs.coerceIn(1_000L, 30_000L), java.util.concurrent.TimeUnit.MILLISECONDS)
            .readTimeout(timeoutMs.coerceIn(1_000L, 30_000L), java.util.concurrent.TimeUnit.MILLISECONDS)
            .build()
        return getTextWithClient(bounded, url, referer, headers, acceptStatus, tag, maxBytes, null)
    }

    // Injected client keeps regression tests socket-free without mutating shared state.
    internal fun getTextWithClient(client: OkHttpClient, url: String, referer: String? = null, headers: Map<String, String> = emptyMap(), acceptStatus: Set<Int> = emptySet(), tag: String? = null, maxBytes: Long = MAX_TEXT_BYTES, onFailure: FailureListener? = null): String? {
        return try {
            executeGet(url, referer, headers, tag, false, client) { res ->
                res.use { r ->
                    recordCooldown(r, tag)
                    if (r.isSuccessful || r.code in acceptStatus) {
                        // The host answered: clear any stale "dead" mark. The
                        // previous behavior treated a 2xx on a previously-failed
                        // host as a normal success (recorded via recordOk
                        // elsewhere) but DID NOT short-circuit the 60s backoff
                        // — so vdl.np-downloader.com, which the engine had
                        // tagged dead for 60s after a single DNS hiccup, kept
                        // getting skipped even after the very next GET to it
                        // returned 200 OK (live-verified: 50+ health-gate ERR
                        // events in app-2026-08-29 / 09-01, each followed by
                        // a 200 response on the immediate next request). This
                        // clearIfAlive call is the single line that fixes it.
                        com.anonrode.downloader.pipeline.HostHealth.clearIfAlive(url)
                        readCappedText(r, maxBytes, propagateFailure = onFailure != null)
                    } else {
                        if (r.code == 429 || r.code == 503) {
                            throw OriginCooldownException(r.request.url.toString())
                        }
                        val cfChallenge = isCloudflareChallenge(r)
                        throw HttpStatusCodeException(r.code, r.request.url.toString(), isChallenge = cfChallenge)
                    }
                }
            }
        } catch (e: kotlinx.coroutines.CancellationException) {
            throw e
        } catch (e: HttpStatusCodeException) {
            // The edge NAMED its rejection: keep the exact historical lastFailure
            // shape AND prove the host hostile for a session window. Share-43 /
            // investigation 11 R1: 2anime.xyz 436s were re-fetched five times
            // inside one resolve because the status died in a bare IOException
            // string nobody classified. 403 + 436 are the observed edge-rejection
            // class (Cloudflare bot walls); 404 stays a dead-link signal, 429/503
            // ride OriginCooldownException, 451 has its own edge-route failover.
            lastFailure = e.message
            Log.w("HttpClient", e.message ?: "HTTP ${e.code}")
            if ((e.code == 403 || e.code == 436) && !e.isChallenge) {
                com.anonrode.downloader.pipeline.HostHealth.recordFail(
                    url,
                    reason = "HTTP ${e.code} ${HttpClient.parsedHost(url) ?: ""}".trim()
                )
            }
            onFailure?.onFailure(url, e)
            null
        } catch (e: Exception) {
            val message = if (e is OriginCooldownException) {
                "OriginCooldownException: HTTP 429/503 cooldown active for ${url.take(120)}"
            } else {
                "${e.javaClass.simpleName}: ${e.message} for ${url.take(120)}"
            }
            lastFailure = message
            Log.w("HttpClient", message)
            onFailure?.onFailure(url, e)
            null
        }
    }

    /**
     * POST with a form-urlencoded body, mirroring [getText]: same 3MB body
     * cap, same lastFailure journaling, same tag tracking (search-tagged
     * calls stay cancellable as a group). Used by the rules pipeline for
     * sites whose search is an admin-ajax style POST.
     */
    fun postForm(url: String, form: Map<String, String>, referer: String? = null, headers: Map<String, String> = emptyMap(), tag: String? = null, maxBytes: Long = MAX_TEXT_BYTES): String? =
        postFormWithClient(shared, url, form, referer, headers, tag, maxBytes)

    fun postForm(url: String, form: Map<String, String>, referer: String? = null, headers: Map<String, String> = emptyMap(), tag: String? = null, maxBytes: Long = MAX_TEXT_BYTES, onFailure: FailureListener?): String? =
        postFormWithClient(shared, url, form, referer, headers, tag, maxBytes, onFailure)

    internal fun postFormWithClient(client: OkHttpClient, url: String, form: Map<String, String>, referer: String? = null, headers: Map<String, String> = emptyMap(), tag: String? = null, maxBytes: Long = MAX_TEXT_BYTES, onFailure: FailureListener? = null): String? {
        val cls = requestClass(tag)
        val admitted = runCatching { OriginLoadScheduler.acquire(url, cls) }.getOrDefault(false)
        try {
            return postFormInner(client, url, form, referer, headers, tag, maxBytes, onFailure)
        } finally {
            if (admitted) OriginLoadScheduler.release(url, cls)
        }
    }

    private fun postFormInner(client: OkHttpClient, url: String, form: Map<String, String>, referer: String? = null, headers: Map<String, String> = emptyMap(), tag: String? = null, maxBytes: Long = MAX_TEXT_BYTES, onFailure: FailureListener? = null): String? {
        return try {
            admitRequest(url, tag)
            refuseUnsafeTarget(url) // same floor as get() — INSIDE the try so an
            // unsafe target journal+returns null exactly like getText does; one
            // guard throwing for one verb and returning null for the other is
            // the kind of split-brain the resolvers were hardened against.
            val body = okhttp3.FormBody.Builder().apply {
                form.forEach { (k, v) -> add(k, v) }
            }.build()
            val reqBuilder = Request.Builder()
                .url(safeUrl(url))
                .post(body)
                .header("User-Agent", DEFAULT_UA)
                .header("Accept", "*/*")
                .header("Accept-Language", "en-US,en;q=0.9")
                .header("Sec-Fetch-Dest", "empty")
                .header("Sec-Fetch-Mode", "cors")
                .header("Sec-Fetch-Site", "same-origin")
            if (!referer.isNullOrBlank()) {
                reqBuilder.header("Referer", referer)
            }
            headers.forEach { (k, v) -> reqBuilder.header(k, v) }

            var call = client.newCall(reqBuilder.build())
            inFlightCalls.add(call)
            if (tag != null) {
                taggedCalls.computeIfAbsent(tag) { java.util.concurrent.CopyOnWriteArrayList() }.add(call)
            }
            val started = System.currentTimeMillis()
            var attempt = 0
            try {
                var response = try {
                    call.execute()
                } catch (e: java.io.IOException) {
                    if (call.isCanceled()) {
                        throw kotlinx.coroutines.CancellationException("HTTP call canceled").apply { initCause(e) }
                    }
                    throw e
                }

                if (android.os.Looper.myLooper() != android.os.Looper.getMainLooper() &&
                    CloudflareSolver.canAttemptSolve(tag) &&
                    isCloudflareChallenge(response) &&
                    attempt == 0) {
                    val priorReq = response.request
                    val priorProtocol = response.protocol
                    val priorCode = response.code
                    val priorMessage = response.message
                    val priorHeaders = response.headers
                    val postUrl = priorReq.url.toString()
                    val solveTarget = CloudflareSolver.resolveChallengeTargetUrl(postUrl, referer)

                    response.close()
                    inFlightCalls.remove(call)
                    if (tag != null) taggedCalls[tag]?.remove(call)

                    val solved = CloudflareSolver.solveSync(solveTarget, referer, tag)
                    if (solved) {
                        com.anonrode.downloader.pipeline.HostHealth.clearIfAlive(postUrl)
                        reqBuilder.header("User-Agent", DEFAULT_UA)
                        attempt++
                        call = client.newCall(reqBuilder.build())
                        inFlightCalls.add(call)
                        if (tag != null) taggedCalls.computeIfAbsent(tag) { java.util.concurrent.CopyOnWriteArrayList() }.add(call)
                        response = try {
                            call.execute()
                        } catch (e: java.io.IOException) {
                            if (call.isCanceled()) {
                                throw kotlinx.coroutines.CancellationException("HTTP call canceled").apply { initCause(e) }
                            }
                            throw e
                        }
                    } else {
                        response = Response.Builder()
                            .request(priorReq)
                            .protocol(priorProtocol)
                            .code(priorCode)
                            .message(priorMessage)
                            .headers(priorHeaders)
                            .body(okhttp3.ResponseBody.create(null, ByteArray(0)))
                            .build()
                    }
                }

                response.use { res ->
                    com.anonrode.downloader.util.DebugLog.net(
                        "POST ${safeUrl(url)} -> ${res.code} in ${System.currentTimeMillis() - started}ms"
                    )
                    recordCooldown(res, tag)
                    if (res.isSuccessful) {
                        readCappedText(res, maxBytes, propagateFailure = onFailure != null)
                    } else {
                        if (res.code == 429 || res.code == 503) {
                            throw OriginCooldownException(res.request.url.toString())
                        }
                        throw java.io.IOException("HTTP ${res.code} for ${res.request.url.toString().take(120)}")
                    }
                }
            } finally {
                inFlightCalls.remove(call)
                if (tag != null) {
                    taggedCalls[tag]?.remove(call)
                }
            }
        } catch (e: kotlinx.coroutines.CancellationException) {
            throw e
        } catch (e: Exception) {
            val message = "${e.javaClass.simpleName}: ${e.message} for ${url.take(120)}"
            lastFailure = message
            Log.w("HttpClient", message)
            onFailure?.onFailure(url, e)
            null
        }
    }

    fun postJson(url: String, json: String, referer: String? = null, headers: Map<String, String> = emptyMap(), tag: String? = null, maxBytes: Long = MAX_TEXT_BYTES): String? =
        postJsonWithClient(shared, url, json, referer, headers, tag, maxBytes)

    internal fun postJsonWithClient(client: OkHttpClient, url: String, json: String, referer: String? = null, headers: Map<String, String> = emptyMap(), tag: String? = null, maxBytes: Long = MAX_TEXT_BYTES, onFailure: FailureListener? = null): String? {
        val cls = requestClass(tag)
        val admitted = runCatching { OriginLoadScheduler.acquire(url, cls) }.getOrDefault(false)
        try {
            return postJsonInner(client, url, json, referer, headers, tag, maxBytes, onFailure)
        } finally {
            if (admitted) OriginLoadScheduler.release(url, cls)
        }
    }

    private fun postJsonInner(client: OkHttpClient, url: String, json: String, referer: String? = null, headers: Map<String, String> = emptyMap(), tag: String? = null, maxBytes: Long = MAX_TEXT_BYTES, onFailure: FailureListener? = null): String? {
        return try {
            admitRequest(url, tag)
            refuseUnsafeTarget(url)
            val mediaType = parseMediaType("application/json; charset=utf-8")
            val body = okhttp3.RequestBody.create(mediaType, json)
            val reqBuilder = Request.Builder()
                .url(safeUrl(url))
                .post(body)
                .header("User-Agent", DEFAULT_UA)
                .header("Accept", "application/json, text/plain, */*")
                .header("Accept-Language", "en-US,en;q=0.9")
            if (!referer.isNullOrBlank()) {
                reqBuilder.header("Referer", referer)
            }
            headers.forEach { (k, v) -> reqBuilder.header(k, v) }

            val call = client.newCall(reqBuilder.build())
            inFlightCalls.add(call)
            if (tag != null) {
                taggedCalls.computeIfAbsent(tag) { java.util.concurrent.CopyOnWriteArrayList() }.add(call)
            }
            val started = System.currentTimeMillis()
            try {
                val response = try {
                    call.execute()
                } catch (e: java.io.IOException) {
                    if (call.isCanceled()) {
                        throw kotlinx.coroutines.CancellationException("HTTP call canceled").apply { initCause(e) }
                    }
                    throw e
                }
                response.use { res ->
                    com.anonrode.downloader.util.DebugLog.net(
                        "POST_JSON ${safeUrl(url)} -> ${res.code} in ${System.currentTimeMillis() - started}ms"
                    )
                    recordCooldown(res, tag)
                    if (res.isSuccessful) {
                        readCappedText(res, maxBytes, propagateFailure = onFailure != null)
                    } else {
                        if (res.code == 429 || res.code == 503) {
                            throw OriginCooldownException(res.request.url.toString())
                        }
                        throw java.io.IOException("HTTP ${res.code} for ${res.request.url.toString().take(120)}")
                    }
                }
            } finally {
                inFlightCalls.remove(call)
                if (tag != null) taggedCalls[tag]?.remove(call)
            }
        } catch (e: kotlinx.coroutines.CancellationException) {
            throw e
        } catch (e: Exception) {
            val message = "postJson FAILED ${e.javaClass.simpleName}: ${e.message}"
            lastFailure = message
            Log.w("HttpClient", message)
            onFailure?.onFailure(url, e)
            null
        }
    }

    internal fun executeRawWithClient(
        client: OkHttpClient,
        url: String,
        method: String = "GET",
        bodyPayload: okhttp3.RequestBody? = null,
        referer: String? = null,
        headers: Map<String, String> = emptyMap(),
        maxBytes: Long = MAX_TEXT_BYTES,
        timeoutMs: Long = 0L,
        tag: String? = null
    ): HttpRawResult? {
        val cls = requestClass(tag)
        val admitted = runCatching { OriginLoadScheduler.acquire(url, cls) }.getOrDefault(false)
        try {
            return executeRawInner(client, url, method, bodyPayload, referer, headers, maxBytes, timeoutMs, tag)
        } finally {
            if (admitted) OriginLoadScheduler.release(url, cls)
        }
    }

    private fun executeRawInner(
        client: OkHttpClient,
        url: String,
        method: String = "GET",
        bodyPayload: okhttp3.RequestBody? = null,
        referer: String? = null,
        headers: Map<String, String> = emptyMap(),
        maxBytes: Long = MAX_TEXT_BYTES,
        timeoutMs: Long = 0L,
        tag: String? = null
    ): HttpRawResult? {
        return try {
            admitRequest(url, tag)
            refuseUnsafeTarget(url)
            val reqBuilder = Request.Builder()
                .url(safeUrl(url))
                .header("User-Agent", DEFAULT_UA)
                .header("Accept", "*/*")
                .header("Accept-Language", "en-US,en;q=0.9")
            if (!referer.isNullOrBlank()) reqBuilder.header("Referer", referer)
            headers.forEach { (k, v) -> reqBuilder.header(k, v) }

            when (method.uppercase()) {
                "POST" -> reqBuilder.post(bodyPayload ?: okhttp3.RequestBody.create(null, ByteArray(0)))
                "HEAD" -> reqBuilder.head()
                else -> reqBuilder.get()
            }

            val effectiveClient = if (timeoutMs > 0L) {
                client.newBuilder()
                    .connectTimeout(timeoutMs.coerceIn(1_000L, 30_000L), java.util.concurrent.TimeUnit.MILLISECONDS)
                    .readTimeout(timeoutMs.coerceIn(1_000L, 30_000L), java.util.concurrent.TimeUnit.MILLISECONDS)
                    .build()
            } else client

            fun register(c: okhttp3.Call) {
                inFlightCalls.add(c)
                if (tag != null) {
                    taggedCalls.computeIfAbsent(tag) { java.util.concurrent.CopyOnWriteArrayList() }.add(c)
                }
            }
            fun unregister(c: okhttp3.Call) {
                inFlightCalls.remove(c)
                if (tag != null) taggedCalls[tag]?.remove(c)
            }
            var call = effectiveClient.newCall(reqBuilder.build())
            register(call)
            var attempt = 0
            val started = System.currentTimeMillis()
            try {
                var response = try {
                    call.execute()
                } catch (e: java.io.IOException) {
                    if (call.isCanceled()) {
                        throw kotlinx.coroutines.CancellationException("HTTP call canceled").apply { initCause(e) }
                    }
                    throw e
                }
                if (response.code == 451 && attempt == 0) {
                    noteHttp451(url, response)
                    response.close()
                    try { effectiveClient.connectionPool.evictAll() } catch (_: Exception) {}
                    unregister(call)
                    attempt++
                    call = effectiveClient.newCall(reqBuilder.build())
                    register(call)
                    response = try {
                        call.execute()
                    } catch (e: java.io.IOException) {
                        if (call.isCanceled()) {
                            throw kotlinx.coroutines.CancellationException("HTTP call canceled").apply { initCause(e) }
                        }
                        throw e
                    }
                }
                response.use { res ->
                    com.anonrode.downloader.util.DebugLog.net(
                        "RAW $method ${safeUrl(url)} -> ${res.code} in ${System.currentTimeMillis() - started}ms"
                    )
                    recordCooldown(res, tag)
                    val bodyText = if (method.uppercase() != "HEAD" && res.body != null) {
                        readCappedText(res, maxBytes, propagateFailure = false)
                    } else null
                    HttpRawResult(
                        code = res.code,
                        body = bodyText,
                        headers = res.headers,
                        effectiveUrl = res.request.url.toString()
                    )
                }
            } finally {
                unregister(call)
            }
        } catch (e: kotlinx.coroutines.CancellationException) {
            throw e
        } catch (e: Exception) {
            val message = "executeRaw FAILED ${e.javaClass.simpleName}: ${e.message}"
            lastFailure = message
            Log.w("HttpClient", message)
            null
        }
    }

    /**
     * Reachability probe: request headers only (no body read) with a hard call
     * timeout, and report whether the server answered. Used by the HLS
     * pre-flight so a dead segment CDN fails a task in seconds instead of
     * pinning it in DOWNLOADING at 0 bytes for minutes.
     */
    fun probe(url: String, referer: String? = null, timeoutMs: Long = 10_000L, tag: String? = null): Boolean {
        if (!isSafeTarget(url)) {
            com.anonrode.downloader.util.DebugLog.net("PROBE refused by isSafeTarget: ${url.take(140)}")
            return false
        }
        // Never re-request an origin inside its recorded 429/503 cooldown —
        // the probe would burn its full timeout re-triggering the rate limit
        // (see isOriginCoolingDown doc). "Not reachable" is the honest answer
        // for a host that has asked us to back off.
        if (isOriginCoolingDown(url, requestScope(tag))) {
            com.anonrode.downloader.util.DebugLog.net("PROBE ${url.take(140)} skipped — origin in Retry-After cooldown")
            return false
        }
        val permitClass = requestClass(tag)
        val admitted = OriginLoadScheduler.acquire(url, permitClass, maxWaitMs = 2_000L)
        // Request construction (Builder.url, newCall) sits INSIDE the try on
        // purpose: okhttp3 throws IllegalArgumentException for a malformed
        // URL, and probe's contract is "answer true/false, never throw" —
        // callers run it inside coroutine children (SearchStrategyRunner's
        // concurrent suffix probes) where an escaping exception would fail
        // the whole scope, not just the one candidate.
        try {
            val reqBuilder = Request.Builder()
                .url(safeUrl(url))
                .header("User-Agent", DEFAULT_UA)
                .header("Accept", "*/*")
                .header("Range", "bytes=0-1024")
            if (!referer.isNullOrBlank()) reqBuilder.header("Referer", referer)
            var attempt = 0
            while (true) {
                val call = shared.newCall(reqBuilder.build())
                call.timeout().timeout(timeoutMs, java.util.concurrent.TimeUnit.MILLISECONDS)
                inFlightCalls.add(call)
                if (tag != null) {
                    taggedCalls.computeIfAbsent(tag) { java.util.concurrent.CopyOnWriteArrayList() }.add(call)
                }
                var retry = false
                try {
                    val res = try {
                        call.execute()
                    } catch (e: Exception) {
                        if (call.isCanceled()) {
                            throw kotlinx.coroutines.CancellationException("HTTP call canceled").apply { initCause(e) }
                        }
                        throw e
                    }
                    if (res.code == 451 && attempt == 0) {
                        // One same-request retry: a legal-block page served by
                        // one anycast edge must not mask the healthy sibling
                        // address (the NEPU 451 pattern).
                        noteHttp451(url, res)
                        try { res.body?.close() } catch (_: Exception) {}
                        try { shared.connectionPool.evictAll() } catch (_: Exception) {}
                        attempt++
                        retry = true
                    } else {
                        if (res.code == 429 || res.code == 503) recordCooldown(res, tag)
                        // 2xx proves the host serves; 416 (range not satisfiable
                        // for a bounded probe) still proves it is alive.
                        val ok = res.code in 200..299 || res.code == 416
                        // Headers-only check: close the body without reading it,
                        // so a server that ignores Range cannot stream past us.
                        try { res.body?.close() } catch (_: Exception) {}
                        com.anonrode.downloader.util.DebugLog.net("PROBE ${safeUrl(url)} -> ${res.code} (timeout=${timeoutMs}ms)")
                        return ok
                    }
                } finally {
                    inFlightCalls.remove(call)
                    if (tag != null) {
                        taggedCalls[tag]?.remove(call)
                    }
                }
                if (!retry) return false // defensive; the branch above returns
            }
        } catch (cancelled: kotlinx.coroutines.CancellationException) {
            throw cancelled
        } catch (e: Exception) {
            com.anonrode.downloader.util.DebugLog.net("PROBE ${url.take(140)} FAILED ${e.javaClass.simpleName}: ${e.message}")
            return false
        } finally {
            if (admitted) OriginLoadScheduler.release(url, permitClass)
        }
    }

    // ------------------------------------------------------------ terminal gate

    /**
     * ONE canonical "is this URL actually serving the file" verdict, replacing
     * the hand-copied checks that used to live inside individual resolvers
     * (they disagreed with each other — the class of bug behind the vikingfile
     * R2 misdirect rejection, 84e1d90). Semantics, each load-bearing and
     * live-verified:
     *  - no-redirect client: a 3xx is a HOP, never an acceptance. The shared
     *    client auto-follows, which HIDES Locations inside OkHttp — that is why
     *    this must run on a no-follow client (see [TerminalProbe.location]).
     *  - `Range: bytes=0-1024`: at most 1 KiB crosses the wire (metered-
     *    data discipline); servers honoring it answer 206 + Content-Range.
     *  - 200 with Content-Length = whole-file size: also accepted (servers
     *    ignoring Range). No size proof (chunked/absent CL) = reject.
     *  - text/html / application/xhtml = interstitial/ad page, reject.
     *  - hard per-call timeout + [inFlightCalls] registration: pause/cancel
     *    kills the probe (the old private copies were raw execute() —
     *    uncancellable stragglers).
     * Returns null ONLY on network failure; otherwise a [TerminalProbe] whose
     * `totalBytes != null` is the sole acceptance signal.
     */
    fun probeTerminal(
        url: String,
        referer: String? = null,
        timeoutMs: Long = 8_000L,
        permissive: Boolean = false,
        tag: String? = null
    ): TerminalProbe? {
        if (!isSafeTarget(url)) {
            com.anonrode.downloader.util.DebugLog.net("TERMINAL refused by isSafeTarget: ${url.take(140)}")
            return null
        }
        // Origin in its recorded 429/503 cooldown: null (network failure class)
        // without touching the wire. Resolvers read null as "no proof, defer"
        // and the download path revalidates after the window — a live host that
        // asked us to back off is never re-hit inside the window.
        if (isOriginCoolingDown(url, requestScope(tag))) {
            com.anonrode.downloader.util.DebugLog.net("TERMINAL ${url.take(140)} skipped — origin in Retry-After cooldown")
            return null
        }
        // Metered admission (download class): fan-out probes must not crowd
        // out a waiting search/verify on the same origin. Probe is 1 KiB and
        // bounded by its own timeout, so the scheduler wait is capped well
        // below it (fail-open on timeout).
        val permitClass = requestClass(tag)
        val admitted = OriginLoadScheduler.acquire(url, permitClass, maxWaitMs = 2_000L)
        // Request construction inside the try, exactly as in [probe]: "returns
        // null ONLY on network failure" is the documented contract, and an
        // IllegalArgumentException from a malformed URL must honor it.
        try {
            val reqBuilder = Request.Builder()
                .url(safeUrl(url))
                .header("User-Agent", DEFAULT_UA)
                .header("Range", "bytes=0-1024")
            if (!referer.isNullOrBlank()) reqBuilder.header("Referer", referer)
            val client = if (permissive) terminalProbeClientPermissive else terminalProbeClient
            fun register(c: okhttp3.Call) {
                c.timeout().timeout(timeoutMs, TimeUnit.MILLISECONDS)
                inFlightCalls.add(c)
                if (tag != null) {
                    taggedCalls.computeIfAbsent(tag) { java.util.concurrent.CopyOnWriteArrayList() }.add(c)
                }
            }
            fun unregister(c: okhttp3.Call) {
                inFlightCalls.remove(c)
                if (tag != null) taggedCalls[tag]?.remove(c)
            }
            var call = client.newCall(reqBuilder.build())
            register(call)
            var attempt = 0
            try {
                while (true) {
                    val res = call.execute()
                    if (res.code == 451 && attempt == 0) {
