```kotlin
                        noteHttp451(url, res)
                        res.close()
                        try { client.connectionPool.evictAll() } catch (_: Exception) {}
                        unregister(call)
                        attempt++
                        call = client.newCall(reqBuilder.build())
                        register(call)
                        continue
                    }
                    res.use { r ->
                        if (r.code == 429 || r.code == 503) recordCooldown(r, tag)
                        val ct = r.header("Content-Type")?.lowercase() ?: ""
                        val total = acceptsTerminalResponse(
                            r.code, r.header("Content-Length"), r.header("Content-Range"), r.header("Content-Type"), url
                        )
                        val tp = TerminalProbe(r.code, r.header("Location"), ct, total)
                        com.anonrode.downloader.util.DebugLog.net(
                            "TERMINAL ${safeUrl(url)} -> ${r.code}" +
                                (if (total != null) " size=$total" else " (not a terminal)")
                        )
                        return tp
                    }
                }
            } finally {
                unregister(call)
            }
        } catch (e: Exception) {
            if (!permissive && isTlsChainFailure(e)) {
                com.anonrode.downloader.util.DebugLog.net(
                    "TERMINAL ${url.take(140)} TLS failure (${e.javaClass.simpleName}: ${e.message}), retrying permissive"
                )
                return probeTerminal(url, referer, timeoutMs, permissive = true, tag = tag)
            }
            com.anonrode.downloader.util.DebugLog.net(
                "TERMINAL ${url.take(140)} FAILED ${e.javaClass.simpleName}: ${e.message}"
            )
            return null
        } finally {
            if (admitted) OriginLoadScheduler.release(url, permitClass)
        }
    }

    /** Cached no-follow variants (pool/dispatcher/cookies/safeDns are shared
     *  with [shared] via newBuilder — only the redirect policy differs). */
    val noRedirectClient: OkHttpClient by lazy {
        shared.newBuilder().followRedirects(false).followSslRedirects(false).build()
    }
    val noRedirectPermissiveClient: OkHttpClient by lazy {
        permissiveClient.newBuilder().followRedirects(false).followSslRedirects(false).build()
    }
    private val terminalProbeClient: OkHttpClient get() = noRedirectClient
    private val terminalProbeClientPermissive: OkHttpClient get() = noRedirectPermissiveClient

    // ------------- OTA diagnostics add-ons (ADDITIVE ONLY — existing bodies
    // above are untouched; these hooks only READ existing private state) -----

    /** What a hostname resolves to through the EXACT pipeline a fetch on
     *  [shared] uses (hybrid system-DNS race + DoH fallback + SSRF floor),
     *  plus whether the DoH cache holds an entry for it — i.e. whether DoH
     *  was ever the path that answered for this host in this process.
     *
     *  Purpose: OTA failure diagnostics (OtaFetchDiagnostics). The known
     *  blind spot is that DoH only engages when the DNS LOOKUP itself
     *  fails/times out — never when the carrier hands back a poisoned but
     *  resolvable answer that then dies at connect/TLS/HTTP. This snapshot
     *  captures whichever answer the pipeline produced so a failure event can
     *  carry the IPs the phone actually had. Bounded: the lookup inherits
     *  BoundedDnsScheduler's 3 s system cap + the 4 s bootstrap DoH caps.
     *  Call only on failure paths (it re-runs resolution). */
    data class OtaDnsSnapshot(val resolved: String?, val dohEntry: Boolean)

    fun otaDnsSnapshot(hostname: String): OtaDnsSnapshot {
        val dohUsed = try { dohCache.containsKey(hostname) } catch (_: Exception) { false }
        val ips = try {
            hybridDns.lookup(hostname)
                .mapNotNull { it.hostAddress }
                .distinct()
                .joinToString(",")
                .ifBlank { null }
        } catch (_: Exception) {
            null
        }
        return OtaDnsSnapshot(ips, dohUsed)
    }
}

data class HttpRawResult(
    val code: Int,
    val body: String?,
    val headers: okhttp3.Headers,
    val effectiveUrl: String
)

/**
 * Result of [HttpClient.probeTerminal]: the raw verdict on ONE no-redirect
 * request. `totalBytes` non-null means VALIDATED TERMINAL (200/206, real size,
 * non-HTML type). `location` is present on 3xx so callers can express the
 * HOP explicitly (auto-following would swallow it).
 */
data class TerminalProbe(
    val code: Int,
    val location: String?,
    val contentType: String,
    val totalBytes: Long?
)

/**
 * Pure decision half of [HttpClient.probeTerminal] — no network, JVM-testable.
 * Returns the file's total byte size when the response proves it serves a
 * real file, else null. Kept top-level per the isTlsChainFailure precedent so
 * tests exercise the real accept/reject matrix without an Android-bound client.
 */
internal fun acceptsTerminalResponse(
    code: Int,
    contentLength: String?,
    contentRange: String?,
    contentType: String?,
    url: String = ""
): Long? {
    if (code != 200 && code != 206) return null
    val ct = (contentType ?: "").lowercase()
    if (ct.startsWith("text/html") || ct.startsWith("application/xhtml")) return null
    if (code == 206) {
        // On 206 the Content-Length is just the 1 probed byte; the real total
        // lives in Content-Range: "bytes 0-0/159703784" (or ".../*" — unknown,
        // in which case the single-byte CL is the only size proof we get).
        val cr = contentRange?.trim()
        if (cr != null) {
            val slash = cr.lastIndexOf('/')
            if (slash >= 0) {
                val t = cr.substring(slash + 1).trim()
                if (t == "*") return (contentLength?.toLongOrNull() ?: 0L).takeIf { it > 0 }
                return t.toLongOrNull()?.takeIf { it > 0 }
            }
            return null // malformed Content-Range: no size proof
        }
        // 206 without Content-Range is spec-violating — refuse, do not guess.
        return null
    }
    // HLS / m3u8 streams: valid terminal response on 200 even with chunked or small size.
    val isHls = ct.contains("mpegurl") || ct.contains("vnd.apple.mpegurl") ||
        url.substringBefore('?').lowercase().endsWith(".m3u8")
    if (isHls) {
        return (contentLength?.toLongOrNull() ?: 1L).coerceAtLeast(1L)
    }
    // 200: Content-Length IS the size. Non-HLS direct media must have substantial size (>= 1KB) to be a valid file.
    return (contentLength?.toLongOrNull() ?: 0L).takeIf { it >= 1024L }
}

/**
 * SSRF address predicate used by [HttpClient.safeDns] and the URL pre-filter.
 * Blocks loopback, "this-network", link-local (incl. 169.254.169.254 cloud
 * metadata), site-local RFC1918, multicast, CGNAT 100.64/10, and the private
 * address smuggled inside 6to4 (2002::/16) / Teredo (2001::/32) IPv6 wrappers.
 * IPv4-mapped v6 (::ffff:x) is delegated to the JDK's own is* checks.
 * Top-level + pure per the isTlsChainFailure convention: full JVM matrix test.
 */
internal fun isBlockedAddress(addr: java.net.InetAddress): Boolean {
    if (addr.isLoopbackAddress || addr.isAnyLocalAddress || addr.isLinkLocalAddress ||
        addr.isSiteLocalAddress || addr.isMulticastAddress
    ) return true
    val b = addr.address ?: return true // fail closed on anything unreadable
    if (b.size == 4) {
        val o0 = b[0].toInt() and 0xFF
        if (o0 == 0) return true // 0.0.0.0/8 "this network"
        if (o0 == 100 && (b[1].toInt() and 0xC0) == 0x40) return true // 100.64.0.0/10 CGNAT
        if (o0 == 0xFF && (b[1].toInt() and 0xFF) == 0xFF && (b[2].toInt() and 0xFF) == 0xFF &&
            (b[3].toInt() and 0xFF) == 0xFF
        ) return true // limited broadcast (JDK's isMulticastAddress does NOT cover it)
        return false
    }
    if (b.size == 16) {
        val b0 = b[0].toInt() and 0xFF
        if ((b0 and 0xFE) == 0xFC) return true // RFC 4193 Unique Local Address fc00::/7 (private IPv6)
        // ::ffff:a.b.c.d (mapped) and the obsolete ::a.b.c.d (compat): unwrap to
        // the v4 rules OURSELVES — whether getByName hands us an Inet4Address
        // or an Inet6Address for those texts is a JDK text-format detail we
        // refuse to depend on. (NAT64 64:ff9b::/96 has non-zero leading bytes
        // and is deliberately left alone: it is how v6-only networks reach
        // public v4.)
        val leadingZeros = (0..9).all { b[it].toInt() == 0 }
        if (leadingZeros) {
            val w10 = b[10].toInt() and 0xFF
            val w11 = b[11].toInt() and 0xFF
            if ((w10 == 0xFF && w11 == 0xFF) || (w10 == 0 && w11 == 0)) {
                val v4 = embeddedV4OrNull(byteArrayOf(b[12], b[13], b[14], b[15])) ?: return true
                if (isBlockedAddress(v4)) return true
            }
        }
        // 6to4: 2002:<v4>:: — unwrap the embedded IPv4 and re-check.
        if (b[0].toInt() and 0xFF == 0x20 && b[1].toInt() and 0xFF == 0x02) {
            val v4 = embeddedV4OrNull(byteArrayOf(b[2], b[3], b[4], b[5])) ?: return true
            if (isBlockedAddress(v4)) return true
        }
        // Teredo: 2001:0000::<..><client-v4 bitwise-NOT> — unwrap and re-check.
        if (b[0].toInt() and 0xFF == 0x20 && b[1].toInt() and 0xFF == 0x01 &&
            b[2].toInt() and 0xFF == 0x00 && b[3].toInt() and 0xFF == 0x00
        ) {
            val raw = byteArrayOf(
                (b[12].toInt() and 0xFF).inv().toByte(), (b[13].toInt() and 0xFF).inv().toByte(),
                (b[14].toInt() and 0xFF).inv().toByte(), (b[15].toInt() and 0xFF).inv().toByte()
            )
            val v4 = embeddedV4OrNull(raw) ?: return true
            if (isBlockedAddress(v4)) return true
        }
    }
    return false
}

private fun embeddedV4OrNull(bytes: ByteArray): java.net.InetAddress? =
    try { java.net.Inet4Address.getByAddress(bytes) } catch (_: Exception) { null }

/**
 * True when [e]'s cause chain is a TLS handshake/chain failure (strict
 * client vs a server that omits its intermediate cert). Only this class
 * of error justifies the trust-all retry — timeouts, DNS and HTTP errors
 * are still real failures and must not be papered over by disabling
 * certificate validation. Top-level (not an [HttpClient] member) so JVM
 * tests can exercise it without initializing the Android-bound client.
 */
internal fun isTlsChainFailure(e: Throwable): Boolean {
    var t: Throwable? = e
    while (t != null) {
        if (t is javax.net.ssl.SSLException || t is java.security.cert.CertPathValidatorException) return true
        val msg = t.message?.lowercase() ?: ""
        if (msg.contains("trust anchor") || msg.contains("certpath") || msg.contains("certificate_unknown")) return true
        t = t.cause
    }
    return false
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Per-origin request scheduler (NEPU rule-13 invariant, 2026-10-20)
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

/**
 * Request class for the per-origin scheduler. Priority order is SEARCH >
 * VERIFY > DOWNLOAD (fan-out): a waiting search is served before any new
 * verify/download starts on that origin, and a waiting verify before any new
 * download. Existing in-flight requests are never preempted — the goal is to
 * stop a resolver fan-out from starving the user's search, not to abort work.
 */
internal enum class OriginRequestClass { SEARCH, VERIFY, DOWNLOAD }

/**
 * Small per-origin admission gate shared by every HttpClient request path.
 *
 * Caps (per origin): SEARCH 3, VERIFY 2, DOWNLOAD 2, total 4. The DOWNLOAD cap
 * is the evidence-backed number from the NEPU log review ("<=2 concurrent
 * fan-out requests per origin while a download resolves"); search keeps three
 * slots because the live 11:09 probe tolerated five concurrent search GETs but
 * five concurrent + typing + fan-out is what produced the 451/429 storm.
 *
 * Blocking, bounded wait (default 4 s). On timeout the caller proceeds WITHOUT
 * a permit (fail-open): metering must never become a new source of hangs.
 * The gate map is bounded and entries with no active/waiting users are
 * removed, so this cannot grow with the number of hosts seen.
 */
internal object OriginLoadScheduler {

    private const val MAX_SEARCH = 3
    private const val MAX_VERIFY = 2
    private const val MAX_DOWNLOAD = 2
    private const val MAX_TOTAL = 4
    private const val MAX_GATES = 64
    private const val MAX_WAIT_MS = 4_000L

    private class Gate {
        var activeSearch = 0
        var activeVerify = 0
        var activeDownload = 0
        var waitSearch = 0
        var waitVerify = 0
        var waitDownload = 0
        fun activeTotal() = activeSearch + activeVerify + activeDownload
        fun empty() = activeTotal() == 0 && waitSearch + waitVerify + waitDownload == 0
    }

    private val lock = java.util.concurrent.locks.ReentrantLock()
    private val changed = lock.newCondition()
    private val gates = HashMap<String, Gate>()

    private fun canStart(g: Gate, cls: OriginRequestClass): Boolean {
        if (g.activeTotal() >= MAX_TOTAL) return false
        return when (cls) {
            OriginRequestClass.SEARCH -> g.activeSearch < MAX_SEARCH
            OriginRequestClass.VERIFY -> g.activeVerify < MAX_VERIFY && g.waitSearch == 0
            OriginRequestClass.DOWNLOAD ->
                g.activeDownload < MAX_DOWNLOAD && g.waitSearch == 0 && g.waitVerify == 0
        }
    }

    private fun incActive(g: Gate, cls: OriginRequestClass) {
        when (cls) {
            OriginRequestClass.SEARCH -> g.activeSearch++
            OriginRequestClass.VERIFY -> g.activeVerify++
            OriginRequestClass.DOWNLOAD -> g.activeDownload++
        }
    }

    private fun decActive(g: Gate, cls: OriginRequestClass) {
        when (cls) {
            OriginRequestClass.SEARCH -> g.activeSearch = (g.activeSearch - 1).coerceAtLeast(0)
            OriginRequestClass.VERIFY -> g.activeVerify = (g.activeVerify - 1).coerceAtLeast(0)
            OriginRequestClass.DOWNLOAD -> g.activeDownload = (g.activeDownload - 1).coerceAtLeast(0)
        }
    }

    private fun incWaiting(g: Gate, cls: OriginRequestClass) {
        when (cls) {
            OriginRequestClass.SEARCH -> g.waitSearch++
            OriginRequestClass.VERIFY -> g.waitVerify++
            OriginRequestClass.DOWNLOAD -> g.waitDownload++
        }
    }

    private fun decWaiting(g: Gate, cls: OriginRequestClass) {
        when (cls) {
            OriginRequestClass.SEARCH -> g.waitSearch = (g.waitSearch - 1).coerceAtLeast(0)
            OriginRequestClass.VERIFY -> g.waitVerify = (g.waitVerify - 1).coerceAtLeast(0)
            OriginRequestClass.DOWNLOAD -> g.waitDownload = (g.waitDownload - 1).coerceAtLeast(0)
        }
    }

    /** @return true when a permit was taken; false = fail-open (no release). */
    fun acquire(url: String, cls: OriginRequestClass, maxWaitMs: Long = MAX_WAIT_MS): Boolean {
        val origin = try { RetryAfterCooldown.originOf(url) } catch (_: Exception) { null } ?: return false
        val deadline = System.currentTimeMillis() + maxWaitMs.coerceAtLeast(0L)
        lock.lock()
        try {
            var gate = gates[origin]
            if (gate == null) {
                if (gates.size >= MAX_GATES) {
                    gates.entries.removeIf { it.value.empty() }
                    if (gates.size >= MAX_GATES) return false
                }
                gate = Gate()
                gates[origin] = gate
            }
            while (true) {
                val g = gates[origin] ?: return false
                if (canStart(g, cls)) {
                    incActive(g, cls)
                    return true
                }
                incWaiting(g, cls)
                try {
                    val remaining = deadline - System.currentTimeMillis()
                    if (remaining <= 0L) return false
                    changed.await(remaining, java.util.concurrent.TimeUnit.MILLISECONDS)
                } catch (_: InterruptedException) {
                    Thread.currentThread().interrupt()
                    return false
                } finally {
                    decWaiting(g, cls)
                }
            }
        } finally {
            lock.unlock()
        }
    }

    fun release(url: String, cls: OriginRequestClass) {
        val origin = try { RetryAfterCooldown.originOf(url) } catch (_: Exception) { return } ?: return
        lock.lock()
        try {
            val g = gates[origin] ?: return
            decActive(g, cls)
            changed.signalAll()
            if (g.empty()) gates.remove(origin)
        } finally {
            lock.unlock()
        }
    }

    /** Tests only: drop all tracked state (thread-safe). */
    internal fun clearForTests() {
        lock.lock()
        try { gates.clear() } finally { lock.unlock() }
    }
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Boot warm-up (RC-2 cold start, 2026-10-21)
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

/**
 * Silent, idempotent, non-blocking boot warm-up for the origins the first
 * user interaction always touches (AsianC search + the four trending feeds).
 *
 * Contract:
 *  - once connectivity exists, [start] launches ONE warm per origin and
 *    returns immediately — app start and the UI thread never wait for it;
 *  - a successful warm is remembered for the process (idempotent: later
 *    [start] calls dial nothing); a FAILED one stays retryable, so the next
 *    connectivity change gives it another chance;
 *  - failures are silent by construction: [HttpClient.warmConnection] returns
 *    false, never throws;
 *  - every warm is a DOWNLOAD-class, cooldown-aware scheduler request, so it
 *    cannot consume the search budget ([HttpClient.WARMUP_TAG]).
 *
 * The transport is injectable ([warmAsync]'s [warmer]) so the idempotence /
 * silence / non-blocking contract is JVM-testable without sockets.
 */
internal object ConnectionWarmup {

    /** The hot origins: AsianC search/detail plus the trending feed fan-out. */
    val HOT_ORIGINS: List<String> = listOf(
        "https://asianc.id/",
        "https://nepu.gd/",
        "https://9jarocks.net/",
        "https://www.naijaprey.tv/",
        "https://thenkiri.com/",
        "https://www.naijavault.com/"
    )

    /** Per-origin budget. Generous for a cold mobile DNS+TLS+H2 negotiation,
     *  far below the 30s read timeout it replaces. */
    const val WARM_TIMEOUT_MS = 5_000L

    private val scope = CoroutineScope(Dispatchers.IO + SupervisorJob())
    private val warmed: MutableSet<String> = java.util.concurrent.ConcurrentHashMap.newKeySet<String>()
    private val inFlight: MutableSet<String> = java.util.concurrent.ConcurrentHashMap.newKeySet<String>()
    private val attempts = AtomicInteger()
    private val successes = AtomicInteger()
    private val failures = AtomicInteger()

    /**
     * Production entry point: fire-and-forget. Idempotence lives in
     * [warmOne] (warmed set + in-flight single-flight), so calling this on
     * every connectivity change costs nothing after the first success and
     * retries only the origins that failed while the network was flapping.
     */
    fun start() {
        warmAsync(HOT_ORIGINS)
    }

    internal data class WarmStats(
        val attempts: Int,
        val successes: Int,
        val failures: Int,
        val warmed: Int
    )

    /**
     * Warm [origins] concurrently. Returns the [Job] so tests can await
     * completion; production ignores it. Distinct origins only. Each origin
     * warms at most once (successes only — a failed origin may be retried).
     */
    internal fun warmAsync(
        origins: List<String>,
        timeoutMs: Long = WARM_TIMEOUT_MS,
        warmer: suspend (String) -> Boolean = { origin ->
            HttpClient.warmConnection(origin, timeoutMs = timeoutMs)
        }
    ): Job = scope.launch {
        coroutineScope {
            origins.distinct().forEach { origin ->
                launch { warmOne(origin, warmer) }
            }
        }
    }

    private suspend fun warmOne(origin: String, warmer: suspend (String) -> Boolean) {
        val url = normalizeOrigin(origin)
        if (url.isBlank() || warmed.contains(url)) return
        // Single-flight per origin: two start()/reconnect calls racing must
        // not double-dial the same host.
        if (!inFlight.add(url)) return
        attempts.incrementAndGet()
        try {
            val ok = try {
                warmer(url)
            } catch (cancelled: kotlinx.coroutines.CancellationException) {
                throw cancelled
            } catch (_: Exception) {
                false
            }
            if (ok) {
                warmed.add(url)
                successes.incrementAndGet()
            } else {
                failures.incrementAndGet()
            }
        } finally {
            inFlight.remove(url)
        }
    }

    private fun normalizeOrigin(origin: String): String {
        val trimmed = origin.trim()
        if (trimmed.isBlank()) return ""
        val withScheme = if (trimmed.startsWith("http://", true) || trimmed.startsWith("https://", true)) {
            trimmed
        } else {
            "https://$trimmed"
        }
        return if (withScheme.endsWith("/")) withScheme else "$withScheme/"
    }

    /** Tiny stats hook for tests. */
    internal fun statsForTest(): WarmStats =
        WarmStats(attempts.get(), successes.get(), failures.get(), warmed.size)

    internal fun resetForTest() {
        warmed.clear()
        inFlight.clear()
        attempts.set(0)
        successes.set(0)
        failures.set(0)
    }
}
```

```kotlin
package com.anonrode.downloader.data.net

/**
 * A non-2xx answer that IS a real HTTP status — the server's edge named its
 * rejection (Cloudflare-style 403/436 embed blocks, 451 legal blocks, plain
 * 404s) and the transport can carry the code end to end. Subclass of
 * [java.io.IOException] with the EXACT same message the untyped throw
 * produced ("HTTP {code} for {url}") so every existing [Throwable.message]
 * caller (lastFailure, park reasons, resolver error text) keeps its shape.
 *
 * Before this class existed, getText swallowed the code into a bare
 * IOException string and every consumer re-parsed prose (investigation 11,
 * share-43: 2anime.xyz's 436 was fetched FIVE times inside one resolve —
 * nothing ever learned the host rejects us until the task died "chain
 * EMPTY").
 */
internal class HttpStatusCodeException(
    val code: Int,
    url: String,
    val isChallenge: Boolean = false
) : java.io.IOException("HTTP $code for ${url.take(120)}")
```

```kotlin
        override fun onActivityStopped(activity: Activity) {
            if (startedCount > 0) startedCount--
            if (startedCount == 0) {

    private suspend fun maybeUpdateYoutubeDL() {
        try {
            val prefs = getSharedPreferences(PREFS_SERVERLESS, Context.MODE_PRIVATE)
            val last = prefs.getLong(KEY_LAST_YTDLP_UPDATE, 0L)
            val now = System.currentTimeMillis()
            if (now - last < UPDATE_INTERVAL_MS) return
            // YtDlpCore owns the channel choice (default MASTER/nightly —
            // YouTube's bot-check fixes land there first) and the one-shot
            // fallback onto the other channel.

            if (outcome.ok) {
                prefs.edit().putLong(KEY_LAST_YTDLP_UPDATE, now).apply()
                Log.i("AnonApp", "yt-dlp auto-update: ${outcome.message} (${outcome.channelUsed})")
            } else {
                Log.w("AnonApp", "yt-dlp auto-update failed: ${outcome.message}")
            }
        } catch (t: Throwable) {
            Log.w("AnonApp", "yt-dlp update failed, keeping bundled binary", t)
        }
    }

    /**
     * The ONLY production image client. PosterImages owns the hard limits:
     * six concurrent requests, three per host, short timeouts. Feed/resolver
     * traffic keeps its own dispatcher (HttpClient.shared), so a poster
     * stampede can never starve a download resolution.
     */
    internal fun buildImageHttpClient(): okhttp3.OkHttpClient =
        PosterImages.configure(
            HttpClient.shared.newBuilder()
                // Coil's networkCachePolicy(DISABLED) maps to OkHttp's
                // only-if-cached, which is a no-op without a Cache. This cache
                // makes the offline/cache-only underlay truly network-free on
                // a disk miss instead of waiting out the call timeout.
                .cache(okhttp3.Cache(File(noBackupFilesDir, "image_http_cache"), 64L * 1024 * 1024))
                .addInterceptor { chain ->
                    val request = chain.request().newBuilder()
                        .header("User-Agent", HttpClient.DEFAULT_UA)
                        .build()
                    chain.proceed(request)
                }
                .build()
        )

    /**
     * 250 MB poster cache in noBackupFilesDir (app-private, not OS-evictable,
     * and excluded from cloud backup so a 250 MB art cache never blows the
     * 25 MB backup quota). The old cacheDir location is migrated once when
     * possible so an upgrade keeps its offline art.
     */
    private fun imageCacheDir(): File {
        val target = File(noBackupFilesDir, "image_cache")
        if (!target.exists()) {
            val legacy = File(cacheDir, "image_cache")
            if (legacy.exists()) {
                try {
                    legacy.renameTo(target)
                } catch (_: Throwable) {
                }
            }
        }
        if (!target.exists()) target.mkdirs()
        return target
    }

    override fun newImageLoader(): ImageLoader {
        val client = buildImageHttpClient()
        return ImageLoader.Builder(this)
            .okHttpClient(client)
            .memoryCache {
                coil.memory.MemoryCache.Builder(this)
                    .maxSizePercent(0.25)
                    .build()
            }
            .diskCache {
                coil.disk.DiskCache.Builder()
                    .directory(imageCacheDir())
                    .maxSizeBytes(250L * 1024 * 1024)
                    .build()
            }
            // CDNs commonly send no-store/private on poster bytes. The disk
            // cache exists precisely to survive that, so ignore the headers.
            .respectCacheHeaders(false)
            .crossfade(120)
            .build()
    }

    companion object {
        lateinit var instance: AnonApp
            private set

        val repository: DownloadRepository by lazy { DownloadRepository() }

        val downloadEngine: DownloadEngine
            get() = instance.engine

        private val appScope = CoroutineScope(Dispatchers.IO + SupervisorJob())
        private val initMutex = Mutex()

        /** Written by AnonApp after each successful sync; UpdateManager reads
         *  it (with the rules cache mtime) as its payload-staleness signal —
         *  do not rename without updating update/UpdateManager.kt. */
        internal const val KEY_LAST_RULES_SYNC = "last_rules_sync"
        private const val KEY_LAST_YTDLP_UPDATE = "last_ytdlp_update"
        private const val UPDATE_INTERVAL_MS = 24L * 60 * 60 * 1000

        /** Prefs home of the sync/update bookkeeping (also read by
         *  UpdateManager as its payload-staleness signal — do not rename
         *  without updating update/UpdateManager.kt). */
        internal const val PREFS_SERVERLESS = "anon_serverless_prefs"

        /** Decision 5: resume-refresh fires when the last successful rules
         *  sync is older than this, even though the auto floor is 24h. */
        private const val RESUME_SYNC_INTERVAL_MS = 6L * 60 * 60 * 1000

        /** Cold-start guard: the initial auto-sync and the first foreground
         *  land nearly together — do not double-fire the sync path. */
        private const val RESUME_SYNC_DEBOUNCE_MS = 10L * 60 * 1000

        /** Last time a rules sync ATTEMPT started (any path), for the
         *  foreground debounce above. */
        @Volatile
        private var lastSyncAttemptMs = 0L

        /**
         * First foreground of a session (Decision 5 + engagement clock).
         * Stamps the last-open time / re-arms the inactivity alarm, and when
         * the last successful rules sync is >6h old triggers the existing
         * sync path with force=true. Cheap, guarded, never throws.
         */
        fun onAppForegrounded() {
            if (!::instance.isInitialized) return
            val app = instance
            try {
                com.anonrode.downloader.update.EngagementScheduler.noteAppOpen(app)
            } catch (_: Throwable) {
            }
            try {
                val now = System.currentTimeMillis()
                if (now - lastSyncAttemptMs < RESUME_SYNC_DEBOUNCE_MS) return
                val lastSync = app.getSharedPreferences(PREFS_SERVERLESS, Context.MODE_PRIVATE)
                    .getLong(KEY_LAST_RULES_SYNC, 0L)
                if (now - lastSync < RESUME_SYNC_INTERVAL_MS) return
                appScope.launch { app.maybeSyncRules(force = true) }
            } catch (_: Throwable) {
            }
        }

        @Volatile
        var ytdlpReady: Boolean = false
            private set

        internal suspend fun initYoutubeDlInternal(context: Context) {
            if (ytdlpReady) return
            initMutex.withLock {
                if (ytdlpReady) return@withLock
                try {
                    YoutubeDL.getInstance().init(context)
                    FFmpeg.getInstance().init(context)
                    ytdlpReady = true
                    Log.i("AnonApp", "youtubedl-android and ffmpeg initialized successfully")
                } catch (t: Throwable) {
                    Log.e("AnonApp", "youtubedl-android init failed", t)
                }
            }
        }

        suspend fun ensureReady(): Boolean {
            if (ytdlpReady) return true
            if (::instance.isInitialized) {
                initYoutubeDlInternal(instance)
            } else {
                initMutex.withLock { /* wait for any in-flight init */ }
            }
            return ytdlpReady
        }
    }
}

/**
 * Hard image-plane policy, extracted so JVM/Robolectric tests can pin it
 * without booting the Application. Six total in flight, three per host:
 * enough to fill a 3-column grid, low enough that poster traffic cannot
 * monopolize sockets, battery or a slow source host.
 */
object PosterImages {
    const val MAX_REQUESTS = 6
    const val MAX_REQUESTS_PER_HOST = 3
    const val CONNECT_TIMEOUT_SECONDS = 8L
    const val READ_TIMEOUT_SECONDS = 20L
    const val CALL_TIMEOUT_SECONDS = 25L

    fun newDispatcher(): okhttp3.Dispatcher = okhttp3.Dispatcher().apply {
        maxRequests = MAX_REQUESTS
        maxRequestsPerHost = MAX_REQUESTS_PER_HOST
    }

    fun configure(base: okhttp3.OkHttpClient): okhttp3.OkHttpClient =
        base.newBuilder()
            .dispatcher(newDispatcher())
            .connectionPool(okhttp3.ConnectionPool(8, 5, TimeUnit.MINUTES))
            .connectTimeout(CONNECT_TIMEOUT_SECONDS, TimeUnit.SECONDS)
            .readTimeout(READ_TIMEOUT_SECONDS, TimeUnit.SECONDS)
            .callTimeout(CALL_TIMEOUT_SECONDS, TimeUnit.SECONDS)
            .build()
}
```

```kotlin
        /** Notification deep-link extra (cross-doc audit BUG 6 / wiring F-11):
         *  tapping a download notification must land on the Downloads tab. */
        const val EXTRA_OPEN_TAB = "extra_open_tab"
    }

    private val viewModel: MainViewModel by viewModels()

    /** Warm-start tab requests. A StateFlow survives the tab's
     *  rememberSaveable: no Activity recreation, and MainScaffold applies the
     *  request directly before clearing it. */
    private val pendingTabRequest = MutableStateFlow<String?>(null)

    override fun onNewIntent(intent: Intent) {
        super.onNewIntent(intent)
        setIntent(intent)
        val tab = intent.getStringExtra(EXTRA_OPEN_TAB)
        if (!tab.isNullOrBlank()) {
            // Do NOT recreate(): instance state restores MainScaffold's
            // rememberSaveable tab ("search") and the old code overwrote the
            // pref back before the new tab ever appeared.
            pendingTabRequest.value = tab
            intent.removeExtra(EXTRA_OPEN_TAB)
            getSharedPreferences("downloader_settings", android.content.Context.MODE_PRIVATE)
                .edit().putString("pref_last_tab", tab).apply()
        }
    }

    override fun onCreate(savedInstanceState: Bundle?) {
        try {
            installSplashScreen()
        } catch (_: Throwable) {}

        super.onCreate(savedInstanceState)
        // Cold-start: fit the window edge-to-edge with the bar icon tint and
        // window background matched to the persisted theme so the first frame
        // already has the right system-bar contrast. Without this, light mode
        // launches with white-on-near-white status icons (invisible) until the
        // first composition. Theme switches later re-run enableEdgeToEdge
        // through syncSystemBars — that is the only call that repaints the bar
        // FILL (see its doc); here it just seeds the first frame.
        // Notification deep-link (cross-doc audit BUG 6/F-11): a tap that
        // starts the app cold must land on the requested tab too — persist it
        // before the initialTab read below picks it up.
        intent?.getStringExtra(EXTRA_OPEN_TAB)?.takeIf { it.isNotBlank() }?.let { tab ->
            getSharedPreferences("downloader_settings", android.content.Context.MODE_PRIVATE)
                .edit().putString("pref_last_tab", tab).apply()
            intent.removeExtra(EXTRA_OPEN_TAB)
        }

        val coldPrefs = getSharedPreferences("downloader_settings", android.content.Context.MODE_PRIVATE)
        val coldTheme = coldPrefs.getString("pref_theme_mode", "dark") ?: "dark"
        applyEdgeToEdge(coldTheme)

        // No share-intent handling here: MainActivity has no ACTION_SEND
        // filter (QuickShareActivity owns the share surface), so the old
        // defensive handleShareIntent call was unreachable and is removed.

        val prefs = getSharedPreferences("downloader_settings", android.content.Context.MODE_PRIVATE)

        // Read both persisted prefs outside the composable: the theme decides
        // the initial colour scheme, the tab decides which screen renders
        // first. Doing the read here (instead of inside Compose) keeps the
        // restore decision in one place and avoids the "first composition
        // flashes the wrong tab" bug.
        val initialThemeMode = prefs.getString("pref_theme_mode", "dark") ?: "dark"
        val initialTab = prefs.getString("pref_last_tab", MainTab.DEFAULT)?.let { stored ->
            if (stored == MainTab.SEARCH || stored == MainTab.DOWNLOADS || stored == MainTab.SETTINGS) stored
            else MainTab.DEFAULT
        } ?: MainTab.DEFAULT

        // Which splash cut plays: the FULL identity animation runs ONCE, on the
        // very first install (the cinematic first impression — user-approved
        // rev-6 study); every warm start gets the QUICK cut. Flag written now so
        // a mid-splash crash still doesn't replay the full show.
        val splashFull = !prefs.getBoolean("splash_full_shown", false)
        if (splashFull) prefs.edit().putBoolean("splash_full_shown", true).apply()
        val splashCutMs = if (splashFull) SplashMotion.FULL_MS else SplashMotion.QUICK_MS

        setContent {
            var themeMode by remember { mutableStateOf(initialThemeMode) }

            // Resolve the effective theme for the system bars and window
            // background. "system" follows the device night mode, mirroring
            // AnonDownloaderTheme's own resolution below, so Auto gets the
            // right bar contrast and background on light AND dark devices.
            val isDark = when (themeMode.lowercase()) {
                "light" -> false
                "system" -> isSystemInDarkTheme()
                // Legacy/defensive alias: "auto" resolves exactly like "system".
                "auto" -> isSystemInDarkTheme()
                else -> true
            }

            // Theme-flip sync: flips ONLY the bar icon appearance and swaps
            // the window background — never re-invoke enableEdgeToEdge, which
            // re-fits the window (setDecorFitsSystemWindows) and re-dispatches
            // window insets (the root cause of the half-screen flicker/jump).
            // SideEffect (not LaunchedEffect): it runs after this scope
            // recomposes successfully and BEFORE the frame is dispatched, so
            // the bar restyle and the Compose color swap land in the SAME frame.
            SideEffect { syncSystemBars(isDark) }

            AnonDownloaderTheme(themeMode = themeMode) {
                val socialTarget by viewModel.activeSocialTarget.collectAsState()

                // Request Notification Permission on Android 13+ (API 33+)
                val permissionLauncher = rememberLauncherForActivityResult(
                    contract = ActivityResultContracts.RequestPermission(),
                    onResult = { _ -> }
                )

                LaunchedEffect(Unit) {
                    if (Build.VERSION.SDK_INT >= Build.VERSION_CODES.TIRAMISU) {
                        val hasPermission = ContextCompat.checkSelfPermission(
                            this@MainActivity,
                            Manifest.permission.POST_NOTIFICATIONS
                        ) == PackageManager.PERMISSION_GRANTED

                        if (!hasPermission) {
                            permissionLauncher.launch(Manifest.permission.POST_NOTIFICATIONS)
                        }
                    }
                }

                // ---- Storage access ----
                // Downloads are written straight into Download/Anon, which on
                // Android 11+ (API 30+) requires MANAGE_EXTERNAL_STORAGE —
                // "All files access". That permission has NO runtime dialog:
                // it can only be granted via a Settings redirect. On Android
                // 9-10 (API 26-29) it is a normal WRITE_EXTERNAL_STORAGE prompt.
                // Neither was ever requested, so fresh installs failed with a
                // confusing IO error until the user manually granted access in
                // app info (tester report). Show a rationale dialog at launch
                // and route to the right grant screen.
                val context = LocalContext.current
                var showStorageRationale by remember { mutableStateOf(false) }
                val writeStorageLauncher = rememberLauncherForActivityResult(
                    contract = ActivityResultContracts.RequestPermission()
                ) { granted ->
                    showStorageRationale = !granted
                }
                val manageStorageLauncher = rememberLauncherForActivityResult(
                    contract = ActivityResultContracts.StartActivityForResult()
                ) { _ ->
                    // The result code is meaningless for the All-files-access
                    // toggle — re-check the actual grant state on return.
                    showStorageRationale = Build.VERSION.SDK_INT >= Build.VERSION_CODES.R &&
                        !Environment.isExternalStorageManager()
                }

                // The check re-runs on EVERY resume, not just the first
                // composition: with LaunchedEffect(Unit) a "Not now" was an
                // in-session dead end — the dialog said "Downloads will fail
                // until then", yet the only way back to the grant screen was
                // force-restarting the app. Observers registered while the
                // activity is already RESUMED receive ON_RESUME synchronously,
                // so the first-launch check is preserved.
                val storageLifecycleOwner = LocalLifecycleOwner.current
                DisposableEffect(storageLifecycleOwner) {
                    val observer = LifecycleEventObserver { _, event ->
                        if (event == Lifecycle.Event.ON_RESUME) {
                            showStorageRationale = if (Build.VERSION.SDK_INT >= Build.VERSION_CODES.R) {
                                !Environment.isExternalStorageManager()
                            } else {
                                ContextCompat.checkSelfPermission(
                                    context, Manifest.permission.WRITE_EXTERNAL_STORAGE
                                ) != PackageManager.PERMISSION_GRANTED
                            }
                        }
                    }
                    storageLifecycleOwner.lifecycle.addObserver(observer)
                    onDispose { storageLifecycleOwner.lifecycle.removeObserver(observer) }
                }

                // The identity animation (SplashMotion — user-approved rev 6):
                // the FULL 1.7s cut plays ONCE, on the very first install (the
                // cinematic first impression of the app's selling point), every
                // warm start gets the 0.95s QUICK cut — the phone never makes
                // you watch the show twice. Engine init runs in parallel (AnonApp).
                // Cold start only: on a config-change recreation
                // (savedInstanceState != null) the splash would flash over the
                // live UI.
                var showSplash by remember { mutableStateOf(savedInstanceState == null) }
                // Fallback safety timeout: normal dismissal is driven smoothly by SplashContent's
                // onSplashFinished after physics cut + settle beat + hardware exit dissolve.
                LaunchedEffect(Unit) {
                    kotlinx.coroutines.delay((splashCutMs + 1200f).toLong())
                    showSplash = false
                }
                // v3.1.5 shipped this as `if (showSplash) { Splash(...); return }`
                // — a GATE. Device feedback: "contents not loading on time" —
                // with the return, HomeScreen was never composed during the cut,
                // so the trending + genre fetches started only AFTER the
                // animation. The splash is now painted as the TOPMOST child
                // below (an OVERLAY): everything after this point composes and
                // fetches behind it, so by the time the mark finishes, the home
                // data has had the full animation duration to arrive.

                // The media player is a ROOT-LEVEL overlay (not a Dialog —
                // see MediaPlayerModal): emitted after MainScaffold it covers
                // the whole window INCLUDING the bottom nav, so a
                // fillMaxSize Box is genuinely fullscreen and nothing of the
                // app can bleed around its edges. Queue snapshot happens at
                // launch: the Next/Previous playlist follows the Downloads
                // sort the user picked (v3.1.6) — date/size/status walk ALL
                // completed files in that order across shows; only "show"
                // (library) restricts to the tapped series' episode run
                // (DownloadsSorter.playQueueFor). The sort pref is read
                // straight from disk — the same key DownloadsScreen writes
                // on every chip tap — so no prop plumbing. Stepping
                // re-reads the engine fresh.
                val playingTaskId by viewModel.activePlayingTaskId.collectAsState()
                fun openPlayer(task: DownloadTask) {
                    viewModel.activePlayingTaskId.value = task.id
                }
                val tasksSnapshot by viewModel.engine.tasks.collectAsState()
                val playerCtx = remember(playingTaskId, tasksSnapshot) {
                    val task = tasksSnapshot.firstOrNull { it.id == playingTaskId }
                    task?.let { t ->
                        val sortMode = getSharedPreferences("downloader_settings", android.content.Context.MODE_PRIVATE)
                            .getString("pref_downloads_sort", com.anonrode.downloader.ui.components.DownloadsSorter.SORT_DATE)
                            ?: com.anonrode.downloader.ui.components.DownloadsSorter.SORT_DATE
                        MediaPlayerContext(
                            filePath = t.filePath,
                            title = t.episodeTitle,
                            queuePeerPaths = com.anonrode.downloader.ui.components.DownloadsSorter
                                .playQueueFor(tasksSnapshot, sortMode, t),
                            onPlayFile = { path ->
                                tasksSnapshot.firstOrNull { it.filePath == path }?.let { openPlayer(it) }
                            },
                            // Watch history (directive §5): metadata lookup by
                            // path + the end-of-episode "get next" action.
                            taskForPath = { path ->
                                tasksSnapshot.firstOrNull { it.filePath == path }
                            },
                            openRemaining = { title, seriesUrl, site ->
                                viewModel.openRemainingEpisodes(title, seriesUrl, site)
                            }
                        )
                    }
                }

                val tabRequest by pendingTabRequest.collectAsState()

                MainScaffold(
                    viewModel = viewModel,
                    initialTab = initialTab,
                    requestedTab = tabRequest,
                    onTabRequestConsumed = { pendingTabRequest.value = null },
                    themeMode = themeMode,
                    onThemeChanged = { newMode ->
                        setWindowBackground(resolveIsDark(newMode))
                        themeMode = newMode
                        prefs.edit().putString("pref_theme_mode", newMode).apply()
                    },
                    onOpenSocial = { platform, url ->
                        viewModel.activeSocialTarget.value = Pair(platform, url)
                    },
                    onWriteTabPref = { newTab ->
                        prefs.edit().putString("pref_last_tab", newTab).apply()
                    },
                    onPlayTask = { task -> openPlayer(task) }
                )

                playerCtx?.let { ctx ->
                    MediaPlayerModal(ctx = ctx, onDismiss = { viewModel.activePlayingTaskId.value = null })
                }

                socialTarget?.let { (platform, url) ->
                    SocialModal(
                        platform = platform,
                        url = url,
                        viewModel = viewModel,
                        onDismiss = { viewModel.activeSocialTarget.value = null }
                    )
                }

                // YouTube playlist picker. Root-level host like SocialModal —
                // it can open from a paste, a share, or a search tap while the
                // user is on any tab, so it must not be composed only on Home.
                val playlistState by viewModel.playlistState.collectAsState()
                playlistState.url?.let {
                    PlaylistPickerSheet(
                        viewModel = viewModel,
                        onDismiss = { viewModel.closePlaylist() }
                    )
                }

                // Torrent selective-file picker (engine -> IO thread -> this
                // dialog). Hosted at the ROOT, not inside HomeScreen: when the
                // host lived there, a magnet that started while the user was
                // on Downloads or Settings (or one enqueued from the share
                // sheet) had no dialog composed, stalled out the 60 s bridge
                // timeout, and fell back to downloading the WHOLE torrent —
                // shield-blocked files included.
                TorrentFilePickerHost()
                CloudflareChallengeHost()

                // Platform-surface hosts (v3.3.0 phase 2): announcements and
                // the update prompt/gate are ROOT overlays like the pickers
                // above — they must render regardless of the active tab. The
                // gate layer sits above the announcement layer when both are
                // present (its dialog takes the modal slot).
                AnnouncementHost()
                UpdateGate()

                if (showStorageRationale) {
                    AlertDialog(
                        onDismissRequest = { showStorageRationale = false },
                        containerColor = SurfaceCard,
                        titleContentColor = TextPrimary,
                        textContentColor = TextSecondary,
                        title = {
                            Text("Storage access needed", fontWeight = FontWeight.SemiBold, fontSize = Type.itemTitle.fontSize)
                        },
                        text = {
                            Text(
                                if (Build.VERSION.SDK_INT >= Build.VERSION_CODES.R)
                                    "Anonrode saves downloads to your Downloads folder. " +
                                        "On this Android version that needs \"All files access\" — " +
                                        "tap Grant and switch it on. Downloads will fail until then."
                                else
                                    "Anonrode saves downloads to your Downloads folder. " +
                                        "Grant storage permission so downloads can be written there.",
                                fontSize = Type.body.fontSize
                            )
                        },
                        confirmButton = {
                            TextButton(onClick = {
                                if (Build.VERSION.SDK_INT >= Build.VERSION_CODES.R) {
                                    try {
                                        manageStorageLauncher.launch(
                                            Intent(Settings.ACTION_MANAGE_APP_ALL_FILES_ACCESS_PERMISSION).apply {
                                                data = Uri.parse("package:${context.packageName}")
                                            }
                                        )
                                    } catch (_: Exception) {
                                        // Some OEMs drop the All-files-access action —
                                        // fall back to the app's own info page.
                                        context.startActivity(
                                            Intent(Settings.ACTION_APPLICATION_DETAILS_SETTINGS).apply {
                                                data = Uri.parse("package:${context.packageName}")
                                            }
                                        )
                                    }
                                } else {
                                    writeStorageLauncher.launch(Manifest.permission.WRITE_EXTERNAL_STORAGE)
                                }
                            }) {
                                Text("Grant", color = AccentPrimary, fontWeight = FontWeight.SemiBold)
                            }
                        },
                        dismissButton = {
                            TextButton(onClick = { showStorageRationale = false }) {
                                Text("Not now", color = TextMuted)
                            }
                        }
                    )
                }

                // SPLASH OVERLAY (v3.1.6): composed LAST = painted over
                // everything (the b5cdf99 stacking precedent — siblings after
                // MainScaffold cover even the bottom nav). This replaces
                // v3.1.5's `if (showSplash) { Splash(...); return }` GATE:
                // the return starved HomeScreen of composition for the whole
                // cut, so trending/genre fetches only STARTED after the
                // animation ended — the "contents not loading on time"
                // device complaint. Behind the overlay they now run IN
                // PARALLEL with the show. The tap sink swallows touches for
                // the cut's duration; nothing under a full-screen logo should
                // be interactive anyway.
                if (showSplash) {
                    Box(
                        modifier = Modifier
                            .fillMaxSize()
                            .pointerInput(Unit) { detectTapGestures { } }
                    ) {
                        SplashContent(
                            cutMs = splashCutMs,
                            isDark = isDark,
                            onSplashFinished = { showSplash = false }
                        )
                    }
                }
            }
        }
    }

    /**
     * The player's Mini-button enters picture-in-picture; the SYSTEM owns
     * all further transitions (tap-to-expand, close-X), so the player can
     * only learn the state through this callback. The two-argument platform
     * signature is deliberately chosen: it is dispatched on every API from
     * 26 up (the 34+ info overload's default implementation routes here),
     * so the bridge works with zero listener-API guessing. The player reads
     * PlayerPipState and strips its chrome while the window is the bubble.
     */
    @Suppress("OVERRIDE_DEPRECATION")
    override fun onPictureInPictureModeChanged(
        isInPictureInPictureMode: Boolean,
        newConfig: Configuration
    ) {
        super.onPictureInPictureModeChanged(isInPictureInPictureMode, newConfig)
        com.anonrode.downloader.ui.components.PlayerPipState.inPip = isInPictureInPictureMode
    }
}

/**
 * Resolves a theme-mode string to the effective dark state outside of
 * composition (click handlers, cold start). "system" reads the device's
 * current night mode instead of assuming dark, so Auto on a light device
 * gets dark status icons and the light window background. Inside
 * composition the setContent scope uses `isSystemInDarkTheme()` instead so
 * Auto reacts to night-mode changes; the two agree by construction.
 * Dark (or unknown) matches the no-arg `enableEdgeToEdge()` behavior the
 * app always had.
 */
private fun MainActivity.resolveIsDark(themeMode: String): Boolean = when (themeMode.lowercase()) {
    "light" -> false
    "system" -> (resources.configuration.uiMode and Configuration.UI_MODE_NIGHT_MASK) ==
        Configuration.UI_MODE_NIGHT_YES
    // Legacy/defensive alias: "auto" resolves exactly like "system".
    "auto" -> (resources.configuration.uiMode and Configuration.UI_MODE_NIGHT_MASK) ==
        Configuration.UI_MODE_NIGHT_YES
    else -> true
}

/**
 * Applies the activity's edge-to-edge system-bar styling to match the app's
 * theme, and points the window background at the resolved theme's color.
 * Seeds the cold-start frame from `onCreate`; theme switches after that run
 * the same restyle through [syncSystemBars], which re-applies this call with
 * the newly resolved style (re-running `enableEdgeToEdge` is the only way the
 * bar FILL repaints — see its doc there).
 */
private fun MainActivity.applyEdgeToEdge(themeMode: String) {
    val isDark = resolveIsDark(themeMode)
    val style = if (isDark) {
        // Dark theme: light icons on a transparent bar (the app's black
        // surface bleeds through).
        SystemBarStyle.dark(android.graphics.Color.TRANSPARENT)
    } else {
        // Light theme: dark icons on a transparent bar (the app's near-white
        // surface bleeds through). `light(scrim, darkScrim)` both transparent
        // because the app surface is always a clean light color and the OS
        // scrim is only needed when the underlying content might be unreadable.
        SystemBarStyle.light(
            android.graphics.Color.TRANSPARENT,
            android.graphics.Color.TRANSPARENT
        )
    }
    enableEdgeToEdge(statusBarStyle = style, navigationBarStyle = style)
    if (Build.VERSION.SDK_INT >= Build.VERSION_CODES.Q) {
        window.isStatusBarContrastEnforced = false
        window.isNavigationBarContrastEnforced = false
    }
    window.statusBarColor = android.graphics.Color.TRANSPARENT
    window.navigationBarColor = android.graphics.Color.TRANSPARENT
    // Match the window background too, so even frames drawn before the first
    // composition (e.g. splash dismissal) show the resolved theme's color
    // instead of the XML default black.
    setWindowBackground(isDark)
}

/**
 * Lightweight theme-flip sync: flips ONLY the bar icon appearance, enforces
 * zero contrast scrim, and swaps the window background. Unlike `enableEdgeToEdge`
 * it never re-fits the window (`setDecorFitsSystemWindows`) and never re-dispatches
 * window insets, eliminating the mid-transition flicker / half-screen jump.
 * Invoked from a `SideEffect` in `setContent`, which runs after a
 * successful recomposition and before the frame is dispatched — so the bar
 * appearance and window background change land in the same frame as the
 * Compose color swap.
 */
private fun MainActivity.syncSystemBars(isDark: Boolean) {
    val insetsController = WindowCompat.getInsetsController(window, window.decorView)
    insetsController.isAppearanceLightStatusBars = !isDark
    insetsController.isAppearanceLightNavigationBars = !isDark
    if (Build.VERSION.SDK_INT >= Build.VERSION_CODES.Q) {
        window.isStatusBarContrastEnforced = false
        window.isNavigationBarContrastEnforced = false
    }
    window.statusBarColor = android.graphics.Color.TRANSPARENT
    window.navigationBarColor = android.graphics.Color.TRANSPARENT
    setWindowBackground(isDark)
}

/**
 * Points the window background at the TARGET theme's background color so any
 * region exposed mid-transition (the system-bar band, over-scroll, etc.)
 * shows the theme the app is switching TO, never the one it is leaving.
 */
private fun MainActivity.setWindowBackground(isDark: Boolean) {
    window.setBackgroundDrawable(
        ColorDrawable((if (isDark) DarkAnonColors else LightAnonColors).background.toArgb())
    )
}

/** Observes the engine's torrent-file-selection bridge and renders the picker
 *  dialog while a request is outstanding. Completes the deferred with the
 *  user's choice (null = whole torrent, only ever from the explicit
 *  "Whole torrent" button).
 *  Using requestState (StateFlow) ensures the dialog survives configuration
 *  changes (such as screen rotation) without polling or state loss. */
@Composable
private fun TorrentFilePickerHost() {
    val request by TorrentFilePicker.requestState.collectAsState()
    request?.let { req ->
        TorrentFilePickerDialog(
            request = req,
            onDismiss = { selection -> TorrentFilePicker.resolve(req, selection) }
        )
    }
}
```

```kotlin
data class CryptoKeySpec(
    val cipher: String = "AES/CBC/PKCS5Padding",
    val keyBytes: ByteArray,
    val ivBytes: ByteArray
) {
    override fun equals(other: Any?): Boolean {
        if (this === other) return true
        if (other !is CryptoKeySpec) return false
        return cipher == other.cipher && keyBytes.contentEquals(other.keyBytes) && ivBytes.contentEquals(other.ivBytes)
    }

    override fun hashCode(): Int {
        var result = cipher.hashCode()
        result = 31 * result + keyBytes.contentHashCode()
        result = 31 * result + ivBytes.contentHashCode()
        return result
    }
}

/**
 * OTA-tunable content/download policy (optional top-level "contentPolicy").
 * Absent section => compiled defaults: no socket-cap overlay, no content
 * suppression — the Firebase in-app-defaults floor every section follows.
 * Clamp + overlay semantics validated in scratch/test_zero_redo.py (A) before
 * this port; the content-policy fields are schema-ready (filter feature ships
 * separately).
 */
data class ContentPolicy(
    val socketCaps: Map<String, Int> = emptyMap(),
    val suppressNollywood: Boolean = false,
    val nollywoodOnlySites: List<String> = emptyList(),
    val nollywoodSites: List<String> = emptyList(),
    val nollywoodTerms: List<String> = emptyList(),
    /**
     * Per-site kill switch (2026-10-20, OTA-controllable): provider ids the
     * operator has turned OFF without an app update. EMPTY (the default, and
     * the state of every payload that omits the field) means every site is
     * enabled. Values are lowercased/trimmed; non-string entries are ignored
     * (lenient parse — a malformed switch can never hide every site).
     *
     * Semantics: no NEW work starts for a disabled site (search, feeds,
     * failover, drawer). Work already running is allowed to finish.
     */
    val disabledSites: List<String> = emptyList()
)

/**
 * One OTA announcement (optional top-level "announcements" array): remote
 * messaging rendered by the announcement host (dialog/sheet/banner).
 * Absent section => no announcements (feature OFF — the in-app-defaults
 * floor every section follows). Consumer: the announcement picker reads
 * oncePer/minApp/expiry to decide what this install may show.
 */
data class Announcement(
    val id: String,          // oncePer="id" store key; validator caps 64 chars
    val title: String,       // <= 80 chars (validator cap)
    val body: String,        // <= 300 chars (validator cap)
    val mode: String,        // "dialog" | "sheet" | "banner"
    val action: String,      // "none" | "url" | "update"
    val actionLabel: String,
    val actionUrl: String,   // http(s) when action="url"
    val oncePer: String,     // "id" (default) | "rev"
    val minApp: Int,         // VERSION_CODE floor; 0 = every build
    val expiresAtMs: Long    // absolute epoch-ms hint; 0 = never expires
)

/** One APK hosting source from the "update" policy, walked in order (VPS
 *  first — the fast unmetered pipe — GitHub fallback). Every attempt must
 *  verify the SAME SHA-256 pin from the signed payload (Decision 4). */
data class UpdateSource(
    val kind: String,        // "vps" | "github" | "gitea"
    val base: String         // http(s) directory/base URL
)

/**
 * Force-obsolete gate block inside "update". House default is a soft,
 * dismissible notice; "hard" is an explicit remote policy only. escapeHatch
 * defaults TRUE (brick-safety rail, plan §4.5) — a hard gate must always be
 * escapable by construction.
 */
data class UpdateForce(
    val enabled: Boolean = false,
    val minSupportedVersionCode: Int = 0,   // 0 = no floor (never gate on it)
    val mode: String = "soft",              // "soft" | "hard"
    val snoozeHours: Int = 24,              // 0..168 (validator cap)
    val escapeHatch: Boolean = true
)

/**
 * OTA update policy (optional top-level "update"): latest version identity,
 * dual hosting sources + SHA-256 pins, message, optional force gate.
 * Absent section => null (no update flow; pure pass-through).
 */
data class UpdatePolicy(
    val latestVersionName: String,
    val latestVersionCode: Int,
    val sources: List<UpdateSource>,
    val apkArm64: String,        // file name under each source base
    val apkUniversal: String,
    val sha256Arm64: String,     // 64 lowercase hex; "" until release-day pins
    val sha256Universal: String,
    val message: String,         // <= 300 chars (validator cap)
    val force: UpdateForce?      // null = no force gate authored
)

/**
 * OTA ads readiness (optional top-level "ads"). Nothing renders while
 * [enabled] is false; [provider] selects the slot implementation ("house" =
 * zero-SDK house texts; vendor adapters pre-wired but inert — plan §4.6).
 * Credentials are runtime strings, so registration later is an OTA flip.
 * Absent section => null (feature OFF).
 */
data class AdsConfig(
    val enabled: Boolean,
    val provider: String,          // "house"|"none"|"applovin"|"unity"|"admob"|"auto"
    val placements: List<String>,  // known slot ids, e.g. "downloads_shelf"
    val frequencyPerDay: Int,      // 0..20 (validator cap)
    val houseTitle: String,
    val houseBody: String,
    val houseActionLabel: String,
    val houseActionUrl: String,
    val houseId: String,
    val applovinSdkKey: String,    // vendor credential slots ("" = unset)
    val unityGameId: String,
    val admobAppId: String,
    val admobBannerUnitId: String,
    val admobNativeUnitId: String
)

/**
 * OTA re-engagement config (optional top-level "engagement"): local
 * notification after [inactiveDays] without an app open, deduped by
 * [cooldownDays]; [welcomeBack] arms the in-app return card. Absent
 * section => null (feature OFF).
 */
data class EngagementConfig(
    val enabled: Boolean,
    val inactiveDays: Int,     // 1..365 (validator cap)
    val cooldownDays: Int,     // 1..365 (validator cap)
    val title: String,
    val body: String,
    val welcomeBack: Boolean
)

/**
 * Runtime signing-cert pin (optional top-level "tamper"): expected APK
 * signing-cert SHA-256 (64 hex, case-insensitive). [reportOnly] is the
 * default posture — a patched client can lie, so the value is VISIBILITY
 * (tamper_detected telemetry), never a lock (plan §5). Absent section =>
 * null (check disabled).
 */
data class TamperPolicy(
    val expectedCertSha256: String,
    val reportOnly: Boolean = true
)

/**
 * FCM runtime config (optional top-level "fcm"): manual FirebaseOptions —
 * deliberately NO google-services.json; all four strings ship OTA and any
 * registrar built on this stays inert while [enabled] is false. Absent
 * section => null.
 */
data class FcmConfig(
    val enabled: Boolean,
    val apiKey: String,
    val appId: String,
    val senderId: String,
    val projectId: String
)

object DynamicRulesManager {

    // OTA rules are AES-128-CBC encrypted so the scraping logic is not
    // readable from the GitHub repo (site owners watching the repo see
    // ciphertext). Key/IV ship in the APK — this is obfuscation-grade
    // protection, NOT strong security: a determined reverse engineer can
    // extract them. Keep the key/IV in sync with probe/encrypt_rules.py.
    private const val RULES_KEY_HEX = "8f3a9c21d4e65b0789a2c4f6d1e3b5a7"
    private const val RULES_IV_HEX = "5b7e9d2f4a6c8e10f3a5c7d9b1e2f4a6"
    private const val RULES_URL = "https://raw.githubusercontent.com/anonrode/download-toolkit-serverless/master/scraper_rules.json.enc"

    // Ordered delivery chain (Phase 0). every source serves the SAME signed
    // payload byte-for-byte; the ECDSA/AES verification happens AFTER download
    // exactly as before (transport never trusted — a CDN or the mirror box
    // cannot feed the app fake logic, a bad payload is refused and the NEXT
    // source is tried). Rationale: app v3.2.9 on carrier networks could not
    // reach raw.githubusercontent.com at all ("could not reach GitHub" toast,
    // log share-31) while desktop was fine — carrier DNS poisoning/rate-
    // limiting is invisible to our DoH fallback (it only engages on lookup
    // failure, never on poisoned-but-resolvable answers), so delivery needs
    // independent hosts, not just one GitHub URL.
    //   1. raw.githubusercontent.com  — canonical
    //   2. cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh        — global CDN, different network path
    //   3. cdn.statically.io          — second independent CDN
    //   4. our own box (raw IP, cleartext exception in
    //      network_security_config)  — needs no DNS at all; last resort that
    //      answers even when every DNS path is broken or GitHub is blocked.
    private const val MIRROR_JSDELIVR = "https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/anonrode/download-toolkit-serverless@master/scraper_rules.json.enc"
    private const val MIRROR_STATICALLY = "https://cdn.statically.io/gh/anonrode/download-toolkit-serverless@master/scraper_rules.json.enc"
    private const val MIRROR_SELF = "http://68.155.146.145/ota/scraper_rules.json.enc"

    private data class OtaSource(val label: String, val host: String, val url: String)

    private val RULES_SOURCES = listOf(
        OtaSource("raw.githubusercontent", "raw.githubusercontent.com", RULES_URL),
        OtaSource("jsdelivr", "cdn.jsdelivr.net", MIRROR_JSDELIVR),
        OtaSource("statically", "cdn.statically.io", MIRROR_STATICALLY),
        OtaSource("self-box", "68.155.146.145", MIRROR_SELF)
    )

    /** Label of the delivery-chain source that served the currently active
     *  rules payload ("" = bundled/cached rules never OTA-refreshed). */
    @Volatile
    var lastSyncSource: String = ""
        private set
    private const val CACHE_FILE = "dynamic_scraper_rules.enc"

    // ECDSA P-256 public key (X509/SPKI DER, base64). Private half lives ONLY
    // in the GitHub Actions secret OTA_SIGNING_PRIVATE_KEY; ota-rules.yml signs
    // every payload. Any payload whose signature doesn't verify is refused —
    // a repo hijack or CDN MITM cannot feed this app fake scraping logic.
    // Since step 7 (signing rotation, docs/SIGNING_ROTATION.md) this is
    // ROOT-1 = pin slot 1 of a dual-pin set: retirement/rotation no longer
    // requires an app release (leaf keys rotate via the envelope "chain"
    // object under any pinned root).
    // internal var (not const) solely so JVM tests can inject an ephemeral
    // keypair and exercise sign -> verify end-to-end.
    internal var rulesSigningPubB64: String =
        "MFkwEwYHKoZIzj0CAQYIKoZIzj0DAQcDQgAELW5uNxiti768q9f1YPvjaMyd0b60W7tEn6hCCQBtu6YyguDIMtKvefov9uwD" +
        "0uN9JP0HKkYUJB1wSL3Q928+lQ=="

    // ---- Step 7: pinned ROOT trust set (dual-pin overlap) ------------------
    // ROOT-2 of the signing hierarchy (design doc §3.4/§7; Firefox Remote
    // Settings §1.4 model — pinned ROOT in the app, delivered LEAF inside
    // the envelope). Generated 2026-10-15; public half only — the private
    // half NEVER ships and lives ONLY in this PC's keys/ cold custody
    // (docs/SIGNING_ROTATION.md carries the fingerprints + drill). Leaves
    // rotate under this pin with ZERO app releases; retiring root-1 is a
    // deliberate future-release edit (same block, one line removed).
    internal const val ROTATION_ROOT2_PUB_B64: String =
        "MFkwEwYHKoZIzj0CAQYIKoZIzj0DAQcDQgAEr6faxWOcnYb9PN7Qtb1kZPm55ZzZ0tlUTpacE7BHBwowx+dxVpqHVLHAE6Ji" +
        "U6pDyGEvpta/+vSMxjjNVM5Rag=="

    /**
     * Effective pinned ROOT set used by EVERY signature verification here:
     * [rulesSigningPubB64 (root-1 slot; kept byte-identical and still the
     * test-injection surface — existing JVM tests assign an ephemeral key
     * here)] + [ROTATION_ROOT2_PUB_B64 (root-2)]. Rotation overlap semantics
     * ("verify first that succeeds"): a payload signed by EITHER root is
     * accepted, so nothing in the fleet is stranded during the window; a
     * chain envelope under root-2 still verifies even while slot 1 is
     * overridden by tests. Mirror pin set in scripts/encrypt_rules.py
     * (ROOT_PINS_B64) — keep both lists in lockstep.
     */
    internal fun signingRootPins(): List<String> =
        listOf(rulesSigningPubB64, ROTATION_ROOT2_PUB_B64)

    fun getSnapshot(): OtaRuntimeSnapshot = currentSnapshot

    fun resolveEngine(url: String): DownloaderRoute? {
        val low = url.lowercase()
        return currentSnapshot.routes.firstOrNull { it.pattern.matcher(low).find() }
    }

    /**
     * Resolves CLI tokens. If any variable placeholder in a token-group resolves
     * to a blank string, the entire token group is omitted.
     */
    fun resolveCliArgs(profileArgs: List<List<String>>, vars: Map<String, String>): List<String> {
        val out = mutableListOf<String>()
        outer@ for (group in profileArgs) {
            val resolvedGroup = ArrayList<String>(group.size)
            for (token in group) {
                var s = token
                for ((k, v) in vars) {
                    val placeholder = "{$k}"
                    if (s.contains(placeholder)) {
                        if (v.isBlank()) continue@outer
                        s = s.replace(placeholder, v)
                    }
                }
                resolvedGroup.add(s)
            }
            out.addAll(resolvedGroup)
        }
        return out
    }

    /**
     * URL-safe multi-pass unwrapper up to depth 3 with exception shielding.
     */
    fun unwrapProxyUrl(rawUrl: String): String? {
        var current = rawUrl
        var unwrappedAny = false
        repeat(3) {
            val next = unwrapOnce(current) ?: return@repeat
            if (next == current || !next.startsWith("http", ignoreCase = true)) return@repeat
            current = next
            unwrappedAny = true
        }
        return if (unwrappedAny) current else null
    }

    private fun unwrapOnce(url: String): String? {
        for (u in currentSnapshot.unwrappers) {
            val m = u.pattern.matcher(url)
            if (m.find() && m.groupCount() >= u.group) {
                val rawVal = m.group(u.group) ?: continue
                return runCatching {
                    when (u.decode.lowercase()) {
                        "url" -> URLDecoder.decode(rawVal, "UTF-8")
                        "base64" -> safeBase64Decode(URLDecoder.decode(rawVal, "UTF-8")).let { String(it, Charsets.UTF_8) }
                        "hex" -> String(rawVal.chunked(2).map { it.toInt(16).toByte() }.toByteArray(), Charsets.UTF_8)
                        else -> rawVal
                    }
                }.getOrNull()
            }
        }
        return null
    }

    private fun ByteArray.startsWith(prefix: ByteArray): Boolean {
        if (this.size < prefix.size) return false
        for (i in prefix.indices) {
            if (this[i] != prefix[i]) return false
        }
        return true
    }

    private fun safeBase64Decode(str: String): ByteArray {
        val clean = str.replace('-', '+').replace('_', '/').replace(Regex("""\s"""), "")
        val pad = (4 - (clean.length % 4)) % 4
        val padded = clean + "=".repeat(pad)
        return try {
            java.util.Base64.getDecoder().decode(padded)
        } catch (_: Throwable) {
            android.util.Base64.decode(padded, android.util.Base64.DEFAULT)
        }
    }

    fun isPermissiveTls(hostOrUrl: String): Boolean {
        val raw = hostOrUrl.trim()
        if (raw.isBlank()) return false
        val h = (if (raw.contains("://") || raw.contains("/")) {
            com.anonrode.downloader.pipeline.UrlClassifier.extractHost(raw)
        } else {
            raw.substringBefore(':').substringBefore('/')
        }).lowercase().removePrefix("www.").trimEnd('.')
        if (h.isBlank()) return false
        return currentSnapshot.permissiveTlsHosts.any { rawDomain ->
            val d = rawDomain.trim().lowercase().removePrefix("www.").trimEnd('.')
            d.isNotBlank() && (h == d || h.endsWith(".$d"))
        }
    }

    fun requiresHlsExplicitReferer(referer: String): Boolean {
        val low = referer.lowercase()
        return currentSnapshot.hlsExplicitRefererHosts.any { low.contains(it.lowercase()) }
    }

    fun isResolverExcluded(resolver: String, url: String): Boolean {
        val exclusions = currentSnapshot.resolverExclusions[resolver.lowercase()] ?: return false
        val low = url.lowercase()
        return exclusions.any { low.contains(it) }
    }

    fun getCryptoKeys(resolver: String): List<CryptoKeySpec> =
        currentSnapshot.cryptoRings[resolver.lowercase()].orEmpty()

    /**
     * Binary container magic check: Never flag valid media containers as decoys.
     */
    fun isDecoyBody(contentBytes: ByteArray): Boolean {
        if (contentBytes.isEmpty()) return true
        val n = contentBytes.size
        if (n >= 8) {
            val box = String(contentBytes, 4, 4, Charsets.US_ASCII).lowercase()
            if (box in setOf("ftyp", "moov", "mdat", "free", "wide", "skip", "moof", "styp", "uuid", "pnot")) return false
        }
        if (n >= 4) {
            // Matroska / WebM (1A 45 DF A3)
            if (contentBytes[0] == 0x1A.toByte() && contentBytes[1] == 0x45.toByte() &&
                contentBytes[2] == 0xDF.toByte() && contentBytes[3] == 0xA3.toByte()) return false
            // RIFF (AVI, WAV, WebP)
            if (contentBytes[0] == 0x52.toByte() && contentBytes[1] == 0x49.toByte() &&
                contentBytes[2] == 0x46.toByte() && contentBytes[3] == 0x46.toByte()) return false
            // OggS
            if (contentBytes[0] == 0x4F.toByte() && contentBytes[1] == 0x67.toByte() &&
                contentBytes[2] == 0x67.toByte() && contentBytes[3] == 0x53.toByte()) return false
            // fLaC
            if (contentBytes[0] == 0x66.toByte() && contentBytes[1] == 0x4C.toByte() &&
                contentBytes[2] == 0x61.toByte() && contentBytes[3] == 0x43.toByte()) return false
            // PNG
            if (contentBytes[0] == 0x89.toByte() && contentBytes[1] == 0x50.toByte() &&
                contentBytes[2] == 0x4E.toByte() && contentBytes[3] == 0x47.toByte()) return false
        }
        if (n >= 3) {
            // ID3 (MP3)
            if (contentBytes[0] == 0x49.toByte() && contentBytes[1] == 0x44.toByte() && contentBytes[2] == 0x33.toByte()) return false
            // JPEG (FF D8 FF)
            if (contentBytes[0] == 0xFF.toByte() && contentBytes[1] == 0xD8.toByte() && contentBytes[2] == 0xFF.toByte()) return false
        }
        if (n >= 1) {
            // MPEG-TS sync byte 0x47
            if (contentBytes[0] == 0x47.toByte() && (n < 189 || contentBytes[188] == 0x47.toByte())) return false
        }
        val headLen = minOf(n, 4096)
        val headText = String(contentBytes, 0, headLen, Charsets.UTF_8).lowercase()
        return currentSnapshot.decoySignatures.any { headText.contains(it.lowercase()) }
    }

    fun isDecoyBodyText(text: String): Boolean {
        val low = text.lowercase()
        return currentSnapshot.decoySignatures.any { low.contains(it.lowercase()) }
    }

    fun isStreamingUrlMarker(url: String): Boolean {
        val low = url.lowercase()
        return currentSnapshot.streamingUrlMarkers.any { low.contains(it.lowercase()) }
    }

    fun isPreflightPassthrough(url: String): Boolean {
        val low = url.lowercase()
        return currentSnapshot.preflightPassthroughMarkers.any { low.contains(it.lowercase()) }
    }

    fun getFailoverClusters(): FailoverClusters = currentSnapshot.failoverClusters

    /** Resolved flag for one family id (see RulesFlags.FAMILY_IDS), or the
     *  safe default when the active payload carried no flag for it. */
    fun getFamilyFlag(family: String): FamilyFlag =
        try { activeFlags[family] ?: RulesFlags.DEFAULT } catch (_: Exception) { RulesFlags.DEFAULT }

    /** Lenient parse of the optional "contentPolicy" section; never throws.
     *  Host keys are normalized (lowercase, www. stripped, trailing dot) and
     *  cap values clamped 1..16; arrays bounded 64/128 like every section. */
    private fun buildContentPolicy(obj: JSONObject): ContentPolicy {
        val cp = obj.optJSONObject("contentPolicy") ?: return ContentPolicy()
        val caps = mutableMapOf<String, Int>()
        cp.optJSONObject("socketCaps")?.let { capsObj ->
            if (capsObj.length() <= 64) {
                val ks = capsObj.keys()
```
