            if (kdArr != null) {
                for (i in 0 until kdArr.length()) {
                    val h = kdArr.optString(i)
                    if (h.isNotBlank()) knownDead.add(h.lowercase())
                }
            }

            // OTA locker host seeds: LockerRegistry.classify() consults these
            // first (prioritization), but never gates — unknown hosts still
            // get probed and can work on first contact.
            val lhArr = obj.optJSONArray("lockerHosts")
            if (lhArr != null) {
                for (i in 0 until lhArr.length()) {
                    val h = lhArr.optString(i)
                    if (h.isNotBlank()) lockerHosts.add(h.lowercase())
                }
            }

            // Remote error-log sink (Track 6): accepted only as a plausible
            // http(s) endpoint — anything else is treated as absent rather
            // than handed to URL.openConnection. Published with the rest of
            // the state in the atomic-swap block below.
            val remoteLogCandidate = obj.optString("remote_logging_url", "").trim()
            val remoteLogSink =
                if (remoteLogCandidate.startsWith("https://") || remoteLogCandidate.startsWith("http://")) {
                    remoteLogCandidate
                } else ""

            // OTA content/download policy (2026-10): socket-cap overlay (live
            // consumer: HostPolicyRegistry) + content-policy fields (schema-
            // ready). Lenient like every section; absent => compiled defaults.
            var contentPolicy = buildContentPolicy(obj)

            // v3.3.0 platform-surface sections (plan §4.1): announcements,
            // update, ads, engagement (flag-backed families, blanked below
            // when their flag holds them back) + tamper and fcm (self-gating
            // via their own enabled / presence flags). Lenient like every
            // section; absent => OFF.
            var announcements = buildAnnouncements(obj)
            var updatePolicy = buildUpdatePolicy(obj)
            var adsConfig = buildAdsConfig(obj)
            var engagementConfig = buildEngagementConfig(obj)
            val tamperPolicy = buildTamperPolicy(obj)
            val fcmConfig = buildFcmConfig(obj)

            val ttl = obj.optLong("tokenTtlMinutes", 10L).coerceIn(1L, 240L)

            // Ordered search strategy chains: when a site's primary search
            // breaks (dramarain ?s= lesson), OTA adds fallback strategies as
            // data — no APK rebuild.
            val ssObj = obj.optJSONObject("searchStrategies")
            if (ssObj != null) {
                val keys = ssObj.keys()
                while (keys.hasNext()) {
                    val k = keys.next()
                    val arr = ssObj.optJSONArray(k) ?: continue
                    val list = mutableListOf<JSONObject>()
                    for (i in 0 until arr.length()) {
                        arr.optJSONObject(i)?.let { list.add(it) }
                    }
                    if (list.isNotEmpty()) searchStrategies[k.lowercase()] = list
                }
            }

            // Declarative step pipelines (search/episode navigation as data).
            // Lenient per site: a malformed entry or an unknown schema version
            // is skipped and journaled, never fatal — that site's compiled
            // provider fallback covers it, and the rest of the payload still
            // applies. (dynamic_providers below follows the same lenient
            // contract after the 2026-09-13 fix; it used to throw.)
            val pipelines = mutableMapOf<String, SitePipeline>()
            val pipelinesObj = obj.optJSONObject("pipelines")
            if (pipelinesObj != null) {
                val keys = pipelinesObj.keys()
                while (keys.hasNext()) {
                    val k = keys.next()
                    val pObj = pipelinesObj.optJSONObject(k) ?: continue
                    val parsed = parseSitePipeline(pObj)
                    if (parsed != null) {
                        pipelines[k.lowercase()] = parsed
                    } else {
                        skippedPipelines++
                        com.anonrode.downloader.util.DebugLog.error(
                            "OTA rules: skipping pipeline for \"$k\" (malformed or unknown schema)"
                        )
                    }
                }
            }

            // Parse any dynamic new providers added remotely.
            // optJSONObject, not getJSONObject: a non-object entry here used
            // to throw JSONException and fail the WHOLE playbook parse — one
            // stray string in dynamic_providers poisoned every OTA update for
            // every site. Malformed entries are skipped, like everywhere else
            // in this parser; id/base_url are load-bearing (a provider
            // without them can never match a URL or build a search), so an
            // entry missing either is skipped too.
            val dynamicList = obj.optJSONArray("dynamic_providers")
            if (dynamicList != null) {
                for (i in 0 until dynamicList.length()) {
                    val item = dynamicList.optJSONObject(i) ?: continue
                    val cfg = DynamicSiteConfig(
                        id = item.optString("id"),
                        displayName = item.optString("display_name"),
                        category = item.optString("category", "Media"),
                        baseUrl = item.optString("base_url"),
                        searchUrlPattern = item.optString("search_url_pattern", "{base}/?s={query}"),
                        searchType = item.optString("search_type", "html"),
                        cardSelector = item.optString("card_selector", "article"),
                        titleSelector = item.optString("title_selector", "h2, .entry-title"),
                        linkSelector = item.optString("link_selector", "a"),
                        posterSelector = item.optString("poster_selector", "img"),
                        episodeLinkSelector = item.optString("episode_link_selector", "a[href*='download']")
                    )
                    if (cfg.id.isBlank() || cfg.baseUrl.isBlank()) {
                        skippedDynProviders++
                        continue
                    }
                    dynProviders.add(GenericDeclarativeProvider(cfg))
                }
            }

            // P2-1/P2-5 enforcement — no provider edits: a family the flags
            // hold back (kill switch off, build below the family's minApp
            // floor, shadow measurement mode, or this device's stable bucket
            // outside a partial rollout) publishes its section EMPTY,
            // byte-for-byte the "missing/malformed section" state every
            // compiled fallback already engages on. The knownDead/lockerHosts
            // note from the plan holds: emptying those only loosens
            // pre-filtering, it can never break a resolution. A payload with
            // no "flags" object leaves every family at DEFAULT (enabled,
            // percent 100) — flags expire with the payload that carried them.
            val deviceUuid = RulesFlags.installUuid(appContext)
            fun familyGateBlank(family: String, blank: () -> Unit) {
                val flag = familyFlags[family] ?: return
                if (RulesFlags.isFamilyActiveForDevice(flag, family, deviceUuid)) return
                val bucket = RulesFlags.stableBucket(deviceUuid, family)
                when {
                    !flag.enabled ->
                        com.anonrode.downloader.util.DebugLog.engine(
                            "OTA rules[$ver] family \"$family\" disabled by kill flag — publishing empty (compiled fallback engages)"
                        )
                    !flag.minAppSatisfied ->
                        com.anonrode.downloader.util.DebugLog.engine(
                            "OTA rules[$ver] family \"$family\" needs app ${flag.minAppVersion}; this is " +
                                com.anonrode.downloader.BuildConfig.VERSION_CODE + " — publishing empty (minApp guard)"
                        )
                    flag.shadow ->
                        com.anonrode.downloader.util.DebugLog.engine(
                            "OTA rules[$ver] family \"$family\" in shadow mode — publishing empty (compiled control serves users)"
                        )
                    else ->
                        com.anonrode.downloader.util.DebugLog.engine(
                            "OTA rules[$ver] family \"$family\" percent rollup ${flag.percent}: bucket $bucket not selected — publishing empty for this device"
                        )
                }
                blank()
            }
            familyGateBlank("domains") { domains.clear() }
            familyGateBlank("mirrors") { mirrors.clear() }
            familyGateBlank("sites") { siteConfigs.clear() }
            familyGateBlank("resolvers") { resolverConfigs.clear() }
            familyGateBlank("directMediaExtensions") { mediaExts.clear() }
            familyGateBlank("hostPolicies") { hostPolicies.clear() }
            familyGateBlank("urlTemplates") { urlTemplates.clear() }
            familyGateBlank("knownDead") { knownDead.clear() }
            familyGateBlank("lockerHosts") { lockerHosts.clear() }
            familyGateBlank("searchStrategies") { searchStrategies.clear() }
            familyGateBlank("contentPolicy") { contentPolicy = ContentPolicy() }
            // v3.3.0 platform surfaces: a held-back family publishes OFF —
            // exact same shape as an absent section, so every consumer's
            // null/empty check doubles as the kill-switch path.
            familyGateBlank("announcements") { announcements = emptyList() }
            familyGateBlank("update") { updatePolicy = null }
            familyGateBlank("ads") { adsConfig = null }
            familyGateBlank("engagement") { engagementConfig = null }

            // P2-4 SHADOW MODE for the behavior family (Scientist rule, plan
            // slice 4): when the payload flags `pipelines` shadow, the section
            // publishes EMPTY — every provider runs its compiled control and
            // the USER-FACING RESULT IS ALWAYS CONTROL — while the parsed
            // candidate set is handed to ShadowRunner for sampled, deferred,
            // never-user-facing measurement. Promotion/kill is all payload
            // data: shadow=false + percent buckets promotes; enabled=false
            // (or no flag at all) disarms via the updateCandidates(emptyMap).
            var shadowArmed = false
            var pipelinesShadowArmed = 0
            val pipelinesFlag = familyFlags["pipelines"]
            if (pipelinesFlag != null && pipelinesFlag.enabled && pipelinesFlag.minAppSatisfied &&
                pipelinesFlag.shadow && pipelines.isNotEmpty()
            ) {
                pipelinesShadowArmed = pipelines.size
                com.anonrode.downloader.pipeline.ShadowRunner.updateCandidates(pipelines.toMap(), pipelinesFlag)
                com.anonrode.downloader.util.DebugLog.engine(
                    "OTA rules[$ver] pipelines SHADOW mode: ${pipelines.size} candidate(s) armed; published section EMPTY (compiled control serves users)"
                )
                pipelines.clear()
                shadowArmed = true
            } else {
                familyGateBlank("pipelines") { pipelines.clear() }
            }
            if (!shadowArmed) {
                com.anonrode.downloader.pipeline.ShadowRunner.updateCandidates(emptyMap(), null)
            }

            familyGateBlank("dynamic_providers") { dynProviders.clear() }

            // P2-7 set-up: previous family target-hosts for the diff —
            // captured BEFORE the atomic swap so the old/new comparison is
            // exact. Empty collections = no rules were active yet (defaults).
            val prevKnownDead = activeKnownDead
            val prevLockerHosts = activeLockerHosts
            val prevHostPolicies = activeHostPolicies
            val prevPipelines = activePipelines
            val prevActiveRev = activeRev

            val newSnapshot = buildOtaSnapshot(obj, familyFlags, deviceUuid, ver)

            // Atomic publish — readers see either the old playbook or the new
            // one, never a mix.
            activeDomains = domains
            activeMirrors = mirrors
            activeSiteConfigs = siteConfigs
            activeResolverConfigs = resolverConfigs
            activeMediaExtensions = mediaExts.ifEmpty { defaultMediaExtensions }
            activeHostPolicies = hostPolicies
            activeUrlTemplates = urlTemplates
            activeKnownDead = knownDead
            activeLockerHosts = lockerHosts
            activeSearchStrategies = searchStrategies
            activePipelines = pipelines
            dynamicProviders = dynProviders
            activeFlags = familyFlags
            activeContentPolicy = contentPolicy
            activeAnnouncements = announcements
            activeUpdatePolicy = updatePolicy
            activeAdsConfig = adsConfig
            activeEngagementConfig = engagementConfig
            activeTamperPolicy = tamperPolicy
            activeFcmConfig = fcmConfig
            remoteLoggingUrl = remoteLogSink
            tokenTtlMinutes = ttl
            currentSnapshot = newSnapshot
            // P2-2: a payload that carries a rev and survived the gate becomes
            // the new activation floor. Rev-less (legacy) payloads never move
            // the pointer — they must stay able to run on any install.
            val revNow = rev
            if (revNow != null && revNow > 0L) {
                // F11 (OTA red-team): the pointer is monotonic — a cache-
                // restore (otaFetch=false) must never REGRESS the persisted
                // floor to an older cached rev.
                val newFloor = maxOf(activeRev, revNow)
                if (newFloor != activeRev) {
                    activeRev = newFloor
                    try {
                        prefs()?.edit()?.putLong(PREF_ACTIVE_REV, newFloor)?.apply()
                    } catch (_: Exception) {}
                }
            }
            // P2-6: ONE activation telemetry record per activation — version,
            // rev, winning source, duration, applied/skipped family entry
            // counts and the delivery-chain per-source roll-up. Content-free
            // (no URLs beyond the well-known chain source labels, no payload
            // fragments). Built here, FLUSHED by the sync path once it knows
            // the winning source (or by init's bundled/cached restore with a
            // blank source). Deduped per version+rev AND capped 1/24h aggregate.
            pendingActivationReport = PendingActivation(
                ver = ver,
                rev = rev,
                durationMs = syncElapsedMs,
                applied = mapOf(
                    "domains" to domains.size,
                    "mirrors" to mirrors.size,
                    "sites" to siteConfigs.size,
                    "resolvers" to resolverConfigs.size,
                    "directMediaExtensions" to mediaExts.size,
                    "hostPolicies" to hostPolicies.size,
                    "urlTemplates" to urlTemplates.size,
                    "knownDead" to knownDead.size,
                    "lockerHosts" to lockerHosts.size,
                    "searchStrategies" to searchStrategies.size,
                    "pipelines" to pipelines.size,
                    "pipelines_shadow_armed" to pipelinesShadowArmed,
                    "dynamic_providers" to dynProviders.size,
                    "disabled_sites" to contentPolicy.disabledSites.size,
                    "downloader_routing" to newSnapshot.routes.size,
                    "engine_profiles" to (newSnapshot.ytdlpProfiles.size + newSnapshot.aria2Profiles.size),
                    "proxy_unwrappers" to newSnapshot.unwrappers.size,
                    "resolver_gates" to newSnapshot.resolverExclusions.size,
                    "resolver_crypto" to newSnapshot.cryptoRings.size,
                    "permissive_tls_hosts" to newSnapshot.permissiveTlsHosts.size,
                    "hls_keep_referer_hosts" to newSnapshot.hlsExplicitRefererHosts.size,
                    "streaming_url_markers" to newSnapshot.streamingUrlMarkers.size,
                    "preflight_passthrough_markers" to newSnapshot.preflightPassthroughMarkers.size,
                    "decoy_signatures" to newSnapshot.decoySignatures.size,
                    "failover_clusters" to (if (newSnapshot.failoverClusters != FailoverClusters()) 1 else 0)
                ),
                skippedEntries = skippedPipelines + skippedDynProviders
            )
            // Rules-rev state invalidation (Remote Settings sync-event
            // semantics, §3.7). P2-7 upgrade: with a rev present the drop is
            // DIFF-SCOPED — only hosts whose knownDead/lockerHosts/hostPolicy/
            // pipeline entry changed or was removed get their stale backoff
            // verdict cleared, so a truly-dead host's live backoff survives
            // unrelated updates. Hosts REMOVED from knownDead/lockerHosts are
            // in the changed set by construction (the confirmed
            // "remembers-dead-after-fix" bug). Legacy payloads without a rev
            // cannot be diffed reliably, so they fall back to the existing
            // coarse whole-ledger clearing. Both paths drop only the judgment;
            // ok/fail history and 429 cooldowns stay.
            val prevVer = _version.value
            // NoSourceLedger: new payload may add platforms — hidden titles
            // get re-judged against the new playbook.
            com.anonrode.downloader.pipeline.NoSourceLedger.clear()
            com.anonrode.downloader.providers.ProviderRegistry.clearEpisodeCache()
            _version.value = ver
            if (ver != prevVer || activeRev != prevActiveRev) {
                val revForDiff = rev
                if (revForDiff != null && revForDiff > 0L) {
                    val changedHosts = computeChangedHosts(
                        prevKnownDead, prevLockerHosts, prevHostPolicies, prevPipelines,
                        knownDead, lockerHosts, hostPolicies, pipelines
                    )
                    if (changedHosts.isEmpty()) {
                        com.anonrode.downloader.util.DebugLog.engine(
                            "OTA rules $prevVer -> $ver (rev $revForDiff): no host-policy changes detected — backoff verdicts kept"
                        )
                    } else {
                        val cleared = com.anonrode.downloader.pipeline.HostHealth.clearBackoffsFor(changedHosts)
                        com.anonrode.downloader.util.DebugLog.engine(
                            "OTA rules $prevVer -> $ver (rev $revForDiff): diff cleared $cleared backoff verdict(s) across ${changedHosts.size} changed host target(s)"
                        )
                        if (cleared == 0) {
                            com.anonrode.downloader.util.DebugLog.trace(
                                "OTA rules diff: changed targets [${changedHosts.take(8).joinToString(", ")}]"
                            )
                        }
                    }
                } else {
                    val cleared = com.anonrode.downloader.pipeline.HostHealth.clearBackoffsOnNewRules()
                    if (cleared > 0) {
                        com.anonrode.downloader.util.DebugLog.engine(
                            "OTA rules $prevVer -> $ver (no rev on payload): cleared $cleared stale host backoff verdicts (coarse fallback)"
                        )
                    }
                }
            }
            true
        } catch (_: Exception) {
            false
        }
    }
}
}

package com.anonrode.downloader.data.rules

import android.content.Context
import com.anonrode.downloader.BuildConfig
import org.json.JSONObject
import java.util.UUID

/**
 * Per-family OTA flags + kill switches (Phase 2, plan slice P2-1; prior art:
 * Mozilla Remote Settings bucket/collection split §1.4, AdGuard trust-level
 * gating §1.5, Firebase in-app-defaults floor §1.6).
 *
 * Payload shape (top-level "flags" object; every field optional):
 * ```
 * "flags": {
 *   "<family>": { "enabled": true|false, "percent": 0..100,
 *                 "minApp": 42, "expiresMs": 1770000000000, "shadow": true|false }
 * }
 * ```
 * `<family>` MUST be one of the literal top-level payload keys in
 * [FAMILY_IDS] (the client's parseRulesJson section names). The publish-side
 * validator (encrypt_rules.py) hard-fails unknown families/sub-keys; this
 * client parser enforces the SAME vocabulary LENIENTLY — unknown family key
 * => journal + skip the entry, unknown SUB-key => skip that family's whole
 * flag object (a typo'd flag must never half-apply; AdGuard trust-level
 * lesson). Leniency is the additive-only rule in action: an old client that
 * has never heard of "flags" ignores the object wholesale.
 *
 * Durability follows Firebase's in-app-defaults floor: flags live ONLY
 * inside the payload that carried them. A payload that omits "flags" (or a
 * family) resets that family to [DEFAULT] — no stale-flag limbo, and the
 * compiled fallback is the instant kill switch. Precedence (plan §3.5 /
 * Chromium variations): bundled default < payload flag entry; a future
 * per-device debug override would slot above (none exists tonight).
 *
 * DEFAULT state per family: enabled, percent 100, no minApp, no expiry,
 * shadow off — i.e. zero behavior change for every payload shipped before
 * this schema existed.
 */

/** One family's flag record. Defaults are the safe state (see class doc). */
data class FamilyFlag(
    /** Kill switch: false => the family publishes EMPTY (compiled fallback). */
    val enabled: Boolean = true,
    /** Stable-bucket rollout percent (0..100). percent >= 100 => every device. */
    val percent: Int = 100,
    /** Minimum app VERSION_CODE for this family; 0 = no floor. Below it the
     *  family publishes empty + journal skip (old-browser-on-new-pack). */
    val minAppVersion: Int = 0,
    /** Absolute epoch-ms expiry hint for the family (uBO/Remote-Settings style
     *  staleness metadata). 0 = no expiry. NOTE: advisory-only this rev cycle —
     *  stale-but-functional is the posture (uBO: "functional even when
     *  'expired'"); expired flags journal, they never disable. */
    val expiresMs: Long = 0L,
    /** Shadow-run marker (GitHub Scientist pattern, plan P2-4): the family's
     *  parsed section is held back from the user path (compiled control runs)
     *  while the candidate engine measures it sample-by-sample. */
    val shadow: Boolean = false
) {
    /** True when this device's app build satisfies the family's minApp floor. */
    val minAppSatisfied: Boolean
        get() = minAppVersion <= 0 || minAppVersion <= BuildConfig.VERSION_CODE

    /** True when the flag carries no signals beyond the defaults — kept so a
     *  no-op flag entry can be distinguished from a real rollout decision. */
    val isDefault: Boolean
        get() = this == RulesFlags.DEFAULT
}

object RulesFlags {

    /**
     * The family-id whitelist — the LITERAL top-level payload keys (coordinator
     * correction 2026-10-15; the client variable names in older notes were NOT
     * ids). Publish-side validator accepts exactly this set; unknown ids here
     * are journaled and skipped.
     */
    val FAMILY_IDS: List<String> = listOf(
        "domains",
        "mirrors",
        "sites",
        "resolvers",
        "directMediaExtensions",
        "hostPolicies",
        "urlTemplates",
        "knownDead",
        "lockerHosts",
        "searchStrategies",
        "pipelines",
        "dynamic_providers",
        "contentPolicy",
        // v3.3.0 platform surfaces (plan §4.1) — kept byte-identical to the
        // publish-side list in scripts/encrypt_rules.py (FAMILY_IDS).
        "announcements",
        "update",
        "ads",
        "engagement",
        // v3.4.0 engine decoupling surfaces
        "downloader_routing",
        "engine_profiles",
        "proxy_unwrappers",
        "resolver_gates",
        "resolver_crypto",
        "permissive_tls_hosts",
        "hls_keep_referer_hosts",
        "streaming_url_markers",
        "preflight_passthrough_markers",
        "decoy_signatures",
        "failover_clusters"
    )

    /** Allowed per-family flag sub-keys; anything else voids that family's
     *  flag object (typo hazard — half-applied flags are worse than none). */
    private val ALLOWED_SUB_KEYS = setOf("enabled", "percent", "minApp", "expiresMs", "shadow")

    /** Safe default: family fully on, no gating, no experiment. */
    val DEFAULT = FamilyFlag()

    /** Flags for [family], with [DEFAULT] when the payload carried none — the
     *  Firebase in-app-defaults floor. */
    fun flagFor(family: String, flags: Map<String, FamilyFlag>): FamilyFlag =
        flags[family] ?: DEFAULT

    /**
     * Lenient flags-object parse. Never throws, never fails the payload —
     * problems are reported through [journal] and the offending entry/family
     * is skipped. An absent "flags" object yields an empty map = all defaults.
     *
     * @param flagsObj the payload's optional "flags" object.
     * @param journal receives one human line per noteworthy decision (wired
     *        to DebugLog.engine with the payload version by the caller).
     */
    fun parse(flagsObj: JSONObject?, journal: (String) -> Unit): Map<String, FamilyFlag> {
        if (flagsObj == null) return emptyMap()
        val out = mutableMapOf<String, FamilyFlag>()
        try {
            val keys = flagsObj.keys()
            while (keys.hasNext()) {
                val family = keys.next()
                if (!FAMILY_IDS.contains(family)) {
                    // Unknown family: not a security risk (it can only affect a
                    // table nobody reads) but a fleet-wide-typo indicator —
                    // journal it and move on. Never fatal.
                    journal("flags: unknown family \"$family\" ignored")
                    continue
                }
                val fo = flagsObj.optJSONObject(family)
                if (fo == null) {
                    journal("flags: family \"$family\" ignored (entry is not an object)")
                    continue
                }
                // Unknown SUB-key => the author diverged from the contract this
                // client speaks; skip the WHOLE family's flags so no half-applied
                // decision can hide behind a mistyped partner field.
                var foreignKey: String? = null
                val subKeys = fo.keys()
                while (subKeys.hasNext()) {
                    val k = subKeys.next()
                    if (!ALLOWED_SUB_KEYS.contains(k)) foreignKey = k
                }
                if (foreignKey != null) {
                    journal("flags: family \"$family\" skipped (unknown key \"$foreignKey\")")
                    continue
                }

                val percent = if (fo.has("percent")) fo.optInt("percent", DEFAULT.percent) else DEFAULT.percent
                if (percent !in 0..100) {
                    journal("flags: family \"$family\" skipped (percent $percent outside 0..100)")
                    continue
                }

                val minApp = parseMinApp(fo)
                if (minApp == MIN_APP_INVALID) {
                    journal("flags: family \"$family\" skipped (minApp not a positive integer)")
                    continue
                }

                val expires = if (fo.has("expiresMs")) fo.optLong("expiresMs", 0L) else 0L
                if (expires < 0L) {
                    journal("flags: family \"$family\" skipped (negative expiresMs)")
                    continue
                }

                out[family] = FamilyFlag(
                    enabled = fo.optBoolean("enabled", DEFAULT.enabled),
                    percent = percent,
                    minAppVersion = minApp,
                    expiresMs = expires,
                    shadow = fo.optBoolean("shadow", DEFAULT.shadow)
                )

                // Expiry is advisory-only (stale-but-functional posture, see
                // FamilyFlag.expiresMs): journal loudly, never disable.
                val flag = out.getValue(family)
                if (flag.expiresMs in 1..System.currentTimeMillis()) {
                    journal("flags: family \"$family\" PAST its expiresMs hint (advisory only — family stays active)")
                }
            }
        } catch (t: Exception) {
            // A syntactically hostile flags object must never take the payload
            // down: report what we have (families parsed so far stay valid).
            journal("flags: parse aborted (${t.javaClass.simpleName}) — ${out.size} family flag(s) kept")
        }
        return out
    }

    private const val MIN_APP_INVALID = -1

    /** minApp accepts a JSON number or a numeric string (authoring comfort);
     *  anything else is invalid => whole family flag skipped. 0 = no floor. */
    private fun parseMinApp(fo: JSONObject): Int {
        if (!fo.has("minApp")) return 0
        return when (val v = fo.opt("minApp")) {
            is Number -> {
                val i = v.toInt()
                if (i >= 0 && i.toDouble() == v.toDouble()) i else MIN_APP_INVALID
            }
            is String -> v.trim().toIntOrNull() ?: MIN_APP_INVALID
            else -> MIN_APP_INVALID
        }
    }

    // ------------------------------------------------------------------
    // P2-5 — stable-bucket percent assignment (client half of the ladder)
    // ------------------------------------------------------------------

    private const val PREF_DEVICE_UUID = "pref_ota_device_uuid"

    /**
     * Install-scoped identity for bucket assignment (plan open-question Q2:
     * app-generated; deliberately NOT the Google advertising id — that API
     * does not exist on this device class and is policy-forbidden for this
     * use anyway). Generated once on first use into app-private prefs, so a
     * bucket assignment is sticky across syncs and restarts; it churns only
     * on app-data wipe/reinstall, which the plan accepts as ladder noise.
     * Returns "" when no Context is available (JVM test path) — callers treat
     * that bucket-free case as OUTSIDE every partial rollout (conservative).
     */
    fun installUuid(context: Context?): String {
        val ctx = context ?: return ""
        return try {
            val prefs = ctx.getSharedPreferences("downloader_settings", Context.MODE_PRIVATE)
            prefs.getString(PREF_DEVICE_UUID, null) ?: run {
                val fresh = UUID.randomUUID().toString()
                prefs.edit().putString(PREF_DEVICE_UUID, fresh).apply()
                fresh
            }
        } catch (_: Exception) {
            ""
        }
    }

    /**
     * stableBucket(uuid, family) = SHA-256("uuid/family") mod 100 (first 8
     * digest bytes, big-endian). Pure and deterministic: the SAME device lands
     * in the SAME bucket for a family on every sync/restart — no Scientist
     * per-run rand() flapping between engines mid-task (§3.5's stickiness
     * note). Different families draw independent buckets, so the promotion
     * of one family does not bias another's cohort. Blank uuid (no Context)
     * returns 100 = never inside a partial rollout.
     */
    fun stableBucket(uuid: String, family: String): Int {
        if (uuid.isBlank()) return 100
        return try {
            val md = java.security.MessageDigest.getInstance("SHA-256")
            val digest = md.digest("$uuid/$family".toByteArray(Charsets.UTF_8))
            var acc = 0L
            for (i in 0 until 8) {
                acc = (acc shl 8) or (digest[i].toLong() and 0xFFL)
            }
            // Long math mod 100 (sha256 mod 100 is uniform; guard the sign for
            // the negative half of the unsigned-64 range).
            val mod = (acc % 100L).toInt()
            if (mod < 0) mod + 100 else mod
        } catch (_: Exception) {
            100
        }
    }

    /**
     * The whole per-device activation decision for one family, in precedence
     * order (plan §3.5: bundled default < payload flag; P2-5 ladder):
     *  1. enabled=false  -> false (kill switch, all devices);
     *  2. minApp floor unsatisfied -> false on this build (P2-1);
     *  3. shadow=true    -> false for the USER path (shadow measurement mode,
     *     plan P2-4 — DynamicRulesManager separately arms ShadowRunner);
     *  4. percent>=100   -> true (fully promoted);
     *  5. otherwise      -> true only when stableBucket(uuid, family) < percent
     *     (the sticky 5 -> 25 -> 100 ladder cohort).
     */
    fun isFamilyActiveForDevice(flag: FamilyFlag, family: String, uuid: String): Boolean {
        if (!flag.enabled) return false
        if (!flag.minAppSatisfied) return false
        if (flag.shadow) return false
        if (flag.percent >= 100) return true
        return stableBucket(uuid, family) < flag.percent
    }
}

package com.anonrode.downloader.data.rules

import org.json.JSONArray
import org.json.JSONObject

/**
 * Load-time validation caps for the OTA payload (Phase 2, plan slice P2-3;
 * prior art: Safe Browsing client-requested caps §1.2, AdGuard in-registry
 * validation §1.5, design doc §3.6).
 *
 * The publish-side validator (scripts/encrypt_rules.py — already updated to
 * validate rev + flags and the shared caps) is the HARD gate; this client-side
 * scan runs the SAME caps at load time. This rev cycle the client phase is
 * WARN ONLY (the plan's canary rule): every violation is journaled and counted
 * to the telemetry sink, but a violating payload still activates. Enforcement
 * flips only after field data shows the caps clean for a full payload cycle.
 *
 * Caps, all mirroring existing engine bounds:
 *  - whole decrypted payload <= [MAX_DECRYPTED_BYTES] (2 MB);
 *  - regex PATTERN strings <= [MAX_REGEX_CHARS] — 300, matching the
 *    publish-side MAX (coordinator correction 2026-10-15; Java's Pattern is a
 *    backtracking engine with no complexity guarantee — Rust-regex §1.11 is
 *    the direction, so cap what we cannot prove);
 *  - pipeline steps / per-step sources against PipelineModels' MAX_STEPS (8)
 *    and MAX_SOURCES (4) — the same numbers the executor refuses at parse;
 *  - pipelines family entry count <= [MAX_PIPELINES] (§3.6 example);
 *  - every URL-bearing string field must be a plausible http(s) endpoint —
 *    the remote_logging_url guard generalized to the whole payload (deny
 *    file://, ws://, javascript:, deny junk schemes).
 *
 * WARN-only is itself a safety property: this scan runs inside the activation
 * parse path, so it is bounded work and can NEVER influence the payload's own
 * fate this cycle.
 */
object RuleCaps {

    /** Whole decrypted payload ceiling (UTF-8 bytes) — the Safe Browsing
     *  shape: "caps requested by the client ... protecting memory/bandwidth"
     *  (§1.2). */
    const val MAX_DECRYPTED_BYTES = 2_000_000

    /** Regex PATTERN length cap. 300 = publish-side MAX (coordinator 2026-10-15). */
    const val MAX_REGEX_CHARS = 300

    /** Mirrors PipelineModels' private MAX_STEPS (deliberate restatement: this
     *  file does not edit that one; if the executor ever raises its bound this
     *  scan over-warns, which fails safe). */
    const val MAX_STEPS = 8

    /** Mirrors PipelineModels' private MAX_SOURCES (see the MAX_STEPS note). */
    const val MAX_SOURCES = 4

    /** Pipelines family entry count (design §3.6: "pipelines <= 64 entries"). */
    const val MAX_PIPELINES = 64

    /** Keys whose string value is a regex PATTERN: the bare "regex" of
     *  urlBinds/terminal/seasonFromUrl plus anything ending "Regex"
     *  (stripRegex/hrefRegex/regexText/regexUrl). */
    private const val REGEX_KEY = "regex"
    private const val REGEX_SUFFIX = "Regex"

    /** Absolute-URL probe: any value carrying an explicit scheme must then be
     *  http(s) — the existing remote_logging_url contract generalized to
     *  every URL-bearing field in the payload. */
    private val SCHEMED_URL = Regex("""^[A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9+.\-]*://""")

    /** Walk budgets for one scan: a hostile/buggy payload must not make the
     *  WARN scan itself expensive (it runs on the activation path). */
    private const val MAX_NODES = 20_000
    private const val MAX_DEPTH = 24
    private const val MAX_VIOLATIONS = 32

    /** Per-scan mutable budget (instance-local to the scan call — no shared
     *  state, so concurrent parses can never corrupt each other's accounting). */
    private class Budget {
        var nodes = 0
        var depth = 0
    }

    /**
     * WARN-phase cap scan. Returns human-readable violation descriptions
     * (empty = clean); never throws; bounded work. Envelope size is checked
     * from [jsonStr]; structural caps from the parsed [obj].
     */
    fun scan(jsonStr: String, obj: JSONObject): List<String> {
        val violations = mutableListOf<String>()
        val budget = Budget()
        try {
            val bytes = jsonStr.toByteArray(Charsets.UTF_8).size
            if (bytes > MAX_DECRYPTED_BYTES) {
                violations.add("payload size $bytes > $MAX_DECRYPTED_BYTES bytes")
            }
            walk(obj, "", violations, budget)
            checkPipelines(obj, violations)
        } catch (_: Exception) {
            // The WARN scan itself must never fail an activation.
        }
        return violations.take(MAX_VIOLATIONS)
    }

    /** Payload-family structural caps: pipelines count, steps-per-stage,
     *  sources-per-step — the load-bearing numbers the executor enforces. */
    private fun checkPipelines(obj: JSONObject, out: MutableList<String>) {
        if (out.size >= MAX_VIOLATIONS) return
        val pipelines = obj.optJSONObject("pipelines") ?: return
        val keys = pipelines.keys()
        var count = 0
        while (keys.hasNext()) {
            if (out.size >= MAX_VIOLATIONS) return
            count++
            val site = keys.next()
            val siteObj = pipelines.optJSONObject(site) ?: continue
            for (stage in listOf("search", "episodes", "resolve")) {
                val stageObj = siteObj.optJSONObject(stage) ?: continue
                val steps = stageObj.optJSONArray("steps") ?: continue
                if (steps.length() > MAX_STEPS) {
                    out.add("pipelines/$site/$stage: ${steps.length()} steps > MAX_STEPS($MAX_STEPS)")
                }
                for (i in 0 until steps.length()) {
                    if (out.size >= MAX_VIOLATIONS) return
                    val step = steps.optJSONObject(i) ?: continue
                    val sources = step.optJSONArray("sources") ?: continue
                    if (sources.length() > MAX_SOURCES) {
                        out.add("pipelines/$site/$stage step$i: ${sources.length()} sources > MAX_SOURCES($MAX_SOURCES)")
                    }
                }
            }
        }
        if (count > MAX_PIPELINES) {
            out.add("pipelines: $count entries > expected max $MAX_PIPELINES")
        }
    }

    /** Recursive value walk: regex-pattern length + URL-scheme shape over
     *  every string field. Bounded by [MAX_NODES]/[MAX_DEPTH]. */
    private fun walk(node: Any?, path: String, out: MutableList<String>, b: Budget) {
        if (out.size >= MAX_VIOLATIONS || b.nodes >= MAX_NODES) return
        b.nodes++
        when (node) {
            is JSONObject -> {
                if (b.depth >= MAX_DEPTH) return
                val keys = node.keys()
                while (keys.hasNext()) {
                    if (out.size >= MAX_VIOLATIONS || b.nodes >= MAX_NODES) return
                    val k = keys.next()
                    val child = node.opt(k)
                    if (child is String) {
                        checkString(k, child, path, out)
                    } else {
                        b.depth++
                        walk(child, if (path.isEmpty()) k else "$path.$k", out, b)
                        b.depth--
                    }
                }
            }
            is JSONArray -> {
                if (b.depth >= MAX_DEPTH) return
                for (i in 0 until node.length()) {
                    if (out.size >= MAX_VIOLATIONS || b.nodes >= MAX_NODES) return
                    val child = node.opt(i)
                    if (child is String) {
                        checkString("", child, "$path[$i]", out)
                    } else {
                        b.depth++
                        walk(child, "$path[$i]", out, b)
                        b.depth--
                    }
                }
            }
        }
    }

    /** One field check: regex-pattern length, then URL-scheme shape. */
    private fun checkString(key: String, value: String, path: String, out: MutableList<String>) {
        if (out.size >= MAX_VIOLATIONS) return
        val isRegex = key == REGEX_KEY || key.endsWith(REGEX_SUFFIX) ||
            (key == "pattern" && (path.startsWith("downloader_routing") || path.startsWith("proxy_unwrappers")))
        if (isRegex && value.length > MAX_REGEX_CHARS) {
            out.add("$path/$key: regex pattern ${value.length} chars > $MAX_REGEX_CHARS")
            return
        }
        if (SCHEMED_URL.containsMatchIn(value) &&
            !value.startsWith("http://") &&
            !value.startsWith("https://")
        ) {
            // Endpoint-shape guard (the remote_logging_url contract applied to
            // every URL-bearing field): non-http(s) schemes are unreviewed
            // attack surface (file://, ws://, javascript:) — this cycle WARN.
            out.add("$path/$key: absolute URL not http(s) ('${value.take(24)}…')")
        }
    }
}

/**
 * Normalize a packed episode number into (season, episode), or null when it
 * is NOT packed. The single source of truth is util.SeasonEpisode: 1000-base
 * values are unambiguous on every site; the historical 100-base decode applies
 * only to sites that actually used it (9jaRocks is flat — 113 is S01E113, not
 * S01E13 — and the codec deliberately excludes it).
 */
internal fun normalizeSeasonEncodedEpisodeNumber(site: String, episodeNum: Int): Pair<Int, Int>? {
    if (episodeNum < 100) return null
    val pair = com.anonrode.downloader.util.SeasonEpisode.of(site, 0, 0, episodeNum)
    // Flat numbering comes back unchanged (S1, same episode) — not packed.
    if (pair.second == episodeNum) return null
    if (pair.first !in 1..30 || pair.second !in 1..999) return null
    // site is part of the contract for logging/telemetry call sites.
    if (site.length > 512) return null
    return pair
}

/**
 * Pure HLS playlist transformations + plan fingerprint (JVM-testable).
 *
 * Live-by-default policy (2026-10-19): a playlist whose URIs are ordinary
 * relative paths is fed to yt-dlp as the LIVE URL. Only a scheme-relative
 * `//host/...` URI (yt-dlp joins it to http:// port 80) or an explicitly
 * approved http->https upgrade forces a local rewritten copy. When a local
 * copy IS needed, every relative URI in it must be absolutized or it would
 * resolve against file://.
 */
internal object HlsPlaylist {

    private val URI_VALUE = Pattern.compile("URI=\"([^\"]+)\"")

    private val IV_ATTRIBUTE = Regex("""(?:^|,)\s*IV=0x[0-9A-Fa-f]+""")

    fun resolveSegmentUrl(base: String, uri: String): String? {
        if (uri.startsWith("http://") || uri.startsWith("https://")) return uri
        if (uri.startsWith("//")) return "https:$uri"
        return try {
            val b = java.net.URI(base)
            val qIdx = uri.indexOf('?')
            val pathPart = if (qIdx >= 0) uri.substring(0, qIdx) else uri
            val queryPart = if (qIdx >= 0) uri.substring(qIdx + 1) else null
            val joined = if (pathPart.startsWith("/")) {
                pathPart
            } else {
                b.path.substringBeforeLast('/') + "/" + pathPart
            }
            java.net.URI(b.scheme, null, b.host, b.port, joined, queryPart, null).toString()
        } catch (_: Exception) {
            null
        }
    }

    /** True when the playlist contains a URI that a local rewrite must fix. */
    fun needsLocalRewrite(playlist: String, upgradeInsecureHttp: Boolean): Boolean {
        for (raw in playlist.lineSequence()) {
            val line = raw.trim()
            if (line.startsWith("//")) return true
            if (upgradeInsecureHttp && line.startsWith("http://")) return true
            if (line.startsWith("#")) {
                val m = URI_VALUE.matcher(line)
                while (m.find()) {
                    val u = m.group(1) ?: ""
                    if (u.startsWith("//") || (upgradeInsecureHttp && u.startsWith("http://"))) return true
                }
            }
        }
        return false
    }

    /** Rewritten playlist text, or null when the LIVE URL is safe to use. */
    fun rewrite(
        playlist: String,
        baseUrl: String,
        upgradeInsecureHttp: Boolean,
        forceLocal: Boolean = false
    ): String? {
        if (!forceLocal && !needsLocalRewrite(playlist, upgradeInsecureHttp)) return null
        val sb = StringBuilder()
        for (rawLine in playlist.lineSequence()) {
            val line = rawLine.trimEnd('\r')
            when {
                line.startsWith("//") -> sb.append("https:").append(line).append('\n')
                line.startsWith("#") -> {
                    var l = line
                    val m = URI_VALUE.matcher(l)
                    if (m.find()) {
                        val out = StringBuffer()
                        do {
                            val u = m.group(1) ?: ""
                            val repl = when {
                                u.startsWith("//") -> "https:$u"
                                u.startsWith("http://") && upgradeInsecureHttp ->
                                    "https://" + u.removePrefix("http://")
                                u.startsWith("http://") || u.startsWith("https://") -> u
                                else -> maybeUpgrade(resolveSegmentUrl(baseUrl, u) ?: u, upgradeInsecureHttp)
                            }
                            m.appendReplacement(out, "URI=\"" + Matcher.quoteReplacement(repl) + "\"")
                        } while (m.find())
                        m.appendTail(out)
                        l = out.toString()
                    }
                    sb.append(l).append('\n')
                }
                else -> {
                    // A local master is consumed from file://, so every
                    // relative URI must become absolute (http is upgraded
                    // only when the caller proved https works).
                    val resolved = when {
                        line.startsWith("http://") -> maybeUpgrade(line, upgradeInsecureHttp)
                        else -> maybeUpgrade(resolveSegmentUrl(baseUrl, line) ?: line, upgradeInsecureHttp)
                    }
                    sb.append(resolved).append('\n')
                }
            }
        }
        return sb.toString()
    }

    /**
     * Structural plan fingerprint. Token/query rotation must NOT change it;
     * a changed segment sequence, duration, key, map, rendition or variant
     * set MUST. Hashed fields:
     *  - segment/URI basenames (query and tokenized path prefixes dropped)
     *  - #EXTINF durations, #EXT-X-BYTERANGE, discontinuity/media-sequence
     *  - RESOLUTION/BANDWIDTH-bearing tags, key method, map/media type
     * IV values are ignored: they may rotate per session without changing the
     * decrypted byte plan.
     */
    fun fingerprint(playlists: List<String>): String {
        // Live media playlists have a sliding window: MEDIA-SEQUENCE and the
        // segment set legitimately change on every fetch. Mark them
        // indeterminate so the caller never purges banked bytes.
        val hasLiveMedia = playlists.any { p ->
            val lines = p.lineSequence().map { it.trim() }.toList()
            lines.isNotEmpty() &&
                lines.none { it.startsWith("#EXT-X-STREAM-INF") } &&
                lines.none { it.startsWith("#EXT-X-ENDLIST") }
        }
        if (hasLiveMedia) return "live"
        val md = MessageDigest.getInstance("SHA-256")
        for (playlist in playlists) {
            for (raw in playlist.lineSequence()) {
                val line = raw.trim()
                if (line.isEmpty()) continue
                val normalized: String? = when {
                    line.startsWith("#EXTINF") ->
                        "EXTINF:" + line.substringAfter(':', "").substringBefore(',')
                    line.startsWith("#EXT-X-KEY") ||
                        line.startsWith("#EXT-X-MAP") ||
                        line.startsWith("#EXT-X-MEDIA") ||
                        line.startsWith("#EXT-X-STREAM-INF") -> normalizeTagLine(line)
                    line.startsWith("#EXT-X-BYTERANGE") ||
                        line.startsWith("#EXT-X-DISCONTINUITY") ||
                        line.startsWith("#EXT-X-TARGETDURATION") ||
                        line.startsWith("#EXT-X-MEDIA-SEQUENCE") ||
                        line.startsWith("#EXT-X-PLAYLIST-TYPE") ||
                        line.startsWith("#EXT-X-ENDLIST") -> line
                    line.startsWith("#") -> null
                    else -> "URI:" + uriBasename(line)
                }
                if (normalized != null) {
                    md.update(normalized.toByteArray(Charsets.UTF_8))
                    md.update('\n'.code.toByte())
                }
            }
        }
        return md.digest().joinToString("") { "%02x".format(it) }
    }

    private fun maybeUpgrade(url: String, upgradeInsecureHttp: Boolean): String =
        if (upgradeInsecureHttp && url.startsWith("http://")) {
            "https://" + url.removePrefix("http://")
        } else url

    private fun uriBasename(uri: String): String =
        uri.substringBefore('?').substringBefore('#').substringAfterLast('/')

    private fun normalizeTagLine(line: String): String {
        val cleaned = line.replace(IV_ATTRIBUTE, "")
        val m = URI_VALUE.matcher(cleaned)
        val out = StringBuffer()
        while (m.find()) {
            val u = m.group(1) ?: ""
            m.appendReplacement(out, "URI=\"" + Matcher.quoteReplacement(uriBasename(u)) + "\"")
        }
        m.appendTail(out)
        return out.toString().replace(Regex("\\s+"), " ").trim()
    }
}

/**
 * Subtitle artifact extensions and the player-facing alignment (2026-10-21).
 *
 * Two different sets, deliberately:
 *  - [PLAYER_SIDECAR_EXTS] is exactly what the player discovers/renders
 *    (`<stem>.<lang>.srt|vtt|ass|ssa`; MediaPlayerModal's sidecar scan).
 *  - [RENAMED_ARTIFACT_EXTS] also carries the timed-text formats yt-dlp can
 *    leave behind (ttml/json3/srv3). They are subtitle artifacts — never the
 *    media file — but the player cannot render them.
 *
 * The engine therefore NEVER exposes an exotic format as a sidecar in the
 * media folder: [alignForPlayer] converts ttml/json3/srv3 to SRT first, and
 * a body it cannot parse is skipped with an explicit log instead of being
 * renamed into a folder where discovery would silently ignore it. This is
 * the engine half of the alignment; no player-side extension list change is
 * needed because unsupported formats never reach the shared folder.
 */
internal object SubtitleArtifacts {

    val PLAYER_SIDECAR_EXTS = setOf("srt", "vtt", "ass", "ssa")
    val EXOTIC_TIMED_TEXT_EXTS = setOf("ttml", "json3", "srv3")
    val RENAMED_ARTIFACT_EXTS = PLAYER_SIDECAR_EXTS + EXOTIC_TIMED_TEXT_EXTS

    data class AlignedSidecar(val extension: String, val body: String)

    /**
     * Returns the body+extension to write into the media folder, or null when
     * [extension] is an unknown / unparseable format. Native player formats
     * pass through (ssa is normalized to ass); exotic formats are converted
     * to SRT.
     */
    fun alignForPlayer(body: String, extension: String): AlignedSidecar? {
        val ext = extension.trim().lowercase().removePrefix(".")
        if (ext in PLAYER_SIDECAR_EXTS) {
            return AlignedSidecar(if (ext == "ssa") "ass" else ext, body)
        }
        val srt = when (ext) {
            "json3" -> json3ToSrt(body)
            "ttml" -> xmlTimedTextToSrt(body, tag = "p")
            "srv3" -> xmlTimedTextToSrt(body, tag = "text")
            else -> null
        } ?: return null
        return AlignedSidecar("srt", srt)
    }

    /** True when the body looks like one of the exotic timed-text formats
     *  (used to avoid labelling an XML/JSON subtitle as SRT). */
    fun sniffExotic(body: String): String? {
        val head = body.take(8192)
        return when {
            head.contains("\"tStartMs\"") && head.contains("\"segs\"") -> "json3"
            head.contains("<text ", ignoreCase = true) &&
                head.contains("start=", ignoreCase = true) -> "srv3"
            (head.contains("<tt", ignoreCase = true) || head.contains(":tt", ignoreCase = true)) &&
                head.contains("<p", ignoreCase = true) -> "ttml"
            else -> null
        }
    }

    private data class Cue(val startMs: Long, val endMs: Long, val text: String)

    private fun json3ToSrt(body: String): String? {
        if (!body.contains("tStartMs")) return null
        // yt-dlp/YouTube json3 events are flat objects carrying tStartMs,
        // dDurationMs and a segs array. Field order is stable in practice;
        // the regex tolerates other keys between them.
        val event = Regex(
            """\{[^{}]*?"tStartMs"\s*:\s*(-?\d+)[^{}]*?"dDurationMs"\s*:\s*(\d+)[^{}]*?"segs"\s*:\s*\[(.*?)]""",
            RegexOption.DOT_MATCHES_ALL
        )
        val jsonString = Regex("\"utf8\"\\s*:\\s*\"((?:[^\"\\\\]|\\\\.)*)\"")
        val cues = event.findAll(body).mapNotNull { m ->
            val start = m.groupValues[1].toLongOrNull() ?: return@mapNotNull null
            val dur = m.groupValues[2].toLongOrNull() ?: 0L
            val text = jsonString.findAll(m.groupValues[3])
                .joinToString("") { unescapeJson(it.groupValues[1]) }
                .replace(Regex("\\s+"), " ")
                .trim()
            if (text.isBlank()) null else Cue(start, start + maxOf(dur, 500L), text)
        }.toList()
        return renderSrt(cues)
    }

    private fun xmlTimedTextToSrt(body: String, tag: String): String? {
        val block = Regex("(?s)<" + tag + "\\b([^>]*)>(.*?)</" + tag + ">")
        val cues = block.findAll(body).mapNotNull { m ->
            val attrs = m.groupValues[1]
            val text = cleanXmlText(m.groupValues[2])
            if (text.isBlank()) return@mapNotNull null
            val startRaw = attrValue(attrs, "begin") ?: attrValue(attrs, "start") ?: return@mapNotNull null
            val start = parseTimeMs(startRaw) ?: return@mapNotNull null
            val end = parseTimeMs(attrValue(attrs, "end") ?: "")
                ?: parseTimeMs(attrValue(attrs, "dur") ?: "")?.let { start + it }
                ?: (start + 2_000L)
            Cue(start, maxOf(end, start + 250L), text)
        }.toList()
        return renderSrt(cues)
    }

    private fun attrValue(attrs: String, name: String): String? =
        Regex("\\b" + name + "\\s*=\\s*\"([^\"]*)\"").find(attrs)?.groupValues?.get(1)

    /** TTML clock ("hh:mm:ss.mmm", "hh:mm:ss:ff") or seconds ("1.5", "1.5s",
     *  "1500ms") to epoch-free milliseconds. */
    private fun parseTimeMs(raw: String): Long? {
        var v = raw.trim()
        if (v.isEmpty()) return null
        if (v.endsWith("ms", ignoreCase = true)) {
            return v.dropLast(2).toDoubleOrNull()?.let { Math.round(it) }
        }
        if (v.endsWith("s", ignoreCase = true)) v = v.dropLast(1)
        if (v.contains(':')) {
            val parts = v.split(':')
            if (parts.size < 3) return null
            val h = parts[0].toLongOrNull() ?: return null
            val m = parts[1].toLongOrNull() ?: return null
            val secPart = parts[2]
            val sec = secPart.toDoubleOrNull() ?: return null
            var ms = ((h * 60 + m) * 60) * 1000L + Math.round(sec * 1000.0)
            if (parts.size >= 4) {
                val frames = parts[3].toLongOrNull() ?: 0L
                ms += Math.round(frames * 1000.0 / 30.0)
            }
            return ms
        }
        return v.toDoubleOrNull()?.let { Math.round(it * 1000.0) }
    }

    private fun cleanXmlText(raw: String): String {
        val withBreaks = raw.replace(Regex("(?i)<br\\s*/?>"), "\n")
        val noTags = withBreaks.replace(Regex("<[^>]+>"), "")
        return decodeEntities(noTags).trim()
    }

    private fun decodeEntities(raw: String): String {
        var out = raw
            .replace("&nbsp;", " ")
            .replace("&lt;", "<")
            .replace("&gt;", ">")
            .replace("&quot;", "\"")
            .replace("&apos;", "'")
            .replace("&#39;", "'")
            .replace("&amp;", "&")
        out = Regex("&#(\\d+);").replace(out) { m ->
            m.groupValues[1].toIntOrNull()?.let { String(Character.toChars(it)) } ?: m.value
        }
        out = Regex("&#x([0-9A-Fa-f]+);").replace(out) { m ->
            m.groupValues[1].toIntOrNull(16)?.let { String(Character.toChars(it)) } ?: m.value
        }
        return out
    }

    private fun unescapeJson(raw: String): String {
        val sb = StringBuilder(raw.length)
        var i = 0
        while (i < raw.length) {
            val c = raw[i]
            if (c != '\\' || i + 1 >= raw.length) {
                sb.append(c)
                i++
                continue
            }
            when (val n = raw[i + 1]) {
                'n' -> sb.append('\n')
                'r' -> sb.append('\r')
                't' -> sb.append('\t')
                'b' -> sb.append('\b')
                'f' -> sb.append('\u000C')
                '"' -> sb.append('"')
                '\\' -> sb.append('\\')
                '/' -> sb.append('/')
                'u' -> {
                    if (i + 5 < raw.length) {
                        val hex = raw.substring(i + 2, i + 6)
                        val code = hex.toIntOrNull(16)
                        if (code != null) {
                            sb.append(code.toChar())
                            i += 6
                            continue
                        }
                    }
                    sb.append(n)
                }
                else -> sb.append(n)
            }
            i += 2
        }
        return sb.toString()
    }

    private fun renderSrt(cues: List<Cue>): String? {
        val usable = cues.filter { it.text.isNotBlank() && it.endMs > it.startMs }.sortedBy { it.startMs }
        if (usable.isEmpty()) return null
        val sb = StringBuilder()
        usable.forEachIndexed { index, cue ->
            sb.append(index + 1).append('\n')
            sb.append(srtTime(cue.startMs)).append(" --> ").append(srtTime(cue.endMs)).append('\n')
            sb.append(cue.text).append("\n\n")
        }
        return sb.toString()
    }

    private fun srtTime(ms: Long): String {
        val safe = ms.coerceAtLeast(0L)
        val h = safe / 3_600_000L
        val m = (safe % 3_600_000L) / 60_000L
        val s = (safe % 60_000L) / 1000L
        val milli = safe % 1000L
        return String.format(java.util.Locale.US, "%02d:%02d:%02d,%03d", h, m, s, milli)
    }
}

class DownloadEngine(
    private val context: Context,
    private val repository: DownloadRepository,
    private val networkObserver: NetworkObserver = NetworkObserver(context)
) {
    private val ASIAN_DRAMA_CLUSTER: Set<String>
        get() = com.anonrode.downloader.data.rules.DynamicRulesManager.getFailoverClusters().asianCluster
    private val WESTERN_CLUSTER: Set<String>
        get() = com.anonrode.downloader.data.rules.DynamicRulesManager.getFailoverClusters().westernCluster
    private val DEDICATED_ASIAN_SITES: Set<String>
        get() = com.anonrode.downloader.data.rules.DynamicRulesManager.getFailoverClusters().dedicatedAsian
    // Secondary Asian-failover targets: mixed Western-cluster sites with PROVEN
    // Asian catalogs (coverage probe 2026-09-20: 50 random Asian series,
    // search-only — 9jarocks 98%, nkiri 62%, and a 6/6 rescue rate on titles
    // ALL dedicated sites missed). Reached ONLY by Asian tasks, and tried at
    // EQUAL RANK with Asian-cluster cards: exact title match + HostHealth
    // decide (deliberate choice — no secondary-tier penalty). Western tasks
    // never touch the dedicated sites; that one-way door stays shut.
    private val SECONDARY_ASIAN_FALLBACK: Set<String>
        get() = com.anonrode.downloader.data.rules.DynamicRulesManager.getFailoverClusters().secondaryAsianFallback
    private val YEAR_REGEX = Regex("""\b(19\d\d|20[0-3]\d)\b""")

    private val engineScope = CoroutineScope(Dispatchers.IO + SupervisorJob())
    private val runtimeRegistry = TaskRuntimeRegistry()

    /**
     * Per-task backend failure tracker (progress-banking guard correction,
     * 2026-10-20). A task with banked bytes used to veto failover forever,
     * which parked f8cf38d2 at 1,669 KiB against a URL class that could never
     * progress (the nsrplay self-loop). Failover is now allowed when the
     * SAME terminal URL has burned a full backend ladder (>=3 failures) and
     * the task's banked bytes belong to that URL — the corruption protection
     * stays for a partial that is making progress; the dead-end escape opens
     * only for a proven-unprogressable source.
     */
    private data class BackendFailures(val url: String, val count: Int, val lastAtMs: Long)
    private val backendFailures = java.util.concurrent.ConcurrentHashMap<String, BackendFailures>()

    private fun noteBackendFailure(task: DownloadTask, failedUrl: String) {
        if (failedUrl.isBlank()) return
        val now = System.currentTimeMillis()
        backendFailures.compute(task.id) { _, old ->
            if (old != null && old.url == failedUrl) old.copy(count = old.count + 1, lastAtMs = now)
            else BackendFailures(failedUrl, 1, now)
        }
    }

    private fun clearBackendFailures(taskId: String) {
        backendFailures.remove(taskId)
    }

    /** True when the task's banked bytes belong to a URL that exhausted at
     *  least one full backend ladder (or is already poisoned as a decoy). */
    private fun bankedSourceUnprogressable(task: DownloadTask): Boolean {
        val current = task.directUrl.trim()
        if (current.isNotBlank() && com.anonrode.downloader.pipeline.ResolveCache.isPoisoned(current)) return true
        val failures = backendFailures[task.id] ?: return false
        if (failures.count < 3) return false
        return failures.url == current || current.isBlank()
    }

    /**
     * Same-show duplicate-terminal guard (Servamp S01E01 == S01E02,
     * 2026-10-20). Two DIFFERENT episodes of one show must never download the
     * SAME direct terminal. The comparison is host+path (query/signature
     * dropped: a CDN signs per request), and only for provable media/HLS
     * URLs. Returns the conflicting task, or null.
     */
    internal fun findDuplicateTerminal(task: DownloadTask, resolvedUrl: String): DownloadTask? {
        if (resolvedUrl.isBlank()) return null
        val classifier = com.anonrode.downloader.pipeline.UrlClassifier
        val looksTerminal = isDirectMediaUrl(resolvedUrl) || isProvablyDirectFile(resolvedUrl) ||
            classifier.isManifestShaped(resolvedUrl)
        if (!looksTerminal) return null
        val target = classifier.canonicalMediaPath(resolvedUrl) ?: return null
        val mine = com.anonrode.downloader.util.SeasonEpisode.of(task)
        return repository.snapshot().firstOrNull { other ->
            if (other.id == task.id) return@firstOrNull false
            if (other.status == TaskStatus.FAILED) return@firstOrNull false
            if (!other.showTitle.equals(task.showTitle, ignoreCase = true)) return@firstOrNull false
            if (other.directUrl.isBlank()) return@firstOrNull false
            val otherPath = classifier.canonicalMediaPath(other.directUrl) ?: return@firstOrNull false
            if (otherPath != target) return@firstOrNull false
            val theirs = com.anonrode.downloader.util.SeasonEpisode.of(other)
            theirs != mine
        }
    }

    private val progressWatchdog by lazy {
        ProgressWatchdog(
            repository = repository,
            computeVerifiedDiskBytes = { t -> computeDiskBytes(t) },
            onStallKill = { taskId, kills, exhausted, stallMsg, t ->
                handleWatchdogStall(taskId, kills, exhausted, stallMsg, t)
            }
        )
    }

    @Volatile var maxConcurrentDownloads: Int = 4
    @Volatile var parallelSocketsPerFile: Int = 16
    @Volatile var defaultQuality: String = "720p"
    @Volatile var autoOrganizeByShow: Boolean = true
    @Volatile var instantSocialDownload: Boolean = false
    @Volatile var wifiOnlyTorrents: Boolean = false
    var downloadTorrentsWifiOnly: Boolean
        get() = wifiOnlyTorrents
        set(value) { wifiOnlyTorrents = value }
    @Volatile var showPostersInResults: Boolean = true
    @Volatile var storageGuardGb: Double = 1.0

    // Tier-A settings (AppSettings-backed): defaults equal the previous
    // hardcoded behavior, so nothing changes until the user opts in.
    @Volatile var stallTimeoutSec: Int = 60
    @Volatile var magnetMaxAttempts: Int = 3
    @Volatile var ytdlpMaxAttempts: Int = 3
    @Volatile var hlsFragmentConcurrency: Int = 16
    @Volatile var globalSpeedLimitKbs: Int = 0          // 0 = unlimited
    @Volatile var torrentPeers: Int = -1                // -1 = auto (RAM tier)
    @Volatile var torrentPrivacyMode: Boolean = false   // qBittorrent anonymous-mode lessons
    @Volatile var wifiOnlyAll: Boolean = false
    @Volatile var clipboardDetect: Boolean = true
    @Volatile var completionNotifications: Boolean = true
    @Volatile var debugLogging: Boolean = false
    @Volatile var logRetentionDays: Int = 7
    // Seal-parity subtitle settings (2026-09-14): yt-dlp extractor downloads
    // fetch subtitles in this language (default English) and embed them in
    // the merged file. Both live in downloader_settings like the rest.
    @Volatile var downloadSubtitles: Boolean = true
    @Volatile var subtitleLanguage: String = "en"
    @Volatile var filterExplicitContent: Boolean = true


    // No byte movement (parsed progress or filesystem bytes) for this long while
    // DOWNLOADING means the backend is hung; the watchdog kills it so the retry
    // wrapper can relaunch, and the task eventually FAILED instead of hanging.
    private val STALL_TIMEOUT_MS: Long
        get() = stallTimeoutSec * 1000L

    /**
     * Set by the UI: called when a torrent's swarm exposes more than one safe
     * file (season packs). Receives the shield-checked file list and must
     * return the selected 1-based aria2c indexes, or null to download the
     * whole torrent. Runs on the engine's IO dispatcher — the UI should
     * bridge it to the main thread (e.g. a Compose dialog).
     */
    var onTorrentFileSelection: (suspend (List<TorrentSecurityShield.TorrentFileEntry>) -> com.anonrode.downloader.ui.screens.TorrentFilePicker.TorrentPickResult)? = null

    val tasks: StateFlow<List<DownloadTask>> = repository.tasks

    init {
        loadPreferences()
        // Global concurrency controller: every ~5s water-fill the 24-lane
        // budget from measured per-task throughput. Turbo applies a new
        // grant at its next piece claim (boundary, never mid-piece); HLS
        // grants are fixed for the run.
        engineScope.launch {
            while (isActive) {
                delay(5_000L)
                com.anonrode.downloader.pipeline.HostPolicyRegistry.LaneBudget.rebalance()
                    .forEach { com.anonrode.downloader.util.DebugLog.engine(it) }
            }
        }
        engineScope.launch {
            // OWNER DIRECTIVE 2026-10-21 ("every error ends in a download"):
            // tasks interrupted by app kill/crash requeue automatically. The
            // repository restore (initPersistence) already mapped mid-flight
            // statuses to a system network pause before the engine was built,
            // so this is defense in depth for any future init reordering —
            // but now it parks as a SYSTEM pause (userPaused=false, network
            // marker) instead of a stranded manual pause, and every restored
            // task gets a one-shot RESTORED_REQUEUE_FLOOR_MS backoff below so
            // boot never silently drains data on open (v3.0.4) while still
            // guaranteeing the retry (the observer's requeue sweep honors the
            // floor). A caught-mid-VALIDATING task re-validates in seconds.
            val restoredFloor = System.currentTimeMillis() + RESTORED_REQUEUE_FLOOR_MS
            val currentTasks = repository.tasks.value
            currentTasks.forEach { t ->
                // QUEUED included: the repository restore parks it too, but a
                // task persisted as QUEUED between enqueue and restore (async
                // persist race) must not reach the network observer below,
                // whose first emission auto-starts every QUEUED task the
                // moment the app opens.
                if (t.status == TaskStatus.DOWNLOADING || t.status == TaskStatus.RESOLVING ||
                    t.status == TaskStatus.VALIDATING || t.status == TaskStatus.QUEUED) {
                    repository.update(t.id) { cur ->
                        if (cur.status != TaskStatus.DOWNLOADING && cur.status != TaskStatus.RESOLVING &&
                            cur.status != TaskStatus.VALIDATING && cur.status != TaskStatus.QUEUED
                        ) cur
                        else cur.copy(
                            status = TaskStatus.PAUSED,
                            speedBytesPerSec = 0.0,
                            errorMessage = NETWORK_PAUSE_MESSAGE,
                            userPaused = false
                        )
                    }
                }
                runtimeRegistry.getOrCreate(t.id).requeueNotBeforeMs.compareAndSet(0L, restoredFloor)
            }
            networkObserver.status.collect { net ->
                if (net.isConnected) {
                    if (lastNetworkTag != null && net.networkTag != null && lastNetworkTag != net.networkTag) {
                        // Network identity changed while still connected (Wi-Fi -> mobile, VPN toggle):
                        // restart active jobs losslessly on the new network instead of letting
                        // their sockets stall against the dead one.
                        runtimeRegistry.activeRunningTaskIds().forEach { id -> pauseForNetwork(id) }
                    }
                    lastNetworkTag = net.networkTag
                    requeueNetworkParkedTasks(isWifi = net.isWifi)
                    processQueue()
                } else {
                    // Park active jobs so a reconnect resumes them instead of failing them
                    lastNetworkTag = null
                    runtimeRegistry.activeRunningTaskIds().forEach { id -> pauseForNetwork(id) }
                }
            }
        }
        // Boot-retry pass (owner directive 2026-10-21): the observer above
        // emits on network CHANGES, so a floor-stamped restored task could
        // otherwise sit the entire session behind its 60s boot floor on a
        // stable network. One delayed pass replays the requeue sweep exactly
        // like a reconnect; only the restored tasks' one-shot boot floor (and
        // any live escalation floor) still gates the outcome.
        engineScope.launch {
            delay(RESTORED_REQUEUE_FLOOR_MS + 250L)
            val net = networkObserver.status.value
            if (net.isConnected) {
                requeueNetworkParkedTasks(isWifi = net.isWifi)
                processQueue()
            }
        }
        // Storage-guard self-heal: tasks parked by the storage limit have no
        // natural resume trigger (the network collector only matches network
        // messages), so a separate loop re-checks periodically and re-queues
        // them when space frees up instead of leaving the queue stuck until
        // manual resume. Runs in its own coroutine — the collector above never
        // returns, so this must not be sequenced after it.
        engineScope.launch {
            while (true) {
                delay(10_000)
                if (!checkStorageAvailable()) continue
                val parked = repository.tasks.value.filter {
                    it.status == TaskStatus.PAUSED && !it.userPaused && it.errorMessage?.startsWith("Storage limit reached") == true
                }
                if (parked.isNotEmpty()) {
                    parked.forEach { repository.update(it.id) { t ->
                        if (t.userPaused || t.status != TaskStatus.PAUSED) t
                        else t.copy(status = TaskStatus.QUEUED, errorMessage = null)
                    } }
                    processQueue()
                }
            }
        }
        // Cooldown-parked auto-retry: a task parked because its locker host
        // is in HostHealth backoff re-queues itself once the host recovers —
        // nothing else resumes it (the network collector only matches network
        // messages). Restore-safe: parkForRestore keeps the marker and
        // userPaused=false for system parks, so a restart re-enters this loop
        // cleanly (pre-fix, restore crushed these to stranded manual pauses).
        //
        // OWNER DIRECTIVE 2026-10-21 ("every error ends in a download or a
        // proven no-source"): the old PARKED_LIFETIME_MS give-up that wrote
        // FAILED for 0-byte tasks is REMOVED — a parked download re-checks on
        // PARKED_RECHECK_FLOOR_MS cadence until the host returns. FAILED is
        // reserved for the proven no-source verdict (failover exhausted every
        // provider; NoSourceLedger), and manual retry always restarts cleanly.
        // Banked-byte tasks were already exempt from the cap and stay exempt.
        //
        // Trickle requeue: when MANY tasks are parked on the same host, requeue
        // at most a few per tick. Releasing all 18 at once recreates the exact
        // request storm that triggered the backoff in the first place.
        engineScope.launch {
            while (true) {
                delay(10_000)
                val parked = repository.tasks.value.filter {
                    it.status == TaskStatus.PAUSED && !it.userPaused && it.errorMessage?.startsWith(PARKED_HOST_MESSAGE) == true
                }
                if (parked.isEmpty()) continue
                var requeued = 0
                var anyRequeued = false
                parked.forEach { t ->
                    val entry = runtimeRegistry.get(t.id)
                    val parkedAt = entry?.firstParkedAtMs?.get() ?: 0L
                    val now = System.currentTimeMillis()
                    val floor = entry?.requeueNotBeforeMs?.get() ?: 0L
                    val banked = maxOf(t.downloadedBytes, computeDiskBytes(t))
                    val longDead = parkedAt > 0L && now - parkedAt > PARKED_LIFETIME_MS && banked == 0L
                    val hostUsable = com.anonrode.downloader.pipeline.HostHealth.isUsable(
                        t.directUrl.ifBlank { t.selectedMirrorUrl }.ifBlank { t.sourceUrl }
                    )
                    // OWNER DIRECTIVE 2026-10-21 ("every error ends in a
                    // download or a proven no-source"): a park NEVER fails the
                    // task and never strands it. The old 30-minute give-up
                    // wrote FAILED for 0-byte tasks — under the invariant that
                    // end state is illegal unless the title is PROVEN
                    // no-source, which only the failover-exhausted
                    // NoSourceLedger path may claim. A long-dead host instead
                    // re-checks on a long floor while HostHealth stays steep;
                    // the moment the host is usable again the requeue below
                    // fires regardless of that floor.
                    if (longDead && !hostUsable) {
                        if (now >= floor) {
                            // One honest card update per re-check window — not
                            // every 10s tick (persist() writes each update).
                            repository.update(t.id) { cur ->
                                if (cur.userPaused || cur.status != TaskStatus.PAUSED) cur
                                else cur.copy(
                                    errorMessage = "$PARKED_HOST_MESSAGE — server unreachable 30+ min, still retrying every ~30 min. Tap retry to try now."
                                )
                            }
                            entry?.requeueNotBeforeMs?.set(now + PARKED_RECHECK_FLOOR_MS)
                            com.anonrode.downloader.util.DebugLog.user(
                                "park long-dead re-check task=${t.id} (retries every ~30m until the host returns)"
                            )
                        }
                        return@forEach
                    }
                    // Re-queue floor: parks escalate their wait (see parkFloorMs)
                    // so a repeatedly-rejected host is probed at most once per
                    // window instead of every tick. A long-dead host that just
                    // became usable bypasses the floor: recovery must win.
                    if (!longDead && now < floor) return@forEach
                    if (hostUsable) {
                        // Max 2 requeues per 10s tick: a 18-task batch comes
                        // back over ~90s instead of one thundering herd.
                        if (requeued >= 2) return@forEach
                        requeued++
                        entry?.firstParkedAtMs?.set(0L)
                        entry?.requeueNotBeforeMs?.set(0L)
                        repository.update(t.id) { task ->
                            if (task.userPaused || task.status != TaskStatus.PAUSED) task
                            else task.copy(status = TaskStatus.QUEUED, errorMessage = null)
                        }
                        anyRequeued = true
                    }
                }
                if (anyRequeued) processQueue()
            }
        }
    }

    /**
     * The two network-family requeue sweeps, shared by the network observer's
     * connect branch and the boot-retry pass. userPaused tasks are excluded
     * everywhere: a pause the user asked for must never be undone by a
     * network event. Each task's requeue-not-before floor gates the requeue:
     * a one-shot boot backoff for restored tasks (RESTORED_REQUEUE_FLOOR_MS),
     * escalation floors set by the park paths otherwise (0 in the common
     * case — in-session network parks requeue on the first heartbeat).
     * Atomic re-check inside the transform (engine-audit P1): the filter
