                // Release only when no newer job has taken the task over; a
                // retry may already have re-reserved the same task id.
                if (grantedLanes > 0 &&
                    (entry == null || ownedByThisJob || entry.activeJob == null)
                ) {
                    com.anonrode.downloader.pipeline.HostPolicyRegistry.LaneBudget.release(task.id)
                }
                if (ownedByThisJob && entry != null) {
                    entry.activeJob = null
                }
                // Never clear a newer job's start flag: release (and drop the
                // full-cancel flag) only when this job still owns the entry or
                // nobody does.
                if (entry == null || entry.activeJob == null) {
                    runtimeRegistry.releaseStartLock(task.id)
                    // This job's Turbo interaction has fully unwound by now; the
                    // flag must not linger for tasks that never re-enter Turbo.
                    TurboDownloader.clearCancelledFlag(task.id)
                }
                // A non-Exception throwable (Error) skips both catch blocks above:
                // repair a still-active row we own so a dead job can never hold a
                // concurrency slot forever. A row owned by a NEWER job is untouched.
                if (ownedByThisJob) {
                    val liveRow = repository.find(task.id)
                    if (liveRow != null && (liveRow.status == TaskStatus.DOWNLOADING || liveRow.status == TaskStatus.RESOLVING || liveRow.status == TaskStatus.VALIDATING)) {
                        repository.update(task.id) { t ->
                            if (t.status == TaskStatus.DOWNLOADING || t.status == TaskStatus.RESOLVING || t.status == TaskStatus.VALIDATING) {
                                t.copy(status = TaskStatus.PAUSED, speedBytesPerSec = 0.0)
                            } else t
                        }
                    }
                }
                // Rewritten HLS masters live in cacheDir/hls as scratch files
                // (950+ lines each). The inline sweep only ran on the success
                // path; a throw or cancel anywhere in the chain leaked them
                // until the OS reclaimed the cache (engine-audit P2). This
                // finally covers every exit; scoped by taskId so a concurrent
                // job for another task is never touched.
                try {
                    File(context.cacheDir, "hls").listFiles { f -> f.name.startsWith("hls-${task.id}") }
                        ?.forEach { it.delete() }
                } catch (_: Exception) {}
                updateServiceState(force = true)
                processQueue()
            }
        }

        runtimeRegistry.attachJob(initialTask.id, job)
        val current = repository.find(initialTask.id)
        if (current == null || current.userPaused || current.status !in setOf(TaskStatus.RESOLVING, TaskStatus.DOWNLOADING, TaskStatus.VALIDATING)) {
            job.cancel()
            // A pause landing after processQueue's status flip leaves the row in
            // RESOLVING/DOWNLOADING while this never-started LAZY job is killed
            // (its finally will never run): repair the row here, otherwise the
            // phantom active status holds a concurrency slot forever.
            if (current != null && current.userPaused &&
                (current.status == TaskStatus.RESOLVING || current.status == TaskStatus.DOWNLOADING)) {
                repository.update(initialTask.id) { t ->
                    if (t.userPaused && (t.status == TaskStatus.RESOLVING || t.status == TaskStatus.DOWNLOADING)) {
                        t.copy(status = TaskStatus.PAUSED, speedBytesPerSec = 0.0)

            // to runtimeRegistry.activeRunningTaskIds().

        // suppresses the runtimeRegistry.isEmpty()/none{} cancel-sweep heuristics.
        // Conditional remove: never clobbers a newer job for the same task.
        if (!job.isActive) {
            val entry = runtimeRegistry.get(initialTask.id)

                entry.activeJob = null
            }
            // The task row itself is gone (cancelled while this start was being
            // registered): drop the entry — no future run can ever clean it.
            if (current == null) {
                runtimeRegistry.forget(initialTask.id)
            }
        }
    }

    // ------------------------------------------------------------------
    // Bulk queue actions (Pause all / Resume all / Cancel all).
    //
    // The activity log showed users hand-tapping pause/cancel on card after
    // card (13 cancels in 2 seconds) because the queue screen had no bulk
    // actions. These run the SAME per-task teardown as the single-task
    // pause()/retry()/cancel() paths above — deliberately line-for-line,
    // so a bulk action can never diverge from what one card tap does —
    // with the service-state/processQueue churn batched to once per action
    // instead of once per task.

    /** Pause every task the user could pause card-by-card: running
     *  (DOWNLOADING/RESOLVING/VALIDATING) via pause()'s exact teardown, and
     *  QUEUED via pause()'s status write (a card tap on a queued card does
     *  the same). QUEUED tasks are included deliberately: each dying job's
     *  finally-guard calls processQueue(), which would otherwise start the
     *  queued tasks behind the user's back right after "Pause all".
     *  userPaused=true marks every one, so no auto-resume path (network
     *  reconnect, storage self-heal, host cooldown) will touch them. */
    fun pauseAll() {
        val pausable = repository.tasks.value.filter {
            it.status == TaskStatus.DOWNLOADING || it.status == TaskStatus.RESOLVING ||
                it.status == TaskStatus.VALIDATING || it.status == TaskStatus.QUEUED
        }
        if (pausable.isEmpty()) return
        com.anonrode.downloader.util.DebugLog.user("pause ALL (${pausable.size} tasks)")
        pausable.forEach { task ->
            val taskId = task.id
            // Same teardown as pause() — active jobs are cancelled, backends
            // killed, blocking HTTP swept once no task is left running.
            runtimeRegistry.getActiveJob(taskId)?.cancel()
            val entry = runtimeRegistry.get(taskId)
            if (entry != null) {
                entry.activeJob = null
                entry.isStarting.set(false)
            }
            YoutubeDlDownloader.killProcess(taskId)
            TurboDownloader.cancelTask(taskId)
            com.anonrode.downloader.util.DebugLog.user("pause $taskId")
            repository.update(taskId) { t ->
                // Status-guarded (engine-audit P2): a task that COMPLETED inside
                // the snapshot window must not be stamped PAUSED+userPaused —
                // that produced a "Paused at 100%" card with no auto-resume.
                if (t.status == TaskStatus.DOWNLOADING || t.status == TaskStatus.RESOLVING ||
                    t.status == TaskStatus.VALIDATING || t.status == TaskStatus.QUEUED
                ) t.copy(status = TaskStatus.PAUSED, speedBytesPerSec = 0.0, errorMessage = null, userPaused = true)
                else t
            }
        }
        // pause() sweeps in-flight HTTP only when the last job is gone; with
        // everything paused that condition holds by definition.
        if (runtimeRegistry.activeRunningTaskIds().isEmpty()) HttpClient.cancelInFlight()
        // One service/notification update for the whole batch, and NO
        // processQueue(): "Pause all" means everything stops, so the free
        // slots must not be refilled from the (now also paused) queue.
        updateServiceState(force = true)
    }

    /** Resume every PAUSED task via retry()'s exact path — including the ones
     *  carrying the userPaused mark: this IS the explicit user resume, the
     *  one path allowed to clear it. One processQueue() fills the slots. */
    fun resumeAll() {
        val paused = repository.tasks.value.filter { it.status == TaskStatus.PAUSED }
        if (paused.isEmpty()) return
        com.anonrode.downloader.util.DebugLog.user("resume ALL (${paused.size} tasks)")
        paused.forEach { task ->
            val taskId = task.id
            // Same per-task body as retry(): one host-health bypass each, a
            // fresh park/failover history, and the userPaused mark cleared.
            runtimeRegistry.markForManualRetry(taskId)
            repository.update(taskId) { it.copy(status = TaskStatus.QUEUED, errorMessage = null, userPaused = false) }
        }
        processQueue()
        updateServiceState(force = true)
    }

    /** Cancel every non-terminal task (QUEUED/DOWNLOADING/RESOLVING/VALIDATING/
     *  PAUSED) via cancel()'s exact teardown. Destructive — the UI confirms
     *  before calling this. Partial files are removed per task exactly as a
     *  single cancel does. */
    fun cancelAll() {
        val cancellable = repository.tasks.value.filter {
            it.status == TaskStatus.QUEUED || it.status == TaskStatus.DOWNLOADING ||
                it.status == TaskStatus.RESOLVING || it.status == TaskStatus.VALIDATING ||
                it.status == TaskStatus.PAUSED
        }
        if (cancellable.isEmpty()) return
        com.anonrode.downloader.util.DebugLog.user("cancel ALL (${cancellable.size} tasks)")
        cancellable.forEach { task ->
            val taskId = task.id
            // Same teardown as cancel(): mark full-cancel intent BEFORE job
            // cancellation, kill the backends, remove partial artifacts.
            val hadLiveJob = runtimeRegistry.getActiveJob(taskId) != null
            runtimeRegistry.markFullyCancelled(taskId)
            runtimeRegistry.getActiveJob(taskId)?.cancel()
            val entry = runtimeRegistry.get(taskId)
            if (entry != null) {
                entry.activeJob = null
                entry.isStarting.set(false)
            }
            YoutubeDlDownloader.killProcess(taskId)
            // Only gate a Turbo unwind; a queued task's flag would linger forever.
            TurboDownloader.cancelTask(taskId, isFullCancel = hadLiveJob)
            com.anonrode.downloader.util.DebugLog.user("cancel $taskId")
            val live = repository.find(taskId)
            // Cancel only what is STILL cancellable (engine-audit P2): if the
            // task completed between the snapshot and here, purging its
            // artifacts would delete a finished download and remove() would
            // drop its history entry.
            if (live != null && (live.status == TaskStatus.QUEUED || live.status == TaskStatus.DOWNLOADING ||
                    live.status == TaskStatus.RESOLVING || live.status == TaskStatus.VALIDATING ||
                    live.status == TaskStatus.PAUSED)
            ) {
                engineScope.launch {
                    purgeTaskArtifacts(live)
                }
                repository.remove(taskId)
            }
            runtimeRegistry.remove(taskId)
        }
        // Every job was cancelled above, so a global in-flight sweep cannot
        // cross-talk into another task — the condition cancel() relies on.
        if (runtimeRegistry.activeRunningTaskIds().isEmpty()) HttpClient.cancelInFlight()
        updateServiceState(force = true)
        processQueue()
    }
}

package com.anonrode.downloader.engine

import com.anonrode.downloader.data.net.HttpClient
import com.anonrode.downloader.pipeline.HostPolicyRegistry
import kotlinx.coroutines.CancellationException
import kotlinx.coroutines.Dispatchers
import kotlinx.coroutines.delay
import kotlinx.coroutines.ensureActive
import kotlinx.coroutines.withContext
import okhttp3.ConnectionPool
import okhttp3.HttpUrl.Companion.toHttpUrlOrNull
import okhttp3.OkHttpClient
import okhttp3.Request
import java.io.File
import java.util.concurrent.TimeUnit
import kotlin.coroutines.coroutineContext
import kotlin.math.max
import kotlin.math.min

/**
 * RC-9 root fix (board row 35, 2026-10-21): an in-process, PLAYER-LIKE HLS
 * VOD lane. Live evidence (activity logs 18/19 + workstation probes): a
 * stream limiter on the anime embed chain (fetch.nexabloom.top manifests,
 * mo6mo.stellarfrontier.space segments) trips on BYTES PER WINDOW per IP
 * (~87.7 MiB observed: every Demon's Ascension retry failed at the identical
 * 89,794 KiB boundary and next-day resume finished in seconds), while a
 * single sequential connection streamed clean through the same host family —
 * exactly how a media player consumes the same content all day.
 *
 * The released path was `yt-dlp -N 16` (`--concurrent-fragments`): 16 lanes ×
 * ~1 MB segments crossed the byte budget in seconds, then every lane 403'd on
 * the next fragment and `--abort-on-unavailable-fragments` failed the whole
 * ladder (blank `ERROR: ` → park; see RC-8). This lane replaces that shape
 * with:
 *   1. ONE manifest lifecycle — the master and the chosen variant are each
 *      fetched once per attempt;
 *   2. ONE pooled keep-alive connection with the task's persisted headers
 *      (Referer/UA/tokens — commit 0c4a35a) on every request;
 *   3. sequential segment fetch, appending in order at an exact water mark;
 *   4. byte-resume via a per-segment sidecar (`.hlsrs`), so a rate-limited
 *      403 parks and RESUMES at the failed boundary when the window resets
 *      instead of refighting the same quota from zero;
 *   5. one ffmpeg `-c copy` remux (no re-encode) through the bundled
 *      youtubedl-android ffmpeg binary (InstagramPhotoMuxer's extraction
 *      pattern).
 *
 * Anything that is NOT a plain unencrypted single-track VOD (AES keys,
 * separate audio renditions, EXT-X-MAP init segments, live windows without
 * `#EXT-X-ENDLIST`, subtitle media) returns `null` from [attempt] before a
 * single segment is fetched, and the engine falls back to yt-dlp unchanged.
 * The pure parsing/resume helpers and [downloadSegments] carry no Android
 * imports so they are JVM-testable.
 */
object HlsVodDownloader {

    /** Parsed single-variant media playlist. */
    data class ParsedVariant(
        val segments: List<String>,
        /** Byterange slice per segment (RC-5/P-2 class): null = full-body GET.
         *  Parallel to [segments]. `start`/`len` from EXT-X-BYTERANGE (RFC
         *  continuation when the offset is omitted). */
        val ranges: List<SegmentRange?>,
        val durationSec: Double,
        val encrypted: Boolean,
        val byterange: Boolean,
        val hasEndlist: Boolean
    ) {
        /** Downloadable by this lane: VOD, unencrypted. Byte-range playlists
         *  ARE supported (P-2: tested live on the vidbasic class). */
        val supported: Boolean
            get() = segments.isNotEmpty() && !encrypted && hasEndlist
    }

    data class SegmentRange(val start: Long, val len: Long)

    /** Typed decoy escape (P-2): the node answered, but with content that
     *  contradicts the playlist's byte math (the vidbasic 577-byte 206 decoy
     *  measured live). Park/resume family: the boundary holds. */
    class DecoyResponse(
        val bytesDone: Long,
        val segmentsDone: Int,
        val expectedLen: Long,
        val gotBytes: Long,
        val lastStatus: Int
    ) : Exception(
        "HLS node served decoy content (HTTP $lastStatus): expected $expectedLen bytes, got $gotBytes " +
            "after $segmentsDone committed segments — dropping this connection and resuming from a fresh one"
    )

    /** Typed rate-limit escape: carries the REAL status and progress (RC-8
     *  charter: no empty error text ever reaches a park banner). */
    class RateLimited(
        val bytesDone: Long,
        val segmentsDone: Int,
        val lastStatus: Int

        "HLS segment fetch blocked (HTTP $lastStatus) after $bytesDone bytes across $segmentsDone " +
            "segments — the stream host is rate-limiting; the download resumes at this exact " +
            "boundary later instead of restarting"
    )

    /** Cumulative segmentsDone+bytes recorded after each completed segment. */
    data class ResumeState(val segmentsDone: Int, val bytes: Long)

    /** Segment fetch shape shared by pacing/unit tests. */
    data class SegmentOutcome(val index: Int, val bytes: Long, val status: Int)

    // ──────────────────────────── pure parsing ────────────────────────────

    /** Absolute-URL resolve (okhttp resolves relative and `//host/…`). */
    internal fun resolveUri(base: String, uri: String): String? {
        if (uri.isBlank()) return null
        return base.toHttpUrlOrNull()?.resolve(uri.trim())?.toString()
    }

    /** Extract the 1080/720/… height from an EXT-X-STREAM-INF line, 0 if none. */
    internal fun variantHeight(tag: String): Int =
        Regex("""RESOLUTION=(\d+)x(\d+)""", RegexOption.IGNORE_CASE)
            .find(tag)?.groupValues?.get(2)?.toIntOrNull() ?: 0

    /**
     * Multi-variant master → the variant URL at-or-below [maxHeight] with the
     * highest resolution (yt-dlp height-selection parity; when nothing fits,
     * the SMALLEST variant, never up-resolve). Returns null when the body is
     * not a multivariant master — the caller then parses it as the variant.
     */
    internal fun parseMaster(body: String, baseUrl: String, maxHeight: Int): String? {
        val lines = body.lineSequence().map { it.trim() }.toList()
        if (lines.none { it.startsWith("#EXT-X-STREAM-INF", ignoreCase = true) }) return null
        var bestUrl: String? = null
        var bestHeight = Int.MAX_VALUE
        var i = 1
        while (i < lines.size) {
            val tag = lines[i - 1]
            val uri = lines[i]
            if (tag.startsWith("#EXT-X-STREAM-INF", ignoreCase = true) &&
                !uri.startsWith("#") && uri.isNotBlank()
            ) {
                val height = variantHeight(tag)
                val resolved = resolveUri(baseUrl, uri)
                if (resolved != null) {
                    if (height in 1..maxHeight) {
                        // At-or-below the cap: prefer the LARGEST such height.
                        if (bestUrl == null || bestHeight > maxHeight || height > bestHeight) {
                            bestUrl = resolved
                            bestHeight = height
                        }
                    } else if (bestUrl == null || (bestHeight > maxHeight && height < bestHeight)) {
                        // Nothing fits yet: keep the SMALLEST as last resort.
                        bestUrl = resolved
                        bestHeight = height
                    }
                }
            }
            i++
        }
        return bestUrl
    }

    /** RC-5: any subtitle WEBVTT/text track declared in EXT-X-MEDIA tags. */
    internal fun hasSubtitleMedia(body: String): Boolean =
        Regex("""#EXT-X-MEDIA:TYPE=SUBTITLES""", RegexOption.IGNORE_CASE).containsMatchIn(body)

    private val AUDIO_MEDIA = Regex(
        """#EXT-X-MEDIA\s*:[^\n]*TYPE\s*=\s*AUDIO""",
        RegexOption.IGNORE_CASE
    )
    private val INIT_MAP = Regex("""#EXT-X-MAP\s*:""", RegexOption.IGNORE_CASE)

    /**
     * Shapes the paced lane cannot reproduce faithfully. It only concatenates
     * one unencrypted video segment stream; a separate AUDIO media group
     * (DASH-derived HLS) would be silently dropped, and an EXT-X-MAP init
     * segment would be omitted, yielding an unplayable or video-only file.
     * Return a human reason so [attempt] can log and hand the job to yt-dlp,
     * which muxes both tracks and honours the init map.
     */
    internal fun unsupportedShapeForPacedLane(masterBody: String, variantBody: String): String? = when {
        hasSubtitleMedia(masterBody) || hasSubtitleMedia(variantBody) -> "subtitle media"
        AUDIO_MEDIA.containsMatchIn(masterBody) -> "separate audio media group"
        INIT_MAP.containsMatchIn(masterBody) || INIT_MAP.containsMatchIn(variantBody) -> "EXT-X-MAP init segment"
        else -> null
    }

    /** Single-variant media playlist → segments, metadata, support flags. */
    internal fun parseVariant(body: String, baseUrl: String): ParsedVariant {
        val raw = body.lineSequence().map { it.trim() }.filter { it.isNotEmpty() }.toList()
        val segments = mutableListOf<String>()
        val ranges = mutableListOf<SegmentRange?>()
        var duration = 0.0
        var encrypted = false
        var byterange = false
        var endlist = false
        // BYTERANGE always precedes its own URI (HLS semantics). An omitted
        // @offset continues after the PREVIOUS sub-range of the same resource
        // (RFC 8216 continuation — the vidbasic shape).
        segments.clear(); ranges.clear()
        var nextOffset = -1L
        var pendingRange: SegmentRange? = null
        for (line in raw) {
            when {
                line.startsWith("#EXT-X-KEY", ignoreCase = true) -> {
                    if (!line.contains("METHOD=NONE", ignoreCase = true)) encrypted = true
                }
                line.startsWith("#EXT-X-BYTERANGE", ignoreCase = true) -> {
                    byterange = true
                    val spec = line.substringAfter(':')
                    val n = spec.substringBefore('@').trim().toLongOrNull() ?: -1L
                    val o = spec.substringAfter('@', "").trim().toLongOrNull()
                    val start = if (o != null && o >= 0) o else nextOffset
                    pendingRange = if (n > 0 && start >= 0) SegmentRange(start, n) else null
                }
                line.startsWith("#EXT-X-ENDLIST", ignoreCase = true) -> endlist = true
                line.startsWith("#EXTINF", ignoreCase = true) -> {
                    val d = line.substringAfter(':').substringBefore(',').trim().toDoubleOrNull()
                    if (d != null) duration += d
                }
                !line.startsWith("#") -> {
                    resolveUri(baseUrl, line)?.let { segments.add(it) }
                    ranges.add(pendingRange)
                    pendingRange?.let { nextOffset = it.start + it.len }
                    pendingRange = null
                }
            }
        }
        return ParsedVariant(segments, ranges, duration, encrypted, byterange, endlist)
    }

    // ──────────────────────────── resume state ────────────────────────────

    private const val SIDECAR_MAGIC = "hlsrs1"

    fun readResume(sidecar: File): ResumeState {
        if (!sidecar.isFile) return ResumeState(0, 0L)
        return try {
            val lines = sidecar.readLines()
            val head = lines.firstOrNull()?.trim().orEmpty()
            if (head != SIDECAR_MAGIC || lines.size < 3) return ResumeState(0, 0L)
            val n = lines[1].trim().toIntOrNull() ?: 0
            val b = lines[2].trim().toLongOrNull() ?: 0L
            if (n < 0 || b < 0) ResumeState(0, 0L)
            else ResumeState(min(n, Int.MAX_VALUE), b)
        } catch (_: Exception) {
            ResumeState(0, 0L)
        }
    }

    /** Atomic-ish sidecar write (tmp + rename) so a crash never forks the
     *  byte offset from the segment index. */
    fun writeResume(sidecar: File, segmentsDone: Int, bytes: Long) {
        try {
            val tmp = File(sidecar.absolutePath + ".tmp")
            tmp.writeText("$SIDECAR_MAGIC\n$segmentsDone\n$bytes\n")
            if (!tmp.renameTo(sidecar)) {
                tmp.copyTo(sidecar, overwrite = true)
                tmp.delete()
            }
        } catch (_: Exception) {
        }
    }

    fun deleteResume(sidecar: File) {
        try { sidecar.delete() } catch (_: Exception) {}
        try { File(sidecar.absolutePath + ".tmp").delete() } catch (_: Exception) {}
    }

    // ──────────────────────────── core fetch loop ────────────────────────────

    /**
     * Sequential, keep-alive segment fetch appending to [dest] in order at an
     * exact water mark. Returns [dest] fully written (raw segment
     * concatenation — remux is the caller's job). Throws [RateLimited] when
     * the host keeps rejecting a segment after small per-segment retries, so
     * the ENGINE can park with a real reason and re-queue; the next attempt
     * resumes from the sidecar position. Pure okhttp: JVM-testable.
     */
    suspend fun downloadSegments(
        client: OkHttpClient,
        segments: List<String>,
        headers: Map<String, String>,
        dest: File,
        sidecar: File,
        estimatedTotalBytes: Long,
        onProgress: (downloaded: Long, total: Long, speed: Long, eta: Long) -> Unit,
        isCancelled: () -> Boolean,
        ranges: List<SegmentRange?>? = null
    ): File = withContext(Dispatchers.IO) {
        val resume = readResume(sidecar)
        var startIndex = resume.segmentsDone.coerceIn(0, segments.size)
        val alreadyBytes = if (startIndex > 0) resume.bytes else 0L
        var cumulative = alreadyBytes
        var speedMeter = SpeedMeter(alreadyBytes)
        var avgSegment = 0L
        dest.parentFile?.mkdirs()

        if (startIndex > 0) {
            // The staging file is our append log; the sidecar is the truth.
            val len = if (dest.isFile) dest.length() else 0L
            if (len > alreadyBytes) {
                // A kill between "append" and "sidecar write" leaves garbage
                // past the water mark — trim back to the exact boundary.
                try { java.io.RandomAccessFile(dest, "rw").use { it.setLength(alreadyBytes) } } catch (_: Exception) {}
            } else if (len < alreadyBytes) {
                // Staging truncated/lost (cache clean): restart the stream.
                writeResume(sidecar, 0, 0L)
                startIndex = 0
                cumulative = 0L
                speedMeter = SpeedMeter(0L)
            }
        }
        if (startIndex == 0) {
            try { dest.delete() } catch (_: Exception) {}
        } else if (estimatedTotalBytes <= 0) {
            avgSegment = max(1L, alreadyBytes / max(1, startIndex))
        }

        val sizesSeen = mutableListOf<Long>()
        // P-2 decoy accounting (vidbasic class): the node pool intermittently
        // answers a 577-byte 206 that contradicts the playlist's byte math.
        var lastFailureWasDecoy = false
        var lastDecoyGot = 0L
        var lastDecoyExpected = 0L
        var lastStatusSeen = 0
        for (idx in startIndex until segments.size) {
            ensureActive()
            check(!isCancelled()) { "HLS lane cancelled" }
            val url = segments[idx]
            val range = ranges?.getOrNull(idx)
            val expectedLen = range?.len ?: -1L
            var lastStatus = 0
            var appended = false
            for (attemptNo in 1..3) {
                ensureActive()
                var bytesThisSegment = 0L
                try {
                    val reqHeaders = if (range != null) {
                        headers + mapOf("Range" to "bytes=${range.start}-${range.start + range.len - 1}")
                    } else headers
                    client.newCall(buildRequest(url, reqHeaders)).execute().use { res ->
                        lastStatus = res.code
                        lastStatusSeen = res.code
                        if (res.code == 403 || res.code == 429) {
                            // P-1 (rows 35/8, owner directive): drop the
                            // throttled connection and pick up a NEW one
                            // BEFORE the typed escape — pooled connections may
                            // carry per-connection limiter state, and a redial
                            // is free under every limiter model (it only
                            // matters if the budget is per-connection). The
                            // park/resume boundary semantics are unchanged:
                            // once the fresh dials are exhausted the escape
                            // below still parks at the committed boundary.
                            runCatching { client.connectionPool.evictAll() }
                            if (attemptNo < 3) {
                                throw java.io.IOException("redial after HTTP ${res.code} (fresh connection)")
                            }
                            // Quota family after a fresh dial also failed:
                            // every committed segment is in the sidecar, so
                            // the resumed attempt continues at THIS boundary.
                            throw RateLimited(cumulative, idx, res.code)
                        }
                        if (!res.isSuccessful) {
                            throw java.io.IOException("HTTP ${res.code}")
                        }
                        val body = res.body ?: throw java.io.IOException("empty body")
                        val src = body.byteStream()
                        val buf = ByteArray(256 * 1024)
                        java.io.RandomAccessFile(dest, "rw").use { raf ->
                            raf.seek(cumulative)
                            while (true) {
                                if (isCancelled()) throw CancellationException("HLS lane cancelled")
                                ensureActive()
                                val n = src.read(buf)
                                if (n < 0) break
                                if (n > 0) raf.write(buf, 0, n)
                                bytesThisSegment += max(0, n)
                            }
                        }
                        // P-2 decoy gate: the playlist's byte math is the truth.
                        // A ranged segment that delivered a different length
                        // than declared is the live-measured vidbasic decoy
                        // (577-byte 206 from a bad node) — do NOT commit it;
                        // drop this connection and let the retry redial fresh.
                        if (range != null && bytesThisSegment != range.len) {
                            runCatching { client.connectionPool.evictAll() }
                            lastFailureWasDecoy = true
                            lastDecoyGot = bytesThisSegment
                            lastDecoyExpected = range.len
                            throw java.io.IOException(
                                "decoy response: expected ${range.len} bytes, got $bytesThisSegment"
                            )
                        }
                    }
                    appended = true
                    lastFailureWasDecoy = false
                    if (bytesThisSegment > 0) {
                        // A partially-written previous attempt is overwritten
                        // from the water mark, so the file never forks.
                        cumulative += bytesThisSegment
                        sizesSeen.add(bytesThisSegment)
                        avgSegment = sizesSeen.sum() / sizesSeen.size
                        writeResume(sidecar, idx + 1, cumulative)
                        val spd = speedMeter.sample(cumulative)
                        val remaining = (segments.size - (idx + 1)).coerceAtLeast(0)
                        val total = if (estimatedTotalBytes > 0)
                            max(estimatedTotalBytes, cumulative)
                        else
                            max(cumulative + avgSegment * remaining, cumulative + 1)
                        val eta = if (spd > 0) (total - cumulative) / spd else 0L
                        onProgress(cumulative, total, spd, eta)
                    }
                    break
                } catch (e: RateLimited) {
                    throw e
                } catch (ce: CancellationException) {
                    // State is already committed per-segment; propagate.
                    throw ce
                } catch (e: Exception) {
                    // Partial bytes past the water mark are overwritten by the
                    // retry (seek(cumulative) above), so integrity holds.
                    if (attemptNo == 3) {
                        if (lastFailureWasDecoy) {
                            // P-2 family escape: park/resume at the boundary
                            // with the real expected/got byte math.
                            throw DecoyResponse(
                                cumulative, idx, lastDecoyExpected, lastDecoyGot, lastStatusSeen
                            )
                        }
                        throw java.io.IOException(
                            "HLS segment $idx failed after 3 attempts (status $lastStatus): ${e.message}"
                        )
                    }
                    delay(attemptNo * 800L)
                }
            }
            if (!appended) throw java.io.IOException("HLS segment $idx failed (status $lastStatus)")
        }
        try {
            java.io.RandomAccessFile(dest, "rw").use { it.setLength(cumulative) }
        } catch (_: Exception) {}
        dest
    }

    internal fun buildRequest(url: String, headers: Map<String, String>): Request {
        val b = Request.Builder().url(url)
        for ((k, v) in headers) {
            if (v.isBlank()) continue
            when (k.lowercase()) {
                "user-agent" -> b.header("User-Agent", v)
                "referer" -> b.header("Referer", v)
                "origin" -> b.header("Origin", v)
                "cookie" -> b.header("Cookie", v)
                "range" -> b.header("Range", v)
                else -> if (!k.contains(':')) b.header(k, v)
            }
        }
        if (headers.entries.none { it.key.equals("User-Agent", true) && it.value.isNotBlank() }) {
            b.header("User-Agent", com.anonrode.downloader.data.net.HttpClient.DEFAULT_UA)
        }
        return b.build()
    }

    // ──────────────────────────── engine-facing driver ────────────────────────────

    /**
     * One paced attempt, manifest to remuxed file. Returns the produced media
     * file, or null when the playlist is not a supported plain VOD (caller
     * falls back to yt-dlp). Throws [RateLimited] for the byte-limiter escape
     * (engine parks and resumes); other failures throw IOException.
     */
    suspend fun attempt(
        masterUrl: String,
        outPath: File,
        sidecar: File,
        headers: Map<String, String>,
        maxHeight: Int,
        estimatedTotalBytes: Long,
        onProgress: (downloaded: Long, total: Long, speed: Long, eta: Long) -> Unit,
        isCancelled: () -> Boolean,
        prefetchedMasterBody: String? = null,
        prefetchedVariantBody: String? = null,
        prefetchedVariantUrl: String? = null
    ): File? = withContext(Dispatchers.IO) {
        val baseClient = if (com.anonrode.downloader.pipeline.HostPolicyRegistry.allowsPermissiveTlsFallback(masterUrl)) {
            HttpClient.permissiveDownloadClient
        } else {
            HttpClient.downloadClient
        }
        val client = baseClient.newBuilder()
            // ONE pooled connection by design: the limiter counts bytes per
            // window; a single keep-alive connection is the browser shape.
            .connectionPool(ConnectionPool(2, 5, TimeUnit.MINUTES))
            .connectTimeout(12, TimeUnit.SECONDS)
            .readTimeout(30, TimeUnit.SECONDS)
            .retryOnConnectionFailure(false)
            .build()

        // Manifest lifecycle (1/2): master, fetched once (or reused from preflight).
        val masterBody = prefetchedMasterBody ?: fetchText(client, masterUrl, headers) ?: return@withContext null
        val variantUrl = prefetchedVariantUrl ?: parseMaster(masterBody, masterUrl, maxHeight) ?: masterUrl
        // Manifest lifecycle (2/2): the chosen variant, fetched exactly once (or reused from preflight).
        val variantBody = if (variantUrl == masterUrl) masterBody
        else prefetchedVariantBody ?: fetchText(client, variantUrl, headers) ?: return@withContext null
        val variant = parseVariant(variantBody, variantUrl)
        // RC-5: a master/variant that DECLARES subtitle media must be served
        // by the yt-dlp path (which requests --write-subs), never by this raw
        // segment lane or the subtitle tracks would be silently dropped.
        // The same handoff applies to DASH-derived HLS: a separate audio
        // media group and/or an EXT-X-MAP init segment cannot be reproduced
        // by concatenating video fragments (2026-10-22 vidbolt bridge:
        // master declared AUDIO, every variant carried EXT-X-MAP). Sending
        // that shape to yt-dlp downloads BOTH tracks and the init segment,
        // instead of burning bandwidth on a video-only remux or failing.
        unsupportedShapeForPacedLane(masterBody, variantBody)?.let { reason ->
            com.anonrode.downloader.util.DebugLog.resolve(
                "paced HLS lane: $reason — handing the job to yt-dlp for a complete mux"
            )
            return@withContext null
        }
        if (!variant.supported) return@withContext null

        com.anonrode.downloader.util.DebugLog.backend(
            "task=${outPath.nameWithoutExtension} paced HLS lane: ${variant.segments.size} segments, " +
                "%.0fs".format(variant.durationSec) + ", resume=${readResume(sidecar).segmentsDone}"
        )

        val staging = File(outPath.absolutePath + ".hts")
        try {
            downloadSegments(
                client, variant.segments, headers, staging, sidecar, estimatedTotalBytes,
                onProgress, isCancelled, variant.ranges
            )
        } catch (e: Exception) {
            // Staged bytes + sidecar are intentionally kept for the resumed
            // attempt (byte-resume, not restart).
            throw e
        }

        // Remux: single -c copy pass (no re-encode), yt-dlp merge parity.
        val remuxed = remuxTo(staging, outPath)
        if (remuxed) {
            deleteResume(sidecar)
            try { staging.delete() } catch (_: Exception) {}
            outPath
        } else {
            null
        }
    }

    private suspend fun fetchText(
        client: OkHttpClient,
        url: String,
        headers: Map<String, String>
    ): String? = withContext(Dispatchers.IO) {
        try {
            client.newCall(buildRequest(url, headers)).execute().use { res ->
                if (!res.isSuccessful) return@use null
                com.anonrode.downloader.data.net.HttpClient.cappedText(res, maxBytes = 2L * 1024 * 1024)
            }
        } catch (_: Exception) {
            null
        }
    }

    // ═════════════════════════════ remux (ffmpeg) ═════════════════════════════

    /**
     * Resolve the youtubedl-android-extracted ffmpeg binary (same precedence
     * as InstagramPhotoMuxer: the extracted archive — whose versioned shared
     * libraries are complete — first, bare jniLibs fallback second).
     */
    internal fun resolveFfmpegBinary(context: android.content.Context): File? {
        try {
            com.yausername.ffmpeg.FFmpeg.getInstance().init(context)
        } catch (_: Throwable) {
        }
        val extracted = File(context.noBackupFilesDir, "youtubedl-android/packages/ffmpeg")
        extracted.walkTopDown()
            .firstOrNull { it.isFile && it.name in setOf("libffmpeg.so", "libffmpeg.bin.so", "ffmpeg") }
            ?.let { return it }
        return File(context.applicationInfo.nativeLibraryDir, "libffmpeg.so").takeIf { it.isFile }
    }

    /**
     * Concat-demux `-c copy` remux of the staged segment stream into
     * [outPath]. Returns false (never throws) when ffmpeg is unavailable or
     * fails; the caller falls back to yt-dlp with the stage + sidecar intact
     * (progress preserved either way).
     */
    internal fun remuxTo(staging: File, outPath: File): Boolean {
        var p: Process? = null
        return try {
            val context = appContextRef?.get() ?: return false
            val ff = resolveFfmpegBinary(context) ?: return false
            val tmpOut = File(outPath.parentFile, outPath.nameWithoutExtension + ".remux.mp4")
            try { tmpOut.delete() } catch (_: Exception) {}
            val cmd = mutableListOf(
                ff.absolutePath,
                "-y", "-loglevel", "error",
                "-i", staging.absolutePath,
                "-c", "copy",
                "-bsf:a", "aac_adtstoasc",
                "-movflags", "+faststart",
                "-f", "mp4",
                tmpOut.absolutePath
            )
            val pb = ProcessBuilder(cmd)
            pb.environment()["TMPDIR"] = outPath.parentFile?.absolutePath ?: "."
            // Same extracted-runtime layout as the photo muxer: versioned
            // libav*.so.* live in usr/lib, not beside the executable.
            val ldLibraryPath = InstagramPhotoMuxer.buildFfmpegLdLibraryPath(context, ff)
            if (ldLibraryPath.isNotBlank()) {
                val existing = pb.environment()["LD_LIBRARY_PATH"]
                pb.environment()["LD_LIBRARY_PATH"] =
                    if (existing.isNullOrBlank()) ldLibraryPath
                    else "$ldLibraryPath${File.pathSeparator}$existing"
            }
            pb.redirectErrorStream(true)
            p = pb.start()
            val proc = p
            // Drain stdout so a chatty build cannot block on a full pipe.
            Thread {
                try { proc.inputStream.readBytes() } catch (_: Exception) {}
            }.apply { isDaemon = true; start() }
            val ok = proc.waitFor(10, TimeUnit.MINUTES) && proc.exitValue() == 0 && tmpOut.length() > 0
            if (!ok) {
                try { tmpOut.delete() } catch (_: Exception) {}
                return false
            }
            if (outPath.exists()) try { outPath.delete() } catch (_: Exception) {}
            tmpOut.renameTo(outPath)
        } catch (e: InterruptedException) {
            try { File(outPath.parentFile, outPath.nameWithoutExtension + ".remux.mp4").delete() } catch (_: Exception) {}
            Thread.currentThread().interrupt()
            throw kotlinx.coroutines.CancellationException("HLS remux interrupted").apply { initCause(e) }
        } catch (_: Exception) {
            try { File(outPath.parentFile, outPath.nameWithoutExtension + ".remux.mp4").delete() } catch (_: Exception) {}
            false
        } finally {
            try { p?.destroyForcibly() } catch (_: Exception) {}
        }
    }

    /** Context hand-off set once by the engine (avoids threading a Context
     *  through every call signature; application-scoped, weakly held). */
    @Volatile
    internal var appContextRef: java.lang.ref.WeakReference<android.content.Context>? = null

    fun attachContext(context: android.content.Context) {
        appContextRef = java.lang.ref.WeakReference(context.applicationContext)
    }
}

package com.anonrode.downloader.engine

import com.anonrode.downloader.data.net.HttpClient
import kotlinx.coroutines.CancellationException
import kotlinx.coroutines.async
import kotlinx.coroutines.coroutineScope
import kotlinx.coroutines.withTimeoutOrNull

/**
 * Segment-Sampling Estimator (SSE): predict an HLS download's final size by
 * MEASURING real segments instead of trusting the master playlist's BANDWIDTH
 * tag — a peak value, not an average, and some CDNs lie outright.
 *
 * The media playlist lists every segment with an exact #EXTINF duration, so
 * the segment count N is exact; the only unknown is the average segment size.
 * That unknown is probed: k=4 segments at ~5/35/65/95% of the playlist with
 * a `Range: bytes=0-1024` request (headers only — the body is never read), all
 * run concurrently. estimate_wire = mean(sampled sizes) * N. When the master
 * carries an #EXT-X-MEDIA:TYPE=AUDIO rendition, that audio playlist is
 * fetched, ONE audio segment is probed, and its projected size
 * (sample * audio segment count) is added to the wire total. Finally the
 * wire total is scaled by the TS→MP4 remux factor (0.93, or 0.99 when the
 * playlist uses fMP4 segments — detected by the absence of .ts names).
 *
 * Every failure path returns null (live/sliding-window playlist without
 * ENDLIST, playlist fetch failure, a single failed probe). Callers must treat
 * null as "no estimate" and never fail a download over it; only coroutine
 * cancellation propagates.
 */
object HlsSizeEstimator {

    /** Playlist percentiles the segment probes land on. */
    private val PROBE_POSITIONS = listOf(5, 35, 65, 95)

    private val URI_VALUE = Regex("URI=\"([^\"]+)\"")

    /**
     * Count media segments in an HLS playlist: every #EXTINF line is exactly
     * one segment (an EXT-X-BYTERANGE segment still carries a single EXTINF).
     * Tag lines, blank lines and URIs are ignored.
     */
    fun parseSegmentCount(playlistText: String): Int {
        if (playlistText.isEmpty()) return 0
        return playlistText.lineSequence().count { it.trimStart().startsWith("#EXTINF") }
    }

    /**
     * The estimate math: (mean of sampled segment sizes) * segmentCount,
     * scaled by the remux factor — 0.93 for TS segments (yt-dlp remuxes TS
     * into MP4, ~7% smaller on the wire), 0.99 for fMP4 segments (copied
     * with a near-neutral factor). Returns 0 for degenerate inputs: no
     * samples, a zero/negative sample, or no segments.
     */
    fun estimateFromSamples(sampleSizes: List<Long>, segmentCount: Int, isFmp4: Boolean): Long {
        if (sampleSizes.isEmpty() || segmentCount <= 0) return 0L
        if (sampleSizes.any { it <= 0L }) return 0L
        val mean = sampleSizes.average()
        val factor = if (isFmp4) 0.99 else 0.93
        return (mean * segmentCount * factor).toLong()
    }
    /**
     * Parse total byte length from #EXT-X-BYTERANGE lines when present.
     * When segments are byte ranges of a combined file, summing the lengths
     * gives the exact total file size without making external network probes.
     */
    fun parseByteRangeTotal(playlistText: String): Long? {
        if (!playlistText.contains("#EXT-X-BYTERANGE")) return null
        val matches = Regex("""#EXT-X-BYTERANGE:\s*(\d+)""").findAll(playlistText).toList()
        if (matches.isEmpty()) return null
        val sum = matches.sumOf { it.groupValues[1].toLongOrNull() ?: 0L }
        return if (sum > 0L) sum else null
    }

    /**
     * Full size-estimation pipeline. [masterText] is the already-fetched
     * master playlist, [masterUrl] its URL (base for relative audio URIs),
     * [variantUrl] the media playlist the real download will consume, and
     * [referer] the same referer the real download uses. Returns the
     * predicted final file size in bytes, or null when no estimate is
     * possible. Never throws (except coroutine cancellation).
     */
    suspend fun estimate(
        masterText: String,
        masterUrl: String,
        variantUrl: String,
        referer: String?,
        prefetchedVariantText: String? = null
    ): Long? {
        try {
            val variantText = prefetchedVariantText
                ?: HttpClient.getText(variantUrl, referer = referer, tag = "hls-estimate")
                ?: return null
            // Live / sliding-window playlists have no ENDLIST: the segment
            // count keeps changing, so no estimate.
            if (!variantText.contains("#EXT-X-ENDLIST")) return null
            val segmentCount = parseSegmentCount(variantText)
            if (segmentCount <= 0) return null
            val segments = segmentUrls(variantText, variantUrl)
            if (segments.isEmpty()) return null
            val fmp4 = isFmp4(segments)

            // Byte-range optimization: when playlist carries #EXT-X-BYTERANGE,
            // calculate exact total directly from range lengths without probing.
            val byteRangeTotal = parseByteRangeTotal(variantText)
            if (byteRangeTotal != null) {
                val factor = if (fmp4) 0.99 else 0.93
                val total = (byteRangeTotal * factor).toLong()
                return if (total in 1L..15_000_000_000L) total else null
            }

            // Probe k=4 segments at spread-out positions, concurrently.
            val indices = PROBE_POSITIONS
                .map { (segmentCount * it / 100).coerceIn(0, segmentCount - 1) }
                .distinct()
            if (indices.any { it >= segments.size }) return null
            val samples = withTimeoutOrNull(8_000L) {
                coroutineScope {
                    indices.map { idx -> async { probeSegmentSize(segments[idx], referer) } }
                        .map { it.await() }
                }
            } ?: return null
            // Reject null or suspiciously huge samples (>= 25MB). A single HLS segment is
            // typically 1-5MB. If a probe returns >= 25MB, the CDN returned the whole file's
            // Content-Range rather than a segment slice.
            if (samples.any { it == null || it >= 25 * 1024 * 1024L }) return null
            var total = estimateFromSamples(samples.filterNotNull(), segmentCount, fmp4)
            if (total <= 0L || total > 15_000_000_000L) return null // Cap estimate at 15GB

            // Optional audio rendition: probe ONE audio segment and add its
            // projected size (sample * audio segment count) to the total.
            val audioUri = audioPlaylistUri(masterText)
            if (audioUri != null) {
                val audioUrl = resolveUrl(masterUrl, audioUri) ?: return null
                val audioText = HttpClient.getText(audioUrl, referer = referer, tag = "hls-estimate") ?: return null
                if (!audioText.contains("#EXT-X-ENDLIST")) return null
                val audioCount = parseSegmentCount(audioText)
                if (audioCount > 0) {
                    val audioSegments = segmentUrls(audioText, audioUrl)
                    if (audioSegments.isEmpty()) return null
                    // Middle segment: representative of a constant-bitrate
                    // audio track (the first can be an intro outlier).
                    val audioSample = probeSegmentSize(
                        audioSegments[(audioCount / 2).coerceIn(0, audioSegments.size - 1)],
                        referer
                    ) ?: return null
                    if (audioSample >= 15 * 1024 * 1024L) return null
                    total += estimateFromSamples(listOf(audioSample), audioCount, fmp4)
                }
            }
            return if (total in 1L..15_000_000_000L) total else null
        } catch (e: CancellationException) {
            throw e
        } catch (_: Exception) {
            return null
        }
    }

    /**
     * Headers-only size probe: GET with `Range: bytes=0-1024` and read the full
     * size out of the response headers — the body is closed, never read
     * (same pattern as HttpClient.probe).
     *  - 206 (range honored): the full size rides in `Content-Range:
     *    bytes 0-0/TOTAL`; Content-Length is only the 1-byte slice.
     *  - 200 (server ignored Range): Content-Length is the full size.
     * `Accept-Encoding: identity` keeps OkHttp from transparently gzipping
     * (which would strip Content-Length from the response).
     */
    private fun probeSegmentSize(url: String, referer: String?): Long? {
        return try {
            HttpClient.get(
                url,
                referer = referer,
                headers = mapOf("Range" to "bytes=0-1024", "Accept-Encoding" to "identity"),
                tag = "hls-estimate"
            ).use { res ->
                val ct = res.header("Content-Type")?.lowercase() ?: ""
                if (ct.contains("text/html") || ct.contains("application/xhtml")) {
                    return null
                }
                when (res.code) {
                    206 -> res.header("Content-Range")?.substringAfter('/')?.trim()?.toLongOrNull()
                    200 -> res.header("Content-Length")?.toLongOrNull()
                    else -> null
                }
            }
        } catch (e: CancellationException) {
            throw e
        } catch (_: Exception) {
            null
        }
    }

    /** Non-tag, non-blank lines of a playlist, resolved against [baseUrl]. */
    private fun segmentUrls(playlistText: String, baseUrl: String): List<String> {
        return playlistText.lineSequence()
            .map { it.trim() }
            .filter { it.isNotBlank() && !it.startsWith("#") }
            .mapNotNull { resolveUrl(baseUrl, it) }
            .toList()
    }

    /** Absolute-https resolution of a playlist-relative / protocol-relative URI. */
    private fun resolveUrl(base: String, uri: String): String? {
        if (uri.startsWith("http://") || uri.startsWith("https://")) return uri
        if (uri.startsWith("//")) return "https:$uri"
        return try {
            HttpClient.safeResolveUri(base, uri)
        } catch (_: Exception) {
            null
        }
    }

    /** fMP4 detection: no segment name carries a .ts extension. */
    private fun isFmp4(segmentUrls: List<String>): Boolean =
        segmentUrls.none { it.substringBefore('?').substringBefore('#').endsWith(".ts", ignoreCase = true) }

    /** First #EXT-X-MEDIA:TYPE=AUDIO rendition that carries a URI, or null. */
    private fun audioPlaylistUri(masterText: String): String? {
        for (line in masterText.lineSequence()) {
            val l = line.trim()
            if (!l.startsWith("#EXT-X-MEDIA")) continue
            if (!l.contains("TYPE=AUDIO")) continue
            val m = URI_VALUE.find(l) ?: continue
            return m.groupValues[1]
        }
        return null
    }
}

import kotlin.coroutines.coroutineContext
import java.io.File

/**
 * yt-dlp's native HLS downloader stages each fragment in
 * `<output>.part-Frag<N>` and deletes them only after concatenation. After a
 * killed/403-aborted run those files are stale resume state: a retry that
 * expects `Frag263` to exist dies with "No such file or directory:
 * ...part-Frag263" before downloading anything (live 2026-10-19). They are
 * scratch, never banked media, so a pre-attempt sweep is always safe.
 *
 * [privateWorkdir] is the per-task `.work-<taskId>` directory: everything
 * there belongs to this task. Otherwise the shared target folder is scanned
 * and only files belonging to [stem] are touched.
 */
internal fun partFragFiles(outDir: File, stem: String, privateWorkdir: Boolean): List<File> {
    val files = outDir.listFiles() ?: return emptyList()
    return files.filter { f ->
        f.isFile &&
            f.name.contains(".part-Frag", ignoreCase = true) &&
            (privateWorkdir || stem.isBlank() || f.name.startsWith("$stem."))
    }
}

internal fun partFragBytes(outDir: File, stem: String, privateWorkdir: Boolean = false): Long =
    partFragFiles(outDir, stem, privateWorkdir).sumOf { it.length() }

internal fun deletePartFragFiles(outDir: File, stem: String, privateWorkdir: Boolean): Int {
    var removed = 0
    for (f in partFragFiles(outDir, stem, privateWorkdir)) {
        try {
            if (f.delete()) removed++
        } catch (_: Exception) {}
    }
    return removed
}

    class BackendInterruptedException(message: String) : Exception(message)

    private fun isNativeBackendInterruption(error: Throwable): Boolean {

    internal fun isAllCanceledLadder(errors: String, attempts: Int): Boolean {
        if (attempts <= 0) return false
        val lines = errors.lineSequence().map { it.trim() }.filter { it.startsWith("run ") }.toList()
        if (lines.isEmpty()) return false
        return lines.all { line ->
            val detail = line.substringAfter(':').trim().lowercase()
            detail.contains("canceledexception") || detail.contains("backendinterrupted") ||
                detail.contains("interrupted")
        }

        if (lines.isEmpty()) return true
        return lines.all { line ->
            val detail = line.substringAfter(':', "").trim()

        killRequested.remove(taskId)

        val isMagnet = sourceUrl.startsWith("magnet:", ignoreCase = true)
        // When a rewritten master file is supplied, yt-dlp consumes that file
        // (file:// + --enable-file-urls) — the m3u8 branch still applies.
        val inputUrl = if (hlsMasterFile != null) "file://$hlsMasterFile" else sourceUrl
        val isM3u8 = inputUrl.lowercase().contains(".m3u8")
        val hlsSeparateAudio = masterDeclaresSeparateAudio(hlsMasterFile)
        // Token-locked HLS CDNs (vidsrc family, live-verified) reject segment
        // requests that carry ANY Referer with 403 while serving them fine
        // without one — and the rewritten playlist was validated exactly that
        // way. A rewritten master therefore runs referer-free, EXCEPT for the
        // anitaku CDNs (cdn.watching.onl / fntb0.anivideo.sbs) which are the
        // inverse: they 403 every request that does NOT carry exactly
        // https://megaplay.buzz/ (live-verified 2026-08-22).
        // Live-by-default HLS (2026-10-19) means the rewritten-master flag is
        // no longer the proxy for "token-locked CDN": the same referer policy
        // must apply to a LIVE m3u8 too. Hosts on the explicit allowlist keep
        // their referer; every other HLS referer is stripped exactly as the
        // rewritten-master path always did.
        val route = DynamicRulesManager.resolveEngine(sourceUrl)
        val keepRefererByRoute = route?.keepReferer == true
        val effReferer = if ((hlsMasterFile != null || isM3u8) &&
            !explicitReferer && !keepRefererByRoute && !requiresExplicitReferer(referer)
        ) "" else referer

        val height = quality.filter { it.isDigit() }.toIntOrNull() ?: when (quality.lowercase()) {
            "4k" -> 2160
            "sd" -> 480
            else -> 720
        }

        if (isMagnet) {
            // Selective-file pass: probe the swarm for its file list; when more
            // than one safe file exists, ask the UI which to download. A single
            // safe file is auto-selected (no picker). A failed probe (null)
            // falls back to the full download; a probe where EVERY file fails
            // the shield refuses the download entirely.
            var selectIndexes: List<Int>? = null
            if (onTorrentFiles != null) {
                val files = listTorrentFiles(context, sourceUrl, File(preferredFilename).nameWithoutExtension, privacyMode)
                if (files != null) {
                    val safe = files.filter { it.isSafe }
                    when {
                        safe.size > 1 -> {
                            when (val res = onTorrentFiles(files)) {
                                is com.anonrode.downloader.ui.screens.TorrentFilePicker.TorrentPickResult.Selected -> selectIndexes = res.indices
                                com.anonrode.downloader.ui.screens.TorrentFilePicker.TorrentPickResult.Cancelled -> throw kotlinx.coroutines.CancellationException("User cancelled torrent selection")
                            }
                        }
                        safe.size == 1 -> selectIndexes = listOf(safe.first().index)
                        // Probe succeeded but EVERY file failed the shield:
                        // surface the picker's warning state and refuse the
                        // legacy fallback — a silent full download here would
                        // fetch exactly the flagged payload.
                        else -> {
                            when (val res = onTorrentFiles(files)) {
                                is com.anonrode.downloader.ui.screens.TorrentFilePicker.TorrentPickResult.Selected -> {
                                    if (res.indices.isEmpty()) {
                                        throw SecurityException(
                                            "All ${files.size} file(s) blocked by security shield — download refused"
                                        )
                                    }
                                    selectIndexes = res.indices
                                }
                                com.anonrode.downloader.ui.screens.TorrentFilePicker.TorrentPickResult.Cancelled -> throw kotlinx.coroutines.CancellationException("User cancelled torrent selection")
                            }
                        }
                    }
                    if (safe.size != files.size) {
                        android.util.Log.w("AnonDownload",
                            "listTorrentFiles: ${files.size - safe.size} of ${files.size} entries blocked by shield")
                    }
                }
            }
            // isActiveCheck keeps the task-level retry loop from relaunching
            // aria2c after the user paused or cancelled the job. Named arg:
            // speedLimitKbs is now the last parameter, so a trailing lambda
            // would no longer bind to isActiveCheck.
            return downloadMagnetAria2c(
                context, taskId, sourceUrl, targetDir, preferredFilename, parallelSockets, onProgress,
                selectIndexes = selectIndexes,
                maxAttempts = magnetMaxAttempts,
                peersOverride = torrentPeers,
                speedLimitKbs = speedLimitKbs,
                privacyMode = privacyMode,
                isActiveCheck = { coroutineContext.isActive },
                estimatedTotal = estimatedTotal
            )
        }

        // Direct HTTP downloads explicitly routed to aria2c (CDNs, movie lockers, etc.).
        // Native aria2c executable handles HTTP downloads directly. On failure the
        // exception propagates to the engine, which owns the park/fail/retry decision.
        if (backend.equals("aria2c", true) && !isM3u8 && !isExtractorTask) {
            val aria2Exec = findAria2Executable(context)
            if (aria2Exec != null) {
                try {
                    val file = downloadHttpAria2c(
                        context = context,
                        taskId = taskId,
                        url = sourceUrl,
                        targetDir = targetDir,
                        preferredFilename = preferredFilename,
                        referer = referer,
                        origin = origin,
                        ua = if (ua.isNotBlank()) ua else com.anonrode.downloader.data.net.HttpClient.DEFAULT_UA,
                        customHeaders = customHeaders,
                        parallelSockets = parallelSockets,
                        speedLimitKbs = speedLimitKbs,
                        maxAttempts = ytdlpMaxAttempts,
                        onProgress = onProgress,
                        isActiveCheck = { coroutineContext.isActive },
                        estimatedTotal = estimatedTotal
                    )
                    if (file != null) return file
                } catch (ce: CancellationException) {
                    throw ce
                } catch (e: Exception) {
                    com.anonrode.downloader.util.DebugLog.backend(
                        "task=$taskId aria2c HTTP failed (${e.message})"
                    )
                    // aria2c failures must reach the engine's park/fail classifier with
                    // their HTTP status intact (the 429/403 message powers
                    // isRateLimitedError and parkInsteadOfFail); swallowing them into a
                    // null return hid throttling and expiry errors from that logic.
                    throw e
                }
            }
        }

        // The yt-dlp/ffmpeg runtime initializes in the app's background
        // bootstrap (AnonApp.appScope): a yt-dlp task enqueued before that
        // finishes would otherwise burn its first attempt on an uninitialized
        // runtime. Magnets above run aria2c directly and don't need it.
        if (!com.anonrode.downloader.AnonApp.ensureReady()) {
            throw java.io.IOException("yt-dlp runtime is not initialized")
        }

        // Extractor tasks (social/YouTube, where yt-dlp picks its own output
        // name) write into a PRIVATE workdir instead of the shared target
        // folder. Two YouTube jobs downloading into Social/YouTube/ at the
        // same time used to count each other's .part files in the engine's
        // disk-progress scan (task 2's first sample read 33 MB at t+2s — task
        // 1's bytes), which then fired phantom watchdog kills
        // (window=-145334KiB) the moment the sibling completed and renamed
        // its parts away. The produced artifact is moved to the real target
        // folder after a successful run; the engine's computeDiskBytes scans
        // the workdir while it exists.
        val outDir = if (isExtractorTask) File(targetDir, ".work-$taskId").apply { mkdirs() } else targetDir

        val request = YoutubeDLRequest(inputUrl).apply {
            if (hlsMasterFile != null) {
                // The input is our own rewritten playlist file in the app cache.
                addOption("--enable-file-urls")
            }
            if (isExtractorTask) {
                // If caller provided a specific preferredFilename (movies / TV show episodes),
                // use that clean filename stem instead of yt-dlp's generic extractor metadata
                // which can produce garbage like "RBNNj1sIT2 [id].unknown_video".
                // %(title)s [%(id)s] is reserved for social video downloads where the title
                // is unknown in advance.
                val isGenericName = isGenericPreferredName(preferredFilename)
                val outTemplate = if (!isGenericName) {
                    val stem = File(outDir, preferredFilename.substringBeforeLast('.')).absolutePath
                    if (audioOnly) {
                        "$stem.%(ext)s"
                    } else {
                        val ext = File(preferredFilename).extension.ifBlank { "mp4" }
                        val safeExt = if (ext.equals("matroska", ignoreCase = true)) "mkv" else ext
                        "$stem.$safeExt"
                    }
                } else {
                    File(outDir, "%(title).100s [%(id)s].%(ext)s").absolutePath
                }
                addOption("-o", outTemplate)
                if (audioOnly) {
                    addOption("-f", "bestaudio/best")
                    addOption("--extract-audio")
                    addOption("--audio-format", "mp3")
                    addOption("--audio-quality", "0")
                    addOption("--write-thumbnail")
                    addOption("--convert-thumbnails", "jpg")
                    addOption("--embed-thumbnail")
                    addOption("--embed-metadata")
                } else {
                    addCommands(hlsFormatOptions(height, hlsSeparateAudio))
                    addOption("-S", "height~$height,+size,+br,abr")
                    addOption("--merge-output-format", "mp4")
                    if (downloadSubs) {
                        // Seal parity (2026-09-14): manual AND auto-generated
                        // captions for the configured language, normalized to
                        // SRT (mp4 mov_text) and embedded by the bundled
                        // ffmpeg during the merge pass — the artifact stays a
                        // single file, so the workdir move logic and the
                        // gallery scan never learn about sidecars. Videos
                        // without subtitles are unaffected (yt-dlp just
                        // reports "no subtitles" and moves on).
                        addOption("--write-subs")
                        addOption("--write-auto-subs")
                        addOption("--sub-langs", subLang.ifBlank { "en" })
                        addOption("--convert-subs", "srt")
                        addOption("--embed-subs")
                    }
                }
                addOption("--no-playlist")
                // Embed/watch-page cracks (nepu, social, etc.) often resolve to HLS.
                // Parallel fragments keep multi-socket speed instead of a single
                // rate-capped connection.
                // Floor 1, ceiling 16; per-host caps arrive pre-applied through
                // HostPolicyRegistry (6/12 on the sensitive lockers, OTA-tunable
                // via contentPolicy.socketCaps) and — after Fix 6b — the HLS
                // path applies the host cap too (minOf below).
                // Fix 6b: host caps must bind on the HLS/extractor path too —
                // hlsFragments > 0 is always true from the engine, which used
                // to bypass every per-host socket cap entirely.
                val hostCap = HostPolicyRegistry.effectiveSocketsForUrl(sourceUrl, 16)
                val rawFrags = if (hlsFragments > 0) hlsFragments else parallelSockets
                val frags = minOf(rawFrags.coerceIn(1, 16), hostCap)
                addOption("-N", "$frags")
                addOption("--concurrent-fragments", "$frags")
                addOption("--buffer-size", "1M")
                // No --http-chunk-size here: FragmentFD already issues one
                // request per fragment, so a 2M chunk was inert at best and
                // an extra range-split at worst. Kept on the direct-HTTP
                // branch below where HttpFD actually consumes it.
                // P-3: monolith fragment patience (exp backoff through
                // replenishment windows instead of the old 5×1s ladder).
                addCommands(hlsFragmentPatienceFlags())
                if (speedLimitKbs > 0) addOption("--limit-rate", "${speedLimitKbs}K")
            } else if (isM3u8) {
                // HLS m3u8 stream variant selection with multi-fragment parallel downloading
                val stem = File(outDir, preferredFilename.substringBeforeLast('.')).absolutePath
                val safeExt = File(preferredFilename).extension.ifBlank { "mp4" }
                if (audioOnly) {
                    addOption("-o", "$stem.%(ext)s")
                    addOption("-f", "bestaudio/best")
                    addOption("--extract-audio")
                    addOption("--audio-format", "mp3")
                    addOption("--audio-quality", "0")
                    addOption("--write-thumbnail")
                    addOption("--convert-thumbnails", "jpg")
                    addOption("--embed-thumbnail")
                    addOption("--embed-metadata")
                } else {
                    addOption("-o", "$stem.$safeExt")
                    addCommands(hlsFormatOptions(height, hlsSeparateAudio))
                    addOption("-S", "height~$height,+size,+br")
                    addOption("--merge-output-format", "mp4")
                }
                addOption("--no-playlist")
                // Fix 6b: host caps must bind on the HLS/extractor path too —
                // hlsFragments > 0 is always true from the engine, which used
                // to bypass every per-host socket cap entirely.
                val hostCap = HostPolicyRegistry.effectiveSocketsForUrl(sourceUrl, 16)
                val rawFrags = if (hlsFragments > 0) hlsFragments else parallelSockets
                val frags = minOf(rawFrags.coerceIn(1, 16), hostCap)
                addOption("-N", "$frags")
                addOption("--concurrent-fragments", "$frags")
                addOption("--buffer-size", "1M")
                // No --http-chunk-size here: FragmentFD already issues one
                // request per fragment, so a 2M chunk was inert at best and
                // an extra range-split at worst. Kept on the direct-HTTP
                // branch below where HttpFD actually consumes it.
                // P-3: monolith fragment patience (see
                // hlsFragmentPatienceFlags / downloader.py:3576-3579).
                addCommands(hlsFragmentPatienceFlags())
                if (speedLimitKbs > 0) addOption("--limit-rate", "${speedLimitKbs}K")
            } else {
                // Direct CDN HTTP fallback via yt-dlp native chunked engine
                val stem = File(outDir, preferredFilename.substringBeforeLast('.')).absolutePath
                val ext = File(preferredFilename).extension.ifBlank { "mp4" }
                val safeExt = if (audioOnly) "mp3" else if (ext.equals("matroska", ignoreCase = true)) "mkv" else ext
                if (audioOnly) {
                    addOption("-o", "$stem.%(ext)s")
                    addOption("-f", "bestaudio/best")
                    addOption("--extract-audio")
                    addOption("--audio-format", "mp3")
                    addOption("--audio-quality", "0")
                    addOption("--write-thumbnail")
                    addOption("--convert-thumbnails", "jpg")
                    addOption("--embed-thumbnail")
                    addOption("--embed-metadata")
                } else {
                    addOption("-o", "$stem.$safeExt")
                }
                val conns = parallelSockets.coerceIn(1, 16)
                addOption("-N", "$conns")
                addOption("--concurrent-fragments", "$conns")
                addOption("--buffer-size", "1M")
                addOption("--http-chunk-size", "2M")
                addOption("--socket-timeout", "15")
                addOption("--retries", "10")
                if (speedLimitKbs > 0) addOption("--limit-rate", "${speedLimitKbs}K")
            }

            addOption("--no-mtime")
            addOption("--no-warnings")
            if (HostPolicyRegistry.allowsPermissiveTlsFallback(sourceUrl) ||
                DynamicRulesManager.isPermissiveTls(sourceUrl)
            ) {
                addOption("--no-check-certificate")
            }
            // --no-restrict-filenames: yt-dlp refuses "unusual" extensions like
            // .mkv by default ("The extracted extension ('matroska') is unusual
            // and will be skipped for safety reasons" — fired 8 times on
            // naijavault→vikingfile .mkv URLs in app-2026-08-29 / 09-01, all
            // returning 0 bytes after the engine had already burned 3-6 minutes
            // cracking the locker URL). Disabling is safe: we always write to
            // our own sanitized path, never to a location derived from the
            // remote filename.
            addOption("--no-restrict-filenames")
            // Remap unsafe/unusual extensions extracted from remote headers (e.g. Content-Type: video/matroska
            // -> ext='matroska', or Content-Type: application/octet-stream -> ext='unknown_video') before
            // yt-dlp's _catch_unsafe_extension_error skips the download.
            addCommands(listOf("--replace-in-metadata", "ext", "(?i)matroska", "mkv"))
            addCommands(listOf("--replace-in-metadata", "ext", "(?i)unknown_video", "mp4"))
            addOption("--newline")
            addOption("--progress")
            // Refuse outside config files: a stray yt-dlp.conf could override
            // -o/-f and silently break the output path (monolith parity).
            addOption("--ignore-config")

            // Cookies support: if user has provided cookies.txt in app storage,
            // forward to yt-dlp so authenticated platforms (Instagram, etc.) succeed.
            val cookieFile = File(context.filesDir, "cookies.txt").takeIf { it.exists() && it.length() > 0 }
                ?: File(context.getExternalFilesDir(null), "cookies.txt").takeIf { it.exists() && it.length() > 0 }
            if (cookieFile != null) {
                addOption("--cookies", cookieFile.absolutePath)
            }

            // --progress-template: emit one templated progress line per tick,
            // parsed by ProgressParser's YTDL_TEMPLATE_REGEX.  Two templates
            // are emitted (yt-dlp allows multiple) — the first mirrors
            // yt-dlp's native "[download] X% of Y at Z" format so the
            // existing YTDL_REGEX keeps matching unchanged (belt-and-
            // suspenders for any download where the structured fields
            // fall back to "NA").  The second carries structured fields
            // (percent, speed, eta, fragment_index, fragment_count,
            // downloaded_bytes, total_bytes, total_bytes_estimate) needed
            // for HLS / segmented downloads where the native line is
            // fragment-internal and the engine's existing YTDL_REGEX
            // never matched (dramakey / wetafiles symptom: "Starting..."
            // for 90s, then BAM "DONE").  The @@DLP@@ sentinel is the
            // same one the Python monolith uses.
            addOption(
                "--progress-template",
                "download:[download]  %(progress._percent_str)s of ~%(progress._total_bytes_str)s at %(progress._speed_str)s ETA %(progress._eta_str)s"
            )
            addOption(
                "--progress-template",
                "download:@@DLP@@ %(progress._percent_str)s|%(progress._speed_str)s|%(progress._eta_str)s|%(progress.fragment_index)s|%(progress.fragment_count)s|%(progress._downloaded_bytes_str)s|%(progress._total_bytes_str)s|%(progress._total_bytes_estimate_str)s"
            )
            // Origin header from the referer's base domain, like the monolith's
            // HLS path always sends it.
            val originToPass = origin.ifBlank {
                effReferer.takeIf { it.isNotBlank() }?.let { r ->
                    Regex("""https?://[^/]+""").find(r)?.value ?: ""
                } ?: ""
            }

            val snapshot = DynamicRulesManager.getSnapshot()
            val profileName = route?.profile ?: "default"
            val profileArgs = snapshot.ytdlpProfiles[profileName]?.args
                ?: snapshot.ytdlpProfiles["default"]?.args

            val isHlsOrExtractor = isExtractorTask || isM3u8
            val effectiveFrags = if (isHlsOrExtractor) {
                val hostCap = HostPolicyRegistry.effectiveSocketsForUrl(sourceUrl, 16)
                val rawFrags = if (hlsFragments > 0) hlsFragments else parallelSockets
                minOf(rawFrags.coerceIn(1, 16), hostCap)
            } else {
                parallelSockets.coerceIn(1, 16)
            }

            if (profileArgs != null && profileArgs.isNotEmpty()) {
                val vars = mapOf(
                    "user_agent" to ua.trim(),
                    "referer" to effReferer.trim(),
                    "origin" to originToPass.trim(),
                    "concurrent_fragments" to effectiveFrags.toString()
                )
                for (group in profileArgs) {
                    val resolved = DynamicRulesManager.resolveCliArgs(listOf(group), vars)
                    val filtered = if (isHlsOrExtractor) {
                        resolved.filter { arg ->
                            arg != "--skip-unavailable-fragments" &&
                            arg != "--no-part" &&
                            arg != "--hls-use-mpegts"
                        }
                    } else {
                        resolved.filter { arg -> arg != "--no-part" }
                    }
                    if (filtered.isNotEmpty()) {
                        addCommands(filtered)
                    }
                }
            } else {
                if (effReferer.isNotBlank()) addOption("--referer", effReferer)
                if (ua.isNotBlank()) addOption("--user-agent", ua)
                if (originToPass.isNotBlank()) {
                    val cleanOrig = originToPass.replace("\r", "").replace("\n", "").trim()
                    if (cleanOrig.isNotBlank()) addOption("--add-header", "Origin: $cleanOrig")
                }
            }

            val profileHeaders = snapshot.ytdlpProfiles[profileName]?.headers.orEmpty()
