                }
                ProbeResult.HtmlPage -> {
                    return@withContext TurboResult.Failure(
                        httpStatus = null,
                        message = "Server returned an HTML page instead of a media file",
                        htmlPage = true
                    )
                }
                is ProbeResult.HttpError -> {
                    // Terminal verdict: hand the code to the engine immediately
                    // (its self-heal/park logic keys on 401/403/404/410/429).
                    return@withContext TurboResult.Failure(
                        httpStatus = probe.code,
                        message = probe.message,
                        htmlPage = false
                    )
                }
                is ProbeResult.Unreachable -> {
                    total = probe.total
                    acceptsRanges = false
                }
            }

            val sockets = HostPolicyRegistry.effectiveSocketsForUrl(safe, configuredSockets)
            val useSegmented = acceptsRanges && total > MIN_SEGMENTED_SIZE && sockets > 1

            val partFile = File(dest.absolutePath + ".part")
            val turboSidecar = File(dest.absolutePath + ".turbo")
            val state = TurboState(turboSidecar)
            val failureStatus = AtomicInteger(0)
            val failureMessage = AtomicReference<String?>(null)

            if (useSegmented) {
                // Defense in depth (audit finding 1): a .turbo without its .part
                // means the plan's offsets describe bytes that are no longer in
                // this .part — a sidecar-driven resume would skip those ranges
                // and zero-fill them. A stale plan can never be trusted here;
                // delete it and start a fresh plan (correctness over redo).
                if (!partFile.exists() && turboSidecar.exists()) {
                    TurboState(turboSidecar).delete()
                }
                val ok = segmented(
                    safe, partFile, headers, total, sockets, state,
                    failureStatus, failureMessage, onProgress, effectiveClient, taskId
                )
                if (ok) {
                    state.delete()
                    if (moveVerified(partFile, dest, total)) {
                        TurboResult.Success(dest, dest.length(), true)
                    } else {
                        failure(failureStatus, failureMessage)
                    }
                } else {
                    val landedBytes = state.writtenBytes() ?: 0L
                    val canFallbackToSingle = canCommit(taskId) && coroutineContext.isActive &&
                        (!partFile.exists() || partFile.length() == 0L || landedBytes == 0L)
                    if (canFallbackToSingle) {
                        partFile.delete()
                        state.delete()
                        if (single(safe, partFile, headers, total, failureStatus, failureMessage, onProgress, effectiveClient, taskId)) {
                            if (moveVerified(partFile, dest, total)) {
                                TurboResult.Success(dest, dest.length(), false)
                            } else {
                                failure(failureStatus, failureMessage)
                            }
                        } else {
                            failure(failureStatus, failureMessage)
                        }
                    } else {
                        failure(failureStatus, failureMessage)
                    }
                }
            } else {
                // BUG FIX (Cross-Mode Resume): If transitioning from a pre-allocated segmented
                // `.part` file to single-stream mode, truncate `.part` to the contiguous prefix
                // AND immediately delete the `.turbo` sidecar so future resumes do not re-truncate
                // newly appended single-stream bytes!
                if (partFile.exists() && partFile.length() > 0L && turboSidecar.exists()) {
                    val prefix = state.contiguousPrefixBytes() ?: 0L
                    try {
                        if (prefix < partFile.length()) {
                            RandomAccessFile(partFile, "rw").use { it.setLength(prefix) }
                        }
                        state.delete()
                    } catch (e: Exception) {
                        partFile.delete()
                        state.delete()
                    }
                }
                if (single(safe, partFile, headers, total, failureStatus, failureMessage, onProgress, effectiveClient, taskId)) {
                    state.delete()
                    if (moveVerified(partFile, dest, total)) {
                        TurboResult.Success(dest, dest.length(), false)
                    } else {
                        failure(failureStatus, failureMessage)
                    }
                } else {
                    failure(failureStatus, failureMessage)
                }
            }
        } finally {
            if (taskId.isNotBlank()) {
                activeCalls.remove(taskId)
                fullyCancelledTaskIds.remove(taskId)
            }
        }
    }

    /**
     * Move the verified .part to its final name and PROVE the move landed.
     * [atomicMove]'s return value used to be ignored, so a failed rename
     * (and a copy fallback killed mid-way, e.g. by disk-full) still reported
     * Success — handing the engine a missing or truncated file that the
     * structure tier could bless (faststart MP4 keeps its moov atom at the
     * head, so a truncated file scans as "structured"). With the length
     * known (Content-Length from the probe), only a byte-exact dest counts;
     * with no known length, existence is all the evidence there is.
     */
    private fun moveVerified(partFile: File, dest: File, total: Long): Boolean {
        if (!atomicMove(partFile, dest)) return false
        if (!dest.exists()) return false
        return total <= 0L || dest.length() == total
    }

    /** Builds a Failure outcome, rethrowing cancellation so a paused job never looks like a server error. */
    private suspend fun failure(status: AtomicInteger, message: AtomicReference<String?>): TurboResult.Failure {
        coroutineContext.ensureActive()
        val code = status.get()
        return TurboResult.Failure(code.takeIf { it != 0 }, message.get() ?: "Download failed")
    }

    /**
     * Single-round-trip fast probe (1DM): the first request is a ranged GET
     * (bytes=0-1023 + Accept-Encoding: identity) returning status, total size,
     * range support AND the first bytes for a best-effort media sniff in ONE
     * round trip. Header verdicts decide first; HEAD remains a fallback for
     * non-206/200 answers (e.g. a rate-limited range server whose HEAD still
     * answers 200 + Accept-Ranges). Decision table validated in
     * scratch/test_probe_logic.py before this port.
     */
    private fun probe(url: String, headers: Map<String, String>, client: OkHttpClient, onFailure: (Throwable) -> Unit = {}): ProbeResult {
        fun buildGet() = Request.Builder().url(url).apply {
            header("User-Agent", headers["User-Agent"] ?: HttpClient.DEFAULT_UA)
            headers.forEach { (k, v) -> if (!k.equals("User-Agent", true)) header(k, v) }
            header("Range", "bytes=0-1023")
            header("Accept-Encoding", "identity")
        }.build()

        fun buildHead() = Request.Builder().url(url).apply {
            header("User-Agent", headers["User-Agent"] ?: HttpClient.DEFAULT_UA)
            headers.forEach { (k, v) -> if (!k.equals("User-Agent", true)) header(k, v) }
            head()
        }.build()

        fun isHtmlPage(contentType: String?): Boolean {
            val ct = contentType?.lowercase() ?: return false
            return ct.startsWith("text/html") || ct.startsWith("application/xhtml")
        }

        fun sniffHead(r: okhttp3.Response): Boolean {
            val head = try {
                r.peekBody(1024).bytes()
            } catch (_: Exception) {
                null // mid-body disconnect: never invalidates a header verdict
            }
            return head != null && head.isNotEmpty() &&
                com.anonrode.downloader.pipeline.StreamValidator.sniff(head) != null
        }

        fun headFallback(carried: Long): ProbeResult {
            var total = carried
            try {
                // Registered so pause/cancel kills the probe too.
                HttpClient.executeRegistered(client.newCall(buildHead())).use { r ->
                    val ct = r.header("Content-Type")
                    val len = r.header("Content-Length")?.toLongOrNull() ?: -1L
                    val ranges = r.header("Accept-Ranges")?.contains("bytes", true) == true
                    if (r.isSuccessful && len > 0 && !isHtmlPage(ct)) {
                        total = len
                        if (ranges) return ProbeResult.File(total, true)
                    }
                }
            } catch (cancelled: CancellationException) {
                throw cancelled
            } catch (e: Exception) {
                onFailure(e)
            }
            return ProbeResult.Unreachable(total)
        }

        // 1. Ranged GET first — one round trip for status + total + sniff.
        var getStatus: Int? = null
        try {
            HttpClient.executeRegistered(client.newCall(buildGet())).use { r ->
                getStatus = r.code
                val ct = r.header("Content-Type")
                if (isHtmlPage(ct)) return ProbeResult.HtmlPage

                val cr = r.header("Content-Range")
                val totalFromCr = cr?.substringAfter('/')?.trim()?.toLongOrNull() ?: -1L
                val lenHeader = r.header("Content-Length")?.toLongOrNull() ?: -1L

                if (r.code == 206 && totalFromCr > 0) {
                    // Header-proven range support: sniff is best-effort AFTER the
                    // verdict — a body read failure must not discard it
                    // (TurboDownloaderTest.givesUpAfterMaxAttempts).
                    if (sniffHead(r)) return ProbeResult.HtmlPage
                    return ProbeResult.File(totalFromCr, true)
                }
                if (r.code == 200 && lenHeader > 0) {
                    if (sniffHead(r)) return ProbeResult.HtmlPage
                    return ProbeResult.File(lenHeader, false)
                }
                // Deliberately NO carry of Content-Length/Content-Range from
                // error or unusable responses (audit finding 2): an error
                // page's byte length must never become the tracked total.
            }
        } catch (cancelled: CancellationException) {
            throw cancelled
        } catch (e: Exception) {
            onFailure(e)
        }

        // 2. HEAD fallback for non-206/200 answers (416/429/403/...) and for
        // responses that did not advertise a usable length — ONE try only.
        // Directive Fix 2, corrected: a 429 whose HEAD still answers 200 +
        // Accept-Ranges keeps the segmented path alive (that is the
        // RateLimitedRangeServer storm-survival constraint); only when HEAD is
        // also unusable does the probe fast-fail.
        val hb = headFallback(-1L)
        if (hb is ProbeResult.File) return hb
        val code = getStatus
        if (code != null) {
            if (code == 429) {
                com.anonrode.downloader.pipeline.HostHealth.recordFail(
                    url, rateLimited = true, reason = "HTTP 429 in Turbo probe"
                )
                return ProbeResult.HttpError(429, "Server rate limited request (HTTP 429)")
            }
            if (code in listOf(401, 403, 404, 410)) {
                return ProbeResult.HttpError(code, "Server rejected link (HTTP $code)")
            }
            // 5xx deliberately falls through to Unreachable: the full
            // 5-attempt retry ladder must stay reachable
            // (TurboDownloaderTest.givesUpAfterMaxAttempts).
        }
        return hb
    }

    private suspend fun segmented(
        url: String,
        dest: File,
        headers: Map<String, String>,
        total: Long,
        sockets: Int,
        state: TurboState,
        failureStatus: AtomicInteger,
        failureMessage: AtomicReference<String?>,
        onProgress: (Long, Long, Long) -> Unit,
        client: OkHttpClient,
        taskId: String = ""
    ): Boolean = coroutineScope {
            // Work-stealing appends split pieces mid-run (Fix 3). CopyOnWrite
            // makes every append atomically visible to concurrent commits and
            // telemetry without wrapping a dozen call sites in synchronized —
            // the steal DECISION itself still runs under synchronized(plan)
            // so two workers can never split the same victim.
            val plan = CopyOnWriteArrayList(state.loadOrCreate(total, sockets))
        // Post-admission growth ceiling: the controller may raise this task's
        // grant, but never past the per-host policy.
        val hostCeiling = HostPolicyRegistry.effectiveSocketsForUrl(url, 16)
        val initialBytes = plan.sumOf { (it.current - it.start).coerceAtLeast(0L) }
        val done = AtomicLong(initialBytes)
            val failed = AtomicBoolean(false)
            val nextPiece = AtomicInteger(0)
            var dynamicSplits = 0  // work-steal splits this run (Fix 3 budget)
            // Best window throughput seen by ANY lane this run — the relative
            // drop guard: a lane is dropped only when slow BOTH absolutely
            // (< DROP_FLOOR_BPS) and relatively (< 30% of the best sibling
            // window), so a uniformly-slow link (live-verified at ~6-9 KB/s
            // total on the maintainer connection) never churns lanes and never
            // wastes multi-second handshakes. Shared-best scenarios validated
            // in scratch/test_drop_replace.py.
            val bestWindowBps = AtomicReference(BestSample(0L, 0L))
        // Rate-limit coordination: one shared cooldown deadline every socket
        // sits out (the limiter is per-IP — only a PAUSE heals it; retrying
        // now deepens it), a cycle counter driving the escalating ladder, and
        // a worker cap halved per cycle; the shared piece queue lets the
        // survivors drain everything the departed workers would have claimed.
        val throttleUntil = AtomicLong(0L)
        val throttleCycles = AtomicInteger(0)
        // Startup ramp state (fresh tasks only). `sockets` is the admission
        // grant; the ramp may grow to the per-host ceiling as the global
        // controller rebalances (growth is consumed at piece boundaries).
        fun laneGrant(): Int {
            if (taskId.isBlank()) return sockets
            val grant = HostPolicyRegistry.LaneBudget.grantFor(taskId)
            return if (grant > 0) minOf(grant, hostCeiling) else sockets
        }
        val freshStart = initialBytes == 0L
        // Warm standby (board row 5): one pre-dialed spare per active task.
        // Its slot is subtracted BEFORE any lane starts, so active lanes +
        // the idle spare can never exceed min(per-host cap, lane grant).
        // A host whose session occupancy is down to one socket gets no spare.
        val initialOccupancy = HostPolicyRegistry.HostSocketOccupancy.currentForUrl(url, hostCeiling)
        val standbyEnabled = StandbyPolicy.standbyAllowed(
            hostCeiling,
            minOf(laneGrant(), initialOccupancy)
        )
        // Adaptive occupancy (B2): the host's session memory is the THIRD cap
        // after the static host policy and the global lane grant. It starts at
        // the host cap and is lowered/raised by HostSocketOccupancy; reading it
        // here keeps every claim site on the live value.
        fun workerCeiling(): Int {
            val occupancy = HostPolicyRegistry.HostSocketOccupancy
                .currentForUrl(url, hostCeiling)
            val total = minOf(hostCeiling, laneGrant(), occupancy)
            return StandbyPolicy.activeWorkerBudgetForTotal(total, standbyEnabled)
        }
        val workerBudget = workerCeiling()
        val standby = if (standbyEnabled) {
            StandbySocket(
                url = url,
                headers = headers,
                baseClient = client,
                taskId = taskId,
                track = { call -> trackCall(taskId, call) },
                untrack = { call -> untrackCall(taskId, call) }
            )
        } else null
        val maxWorkers = AtomicInteger(workerBudget)
        // Speed-first startup (B2): open the task at its allowed width (host
        // cap bounded by the lane grant and adaptive occupancy) instead of
        // ramping up from 4. The expected-default case only enters this branch
        // when the grant itself is narrow.
        val rampStart = minOf(sockets, workerBudget)
        val activeWorkers = AtomicInteger(rampStart)
        val rampStartedAt = System.currentTimeMillis()
        val sawFirstByte = AtomicBoolean(false)
        val sawFirstMegabyte = AtomicBoolean(false)
        if (freshStart && taskId.isNotEmpty()) {
            com.anonrode.downloader.util.DebugLog.backend(
                "task=$taskId lane start=$rampStart cap=$hostCeiling " +
                    "occupancy=$initialOccupancy standby=${if (standbyEnabled) 1 else 0} total=0KB/s"
            )
        }
        fun enterRateLimit() {
            val cycle = throttleCycles.incrementAndGet()
            val waitMs = (throttleBaseDelayMs shl (cycle - 1).coerceAtMost(5)).coerceAtMost(THROTTLE_MAX_MS)
            val until = System.currentTimeMillis() + waitMs
            throttleUntil.set(until)
            if (taskId.isNotEmpty()) throttleDeadlines[taskId] = until
            // B2 fast backoff: halve the host's remembered occupancy NOW (a
            // 429/503 is the host telling us the request width is too high).
            val occupancy = HostPolicyRegistry.HostSocketOccupancy
                .recordBackoff(url, hostCeiling)
            maxWorkers.set(maxOf(2, maxWorkers.get() / 2))
            com.anonrode.downloader.util.DebugLog.backend(
                "task=$taskId rate limited (cycle $cycle): all sockets cooling ${waitMs / 1000}s, " +
                    "workers→${maxWorkers.get()} occupancy→$occupancy"
            )
        }

        RandomAccessFile(dest, "rw").use { raf ->
            if (raf.length() != total) raf.setLength(total)
        }

        val speed = SpeedMeter(initialBytes)
        // Progress truth = bytes committed to the file, NOT bytes received.
        // `done` counts every socket's reads; with out-of-order pieces the
        // received total runs ahead of what the resume map holds — the Suits
        // download (activity-log-share-5) showed the bar pinned at 100% for
        // 2+ minutes while one slow socket still held the committed prefix
        // 60 MiB short. The engine's watchdog disk feed (computeDiskBytes)
        // reads exactly this sidecar sum, so reporting it here keeps the bar,
        // the watchdog and a future resume all on the same number. Speed
        // still samples `done`: displayed speed is the real transfer rate.
        fun committed(): Long = plan.sumOf { (it.current - it.start).coerceAtLeast(0L) }
        onProgress(initialBytes, total, 0L)

        // Adaptive occupancy (B2): aggregate goodput is sampled every few
        // seconds and feeds the per-host controller. Recovery is deliberately
        // slow (+1 lane per two consecutive improving samples) and every
        // raise is clamped by the lane grant, host cap and standby slot.
        var lastAdaptAt = System.currentTimeMillis()
        fun adaptFromGoodput(bps: Double) {
            if (taskId.isBlank()) return
            val previous = HostPolicyRegistry.HostSocketOccupancy.currentForUrl(url, hostCeiling)
            val occupancy = HostPolicyRegistry.HostSocketOccupancy.recordGoodput(url, hostCeiling, bps, taskId)
            val total = minOf(hostCeiling, laneGrant(), occupancy)
            val target = StandbyPolicy.activeWorkerBudgetForTotal(total, standbyEnabled)
            val targetAboveWidth = target > activeWorkers.get()
            val occupancyGrew = occupancy > previous
            if (targetAboveWidth) activeWorkers.set(target)
            // A recovery may undo the rate-limit worker halving — but ONLY on
            // evidence that the host's occupancy actually grew. Comparing
            // against activeWorkers alone never restores maxWorkers after a
            // throttle cycle (active was not lowered by it), which would pin
            // the task at the halved width for the rest of the run. The
            // throttle ladder's cooldown deadline is untouched.
            if (occupancyGrew && target > maxWorkers.get()) {
                maxWorkers.set(
                    HostPolicyRegistry.HostSocketOccupancy.recoveryMaxWorkers(
                        currentMax = maxWorkers.get(),
                        target = target,
                        occupancyGrew = true
                    )
                )
            }
            if (targetAboveWidth || occupancyGrew) {
                com.anonrode.downloader.util.DebugLog.backend(
                    "task=$taskId lane adapt occupancy=$occupancy target=$target " +
                        "workers=${activeWorkers.get()}/${maxWorkers.get()} " +
                        "total=${(bps / 1024).toInt()}KB/s"
                )
            }
        }

        // Decoupled Telemetry Dispatcher: Ticks every 250ms with smoothed EMA speed
        val telemetryTicker = launch(Dispatchers.Default) {
            while (isActive) {
                delay(250)
                val currentDone = done.get()
                val currentSpeed = speed.sample(currentDone)
                if (taskId.isNotEmpty()) {
                    HostPolicyRegistry.LaneBudget.reportSpeed(taskId, currentSpeed.toDouble())
                    val now = System.currentTimeMillis()
                    if (now - lastAdaptAt >= ADAPT_SAMPLE_MS) {
                        lastAdaptAt = now
                        adaptFromGoodput(currentSpeed.toDouble())
                    }
                }
                onProgress(committed(), total, currentSpeed)
            }
        }

        try {
            RandomAccessFile(dest, "rw").use { raf ->
                val channel: FileChannel = raf.channel

                // Shared piece queue (BitTorrent style): workers pull the next
                // unfinished piece. When every initial piece is claimed, a free
                // worker STEALS: it splits the active piece with the largest
                // remaining range in half and takes the back half (directive
                // Fix 3, "hurry up"). Threshold/budget corrected per
                // scratch/test_work_steal.py: 512 KiB minimum remainder (pieces
                // are 1 MiB, so a 2 MiB threshold could never fire) and the cap
                // counts SPLITS (initial plans hold up to 2048 pieces).
                fun claimOrStealNext(): TurboChunk? {
                    while (true) {
                        val idx = nextPiece.getAndIncrement()
                        if (idx >= plan.size) break
                        val c = plan[idx]
                        if (c.current <= c.end) return c
                    }
                    synchronized(plan) {
                        if (dynamicSplits >= MAX_DYNAMIC_SPLITS) return null
                        var victim: TurboChunk? = null
                        var victimRemaining = 0L
                        for (c in plan) {
                            if (c.current <= c.end) {
                                val remaining = c.end - c.current + 1L
                                if (remaining >= STEAL_MIN_REMAINING_BYTES && remaining > victimRemaining) {
                                    victim = c
                                    victimRemaining = remaining
                                }
                            }
                        }
                        val v = victim ?: return null
                        val splitOffset = v.current + victimRemaining / 2L
                        if (splitOffset <= v.current || splitOffset > v.end) return null
                        val oldEnd = v.end
                        v.end = splitOffset - 1L
                        val stolen = TurboChunk(start = splitOffset, end = oldEnd, current = splitOffset)
                        plan.add(stolen)
                        dynamicSplits++
                        com.anonrode.downloader.util.DebugLog.backend(
                            "task=$taskId work-steal split piece=${v.start}-$oldEnd -> victimEnds=${v.end} stolen=${stolen.start}-${stolen.end}"
                        )
                        return stolen
                    }
                }

                /**
                 * Download one piece. NETWORK failures follow the normal
                 * policy: 5 attempts with exponential backoff, each retry
                 * re-requesting from the piece's committed offset so a mid-body
                 * drop resumes instead of restarting. RATE-LIMIT answers
                 * (429/503) never consume an attempt — they park the whole
                 * socket pool in the shared cooldown (enterRateLimit) and the
                 * piece retries after the host calmed down. The global failure
                 * flag is only set once a piece exhausts attempts on REAL
                 * failures, so a single hiccup never aborts the siblings.
                 */
                suspend fun downloadPiece(chunk: TurboChunk): Boolean {
                    var attempt = 0
                    // Drop-and-replace state is PER PIECE (survives retries);
                    // semantics validated in scratch/test_drop_replace.py.
                    var drops = 0
                    var slowAfterDrop = 0
                    var noMoreDrops = false
                    var lastConnWasPostDrop = false
                    while (true) {
                        if (failed.get() || !coroutineContext.isActive) return false
                        // Sit out a live cooldown in ≤2s slices so pause/kill
                        // stays responsive; a cancellation here escapes as the
                        // CancellationException the worker handler commits on.
                        while (System.currentTimeMillis() < throttleUntil.get()) {
                            if (failed.get() || !coroutineContext.isActive) return false
                            delay((throttleUntil.get() - System.currentTimeMillis()).coerceIn(0L, 2_000L))
                        }
                        if (attempt >= MAX_ATTEMPTS) break
                        var completed = false
                        var rateLimited = false
                        var hostBackoff = false
                        var dropped = false
                        var connStartedAt = System.currentTimeMillis()
                        var dropWindowStart = connStartedAt
                        var dropWindowBytes = 0L
                        try {
                            // Remember what we ASKED for: if a work-stealer shortens
                            // chunk.end below this while we are mid-read, the call
                            // must be cancelled so OkHttp closes the socket instead
                            // of draining the stolen tail (Fix 3).
                            val requestedRangeEnd = chunk.end
                            val req = Request.Builder().url(url).apply {
                                header("User-Agent", headers["User-Agent"] ?: HttpClient.DEFAULT_UA)
                                headers.forEach { (k, v) -> if (!k.equals("User-Agent", true)) header(k, v) }
                                header("Range", "bytes=${chunk.current}-$requestedRangeEnd")
                                // After a drop, force a brand-new connection: the pool
                                // could otherwise hand back the throttled socket.
                                if (drops > 0) header("Connection", "close")
                            }.build()
                            // A dropped piece promotes the pre-dialed spare
                            // when one is ready: the next attempt starts on an
                            // established connection, hiding the TCP+TLS
                            // handshake the dip used to show. The fallback
                            // stays the old fresh-dial client.
                            val standbyClient = if (drops > 0) standby?.promote() else null
                            val attemptClient = standbyClient
                                ?: if (drops > 0) freshConnectionClient(client) else client
                            val call = attemptClient.newCall(req)
                            trackCall(taskId, call)
                            try {
                                call.execute().use { res ->
                                if (res.code == 206) {
                                    // Audit finding 4: a 206 from the WRONG start
                                    // offset would write the file head at a piece
                                    // offset (silent duplication) — verify the
                                    // server honored the requested Range.
                                    val crStart = res.header("Content-Range")
                                        ?.substringAfter("bytes ", "")?.substringBefore('-')?.trim()?.toLongOrNull()
                                    if (crStart != null && crStart != chunk.current) {
                                        throw java.io.IOException(
                                            "range start mismatch: asked ${chunk.current}, server began at $crStart"
                                        )
                                    }
                                    val src = res.body?.source() ?: throw IOException("Empty response body from server")
                                    val buf = ByteArray(BUFFER)
                                    var pos = chunk.current
                                    var bytesSinceLastCommit = 0L
                                    connStartedAt = System.currentTimeMillis()
                                    dropWindowStart = connStartedAt
                                    dropWindowBytes = 0L
                                    while (pos <= chunk.end && !failed.get()) {
                                        if (!coroutineContext.isActive) {
                                            if (canCommit(taskId)) {
                                                state.commit(plan, total, force = true)
                                            }
                                            return@use
                                        }
                                        val liveEnd = chunk.end
                                        val remainingInChunk = liveEnd - pos + 1L
                                        if (remainingInChunk <= 0L) break
                                        val want = minOf(buf.size.toLong(), remainingInChunk).toInt()
                                        val n = readCoalesced(src, buf, want)
                                        if (n <= 0) break

                                        // Lock-free positional writes: FileChannel.write
                                        // (ByteBuffer, position) is kernel-atomic
                                        // (pwrite64) and each piece owns a DISJOINT byte
                                        // range, so lanes no longer queue behind one
                                        // monitor. The drain loop stays: a short write
                                        // (legal per contract) must surface as a
                                        // retryable failure, never as silent zero holes.
                                        // Re-clamp: a work-stealer may have shortened
                                        // chunk.end while readCoalesced was in flight —
                                        // bytes past the new end belong to the stealer.
                                        val allowedBytes = (chunk.end - pos + 1L).coerceAtLeast(0L).toInt()
                                        val writeLen = minOf(n, allowedBytes)
                                        if (writeLen > 0) {
                                            val bb = ByteBuffer.wrap(buf, 0, writeLen)
                                            var w = 0
                                            while (bb.hasRemaining()) {
                                                val k = channel.write(bb, pos + w)
                                                if (k <= 0) throw java.io.IOException(
                                                    "short positional write at ${pos + w}"
                                                )
                                                w += k
                                            }

    private suspend fun single(

        dest: File,
        headers: Map<String, String>,

        failureStatus: AtomicInteger,
        failureMessage: AtomicReference<String?>,
        onProgress: (Long, Long, Long) -> Unit,
        client: OkHttpClient,
        taskId: String = ""

        val done = AtomicLong(initialBytes)

            while (isActive) {
                delay(250)

                onProgress(currentDone, if (total > 0) total else 0L, currentSpeed)

                        header("User-Agent", headers["User-Agent"] ?: HttpClient.DEFAULT_UA)
                        headers.forEach { (k, v) -> if (!k.equals("User-Agent", true)) header(k, v) }
                        if (resumeAt > 0) header("Range", "bytes=$resumeAt-")
                    }.build()

                    trackCall(taskId, call)

                        call.execute().use { res ->

                                lastRateLimited = res.code == 429 || res.code == 503

                            }

                                return false

                            done.set(startAt)
                            RandomAccessFile(dest, "rw").use { raf ->
                                if (!resuming || raf.length() < startAt) raf.setLength(startAt)
                                raf.seek(startAt)

                    throw e
                } catch (e: Exception) {
                    // One attempt failing (disconnect, timeout) must not abort the
                    // retry loop: record the cause and let the next attempt resume.
                    failureMessage.compareAndSet(null, e.message ?: e.javaClass.simpleName)

                }

                // the CancellationException caught below (a paused job never
                // looks like a failure).
                while (System.currentTimeMillis() < throttleUntil) {
                    delay((throttleUntil - System.currentTimeMillis()).coerceIn(0L, 2_000L))
                }
                if (attemptCount >= MAX_ATTEMPTS) break
                if (attempt()) {
                    success = true

                    // attempt: the next request resumes from dest.length() via
                    // the Range header, after an escalating pause.
                    throttleCycles++
                    val waitMs = (throttleBaseDelayMs shl (throttleCycles - 1).coerceAtMost(5))
                        .coerceAtMost(THROTTLE_MAX_MS)

                        "task=$taskId single stream rate limited (cycle $throttleCycles): cooling ${waitMs / 1000}s"
                    )
                } else {
                    attemptCount++
                    if (attemptCount < MAX_ATTEMPTS) delay(backoffMillis(attemptCount))
                }
            }
        } catch (_: CancellationException) {
            // A paused job never surfaces as a failure.
        } catch (e: Exception) {
            failureMessage.compareAndSet(null, e.message ?: e.javaClass.simpleName)
        } finally {
            telemetryTicker.cancel()
            val finalDone = done.get()
            onProgress(finalDone, if (total > 0) total else 0L, speed.getSpeed())
            if (taskId.isNotEmpty()) {
                throttleDeadlines.remove(taskId)
            }
        }
        return@coroutineScope success
    }
}

/** One segment's byte window plus how far it has been committed to disk. */
/** One segment's byte window plus how far it has been committed to disk.
 *  [end] is @Volatile: a work-stealing sibling may SHORTEN it in flight
 *  (directive Fix 3), and the victim must observe the new end immediately. */
class TurboChunk(val start: Long, @Volatile var end: Long, @Volatile var current: Long)

/**
 * Thread-safe aggregate speed meter utilizing Exponential Moving Average (EMA).
 *
 * Samples at a 250ms cadence. The first ~1 second uses a heavy alpha (fast
 * acquisition) so the readout tracks the real transfer ramp: TCP slow start
 * and fresh sockets make the first windows genuinely slow, and a light EMA
 * from sample one made the displayed speed chase the true speed for ~2.5s —
 * user-visible as "100KB → 400KB → 3MB" long after the transfer was already
 * at full speed. After acquisition it settles to alpha = 0.25 to smooth
 * TCP burst jitter.
 */
class SpeedMeter(initialBytes: Long = 0L) {
    private var lastBytes = initialBytes
    private var lastTime = System.currentTimeMillis()
    private var emaSpeed = 0.0
    private var initialized = false
    private var sampleCount = 0

    @Synchronized
    fun sample(totalBytes: Long): Long {
        val now = System.currentTimeMillis()
        val dt = now - lastTime
        if (dt >= 250) {
            val delta = (totalBytes - lastBytes).coerceAtLeast(0L)
            val instantBps = (delta * 1000.0) / dt
            sampleCount++
            if (!initialized) {
                emaSpeed = instantBps
                initialized = true
            } else {
                val alpha = if (sampleCount <= FAST_ACQUIRE_SAMPLES) 0.6 else 0.25
                emaSpeed = (alpha * instantBps) + ((1.0 - alpha) * emaSpeed)
            }
            lastBytes = totalBytes
            lastTime = now
        }
        return emaSpeed.toLong().coerceAtLeast(0L)
    }

    @Synchronized
    fun getSpeed(): Long = emaSpeed.toLong().coerceAtLeast(0L)

    private companion object {
        /** Samples 2..5 (roughly the first second) run in fast-acquire mode. */
        const val FAST_ACQUIRE_SAMPLES = 5
    }
}

    }

    fun update(taskId: String, transform: (DownloadTask) -> DownloadTask) {
        var clearWindow = false
        _tasks.update { list ->
            list.map {
                if (it.id == taskId) {
                    val updated = transform(it)
                    if (updated.totalBytes == 0L || updated.status != TaskStatus.DOWNLOADING) {
                        clearWindow = true
                    }
                    updated
                } else it
            }
        }
        if (clearWindow) {
            displayWindows.remove(taskId)
        }
        persist()
    }

    fun updateProgress(taskId: String, downloaded: Long, total: Long, speed: Double, eta: Long) {
        val nowMs = clockMs()
        // Cheap drift guard before touching the map (see pruneDisplayWindows).
        pruneDisplayWindows(_tasks.value)
        val window = displayWindows.computeIfAbsent(taskId) { TaskDisplayWindow() }
        // Window record happens BEFORE the state write, from the row as it
        // currently stands plus this tick's bytes: MutableStateFlow.update
        // retries its lambda under contention (progress ticks arrive at
        // 4 Hz per task, several tasks at once), so any side effect inside
        // it would double-append samples. A racing tick self-corrects — the
        // next 250 ms sample re-bases the window, and byte totals are
        // monotonic at both the task level and inside the window.
        var windowReading: Double? = null
        var windowEta: Long? = null
        val current = _tasks.value.firstOrNull { it.id == taskId }
        // Sticky max total: once a size has been reported for this task, no
        // later (reset-shaped) report can shrink the displayed denominator.
        // Tracked on the same per-task window object, raised by the stored
        // row AND this tick's total.
        val stickyTotal = window.maxTotalOf(maxOf(current?.totalBytes ?: 0L, total))
        if (current != null && current.status == TaskStatus.DOWNLOADING) {
            val bytesNow = if (downloaded > 0) maxOf(current.downloadedBytes, downloaded)
            else current.downloadedBytes
            windowReading = window.record(nowMs, bytesNow)
            // Display ETA from the SAME windowed speed: the raw per-backend
            // eta (yt-dlp's literal per-line "ETA 00:05") keeps its raw
            // field, but the card shows the stable value whenever the
            // window knows both a rate and a remaining size.
            if (windowReading != null && windowReading > 0.0 && stickyTotal > 0L && bytesNow < stickyTotal) {
                windowEta = ceil((stickyTotal - bytesNow) / windowReading).toLong().coerceAtLeast(1L)
            }
        }
        _tasks.update { list ->
            list.map {
                if (it.id == taskId) {
                    // First bytes landing flips RESOLVING -> DOWNLOADING here, in
                    // the SAME atomic write as the progress: some backends (Turbo
                    // direct downloads) report progress with no separate status
                    // event, so without this the card sits at "Resolving" with no
                    // bar while the notification already shows live percent.
                    val status = if (it.status == TaskStatus.RESOLVING && downloaded > 0) {
                        TaskStatus.DOWNLOADING
                    } else it.status
                    // Monotonic downloaded bytes: a late telemetry tick racing the
                    // COMPLETED write (or a stale tick after pause) must never
                    // regress the recorded size. Speed/ETA are only meaningful
                    // while actually transferring — writing them on a PAUSED or
                    // COMPLETED task would re-stamp a stale "0.5 MB/s".
                    // A COMPLETED row is closed: the recorded size is the on-disk
                    // file length, not a backend estimate — a late tick racing the
                    // terminal write must never re-stamp downloaded/total.
                    val finalDl = if (it.status == TaskStatus.COMPLETED) it.downloadedBytes
                    else if (downloaded > 0) maxOf(it.downloadedBytes, downloaded) else it.downloadedBytes
                    // Displayed totals cannot regress mid-download (speed readout
                    // fix): the old ">10 GB rows may switch to a <5 GB total"
                    // allowance let a banked-stream reset (yt-dlp's second
                    // "Destination:" line) SHRINK the denominator between its
                    // video and audio stream, so a huge file's percent crept
                    // backwards. max against the sticky per-task maximum kept in
                    // the same in-memory window map instead — refinements only
                    // ever raise the known total; a COMPLETED row stays frozen.
                    val finalTot = if (it.status == TaskStatus.COMPLETED) it.totalBytes
                    else maxOf(it.totalBytes, stickyTotal)
                    val transferring = status == TaskStatus.DOWNLOADING
                    val finalEta = when {
                        !transferring -> 0L
                        eta > 0L -> eta
                        it.etaSeconds > 0L -> it.etaSeconds
                        else -> 0L
                    }
                    it.copy(
                        status = status,
                        downloadedBytes = finalDl,
                        totalBytes = finalTot,
                        speedBytesPerSec = if (transferring) speed else 0.0,
                        etaSeconds = finalEta,
                        // Display smoothing: populated only while actually
                        // transferring (null = "Starting…" until the window
                        // has ~3 s of samples); paused/queued/validating rows
                        // clear both so no windowed value can go stale.
                        displaySpeedBytesPerSec = if (transferring) windowReading else null,
                        displayEtaSeconds = if (transferring) windowEta else null
                    )
                } else it
            }
        }
    }
}

/**
 * Per-task (time, bytes) ring for the DISPLAYED speed — the speed readout
 * fix at the repository chokepoint (investigation/14_player_trace.md §B).
 *
 * Displayed rate = byte delta across the trailing [DISPLAY_WINDOW_MS],
 * not the raw 250 ms EMA (Turbo) or the verbatim parsed yt-dlp/aria line.
 * Until the window spans [DISPLAY_MIN_WINDOW_MS] the reading is null —
 * the UI renders "Starting…" — which kills both the ramp flicker and the
 * 2.4 TB/s resume-priming burst at every consumer of the display fields.
 * ProgressWatchdog compatibility: the RAW task.speedBytesPerSec is written
 * unchanged beside this; nothing here feeds back into it.
 */
internal const val DISPLAY_WINDOW_MS = 4_000L
internal const val DISPLAY_MIN_WINDOW_MS = 3_000L

/** Physical-cap sanity bound (~2 GB/s) for any displayed rate: impossible
 *  bursts (aria/yt-dlp resume recount lines, parsed at face value with a
 *  TB factor upstream) are clamped against the previous sample, and the
 *  final reading is clamped again. */
internal const val DISPLAY_SPEED_CEILING_BPS = 2_000_000_000.0

internal class TaskDisplayWindow {
    private class Sample(val atMs: Long, val bytes: Long)

    private val lock = Any()
    private val samples = ArrayDeque<Sample>()
    private var stickyTotalBytes = 0L

    /** Monotonic known total: refinements raise it, reset-shaped reports
     *  never shrink it. */
    fun maxTotalOf(total: Long): Long = synchronized(lock) {
        if (total > stickyTotalBytes) stickyTotalBytes = total
        stickyTotalBytes
    }

    /**
     * Append a (time, monotonic-bytes) sample and return the windowed rate
     * in bytes/s — null while the window is younger than
     * [DISPLAY_MIN_WINDOW_MS].
     *
     * An impossible burst between two samples is CLAMPED (not dropped:
     * real progress must still register, at the cap) so the whole window
     * stays bounded; byte values never move backwards inside the window.
     * Samples older than the window edge drop on every record, so a
     * pause/resume gap (or a cold start) begins a fresh window that reads
     * null until ~3 s of new samples exist again.
     *
     * Synchronized: the backend's progress coroutine and the watchdog's
     * filesystem bridge can race into the same task's updateProgress —
     * at 4 Hz the lock cost is nil and the window must stay coherent.
     */
    fun record(nowMs: Long, downloadedBytes: Long): Double? = synchronized(lock) {
        val prev = samples.lastOrNull()
        val bytes = if (prev == null) {
            downloadedBytes.coerceAtLeast(0L)
        } else {
            val dtMs = (nowMs - prev.atMs).coerceAtLeast(0L)
            val ceilingBytes = prev.bytes + (DISPLAY_SPEED_CEILING_BPS * dtMs / 1000.0).toLong()
            downloadedBytes.coerceIn(prev.bytes, ceilingBytes)
        }
        samples.addLast(Sample(atMs = nowMs, bytes = bytes))
        // Prune strictly-before the window edge: the survivor becomes the
        // delta base, so the computed span never exceeds the window and a
        // multi-second gap leaves nothing to dilute the rate with.
        val cutoffMs = nowMs - DISPLAY_WINDOW_MS
        while (samples.isNotEmpty() && samples.first().atMs < cutoffMs) {
            samples.removeFirst()
        }
        val first = samples.first()
        val last = samples.last()
        val spanMs = last.atMs - first.atMs
        if (spanMs < DISPLAY_MIN_WINDOW_MS) return@synchronized null
        val rate = (last.bytes - first.bytes).toDouble() / spanMs * 1000.0
        rate.coerceIn(0.0, DISPLAY_SPEED_CEILING_BPS)
    }
}

package com.anonrode.downloader.pipeline

import com.anonrode.downloader.data.net.HttpClient
import com.anonrode.downloader.data.rules.DynamicRulesManager
import okhttp3.HttpUrl.Companion.toHttpUrlOrNull
import java.net.URI
import java.net.URLDecoder

object UrlClassifier {

    private val STREAMING_EXTENSIONS = setOf("m3u8", "mpd", "m3u", "ism", "f4m")
    private val IMAGE_EXTENSIONS = setOf("jpg", "jpeg", "png", "webp")
    private val DIRECT_MEDIA_EXTENSIONS = setOf(
        "mp4", "mkv", "webm", "avi", "mov", "flv", "ts", "m4v",
        "mp3", "m4a", "aac", "flac", "opus", "ogg", "wav",
        "jpg", "jpeg", "png", "webp"
    )
    private val STREAMING_QUERY_REGEX = Regex("""(?:^|&)[^=&]*=(?:mpd|dash|hls|m3u8)(?:&|$)""", RegexOption.IGNORE_CASE)

    /**
     * Safely strips the `preview` query parameter ONLY if it is an actual query parameter,
     * preserving all other query parameters (such as auth tokens or signatures).
     */
    fun stripPreviewParam(rawUrl: String): String {
        val trimmed = rawUrl.trim()
        val httpUrl = trimmed.toHttpUrlOrNull() ?: return trimmed
        val matchingNames = httpUrl.queryParameterNames.filter { it.equals("preview", ignoreCase = true) }
        if (matchingNames.isEmpty()) return trimmed
        val builder = httpUrl.newBuilder()
        matchingNames.forEach { builder.removeAllQueryParameters(it) }
        return builder.build().toString()
    }

    /**
     * Safely extracts the lowercase hostname without credentials, ports, or path segments.
     */
    fun extractHost(rawUrl: String): String {
        val trimmed = rawUrl.trim()
        trimmed.toHttpUrlOrNull()?.host?.let { return it.lowercase() }
        return try {
            URI(trimmed).host?.lowercase() ?: ""
        } catch (_: Exception) {
            trimmed.substringAfter("://", "")
                .substringAfter('@')
                .substringBefore('/')
                .substringBefore('?')
                .substringBefore('#')
                .substringBefore(':')
                .lowercase()
        }
    }

    /**
     * Safely extracts `scheme://host[:port]` for Origin headers.
     */
    fun extractOrigin(rawUrl: String): String {
        val httpUrl = rawUrl.trim().toHttpUrlOrNull() ?: return ""
        val defaultPort = (httpUrl.scheme == "http" && httpUrl.port == 80) ||
            (httpUrl.scheme == "https" && httpUrl.port == 443)
        return if (defaultPort) {
            "${httpUrl.scheme}://${httpUrl.host}"
        } else {
            "${httpUrl.scheme}://${httpUrl.host}:${httpUrl.port}"
        }
    }

    /**
     * Extracts a clean file extension (2..5 alphanumeric chars) from the URL path or
     * `filename=` query parameter, returning null if none is found.
     */
    fun extractMediaExtension(rawUrl: String): String? {
        val httpUrl = rawUrl.trim().toHttpUrlOrNull()
        val lastSegment = httpUrl?.pathSegments?.lastOrNull { it.isNotBlank() }
            ?: rawUrl.substringBefore('?').substringBefore('#').substringAfterLast('/')
        val pathExt = lastSegment.substringAfterLast('.', "").lowercase()
        if (pathExt in DIRECT_MEDIA_EXTENSIONS) {
            return pathExt
        }
        val encodedQuery = httpUrl?.encodedQuery ?: rawUrl.substringAfter('?', "")
        val decodedQuery = httpUrl?.query ?: encodedQuery
        val filenameRegex = Regex("""filename[*]?=[^&;]+\.([a-zA-Z0-9]{2,5})""")
        // LAST filename= wins: repeated query parameters are resolved last-one-wins
        // by virtually every server-side parser (first-match renamed tasks to a
        // thumbnail's extension on double-filename signed URLs).
        val queryExt = (filenameRegex.findAll(encodedQuery).lastOrNull()
            ?: filenameRegex.findAll(decodedQuery).lastOrNull())
            ?.groupValues?.get(1)?.lowercase()
        return if (queryExt != null && queryExt in DIRECT_MEDIA_EXTENSIONS) queryExt else null
    }

    /**
     * A player/bridge URL can hide the real manifest in a query parameter:
     *   https://bridge.example/?url=https%3A%2F%2Fcdn%2Fmaster.m3u8
     * Path-only classification called that a direct `.mp4` and downloaders
     * saved the playlist text as a video (NEPU 10-22 15:39). Decode query
     * values recursively (bounded) and return the first embedded manifest URL.
     */
    fun embeddedStreamingUrl(rawUrl: String, depth: Int = 0): String? {
        if (depth == 0) {
            DynamicRulesManager.unwrapProxyUrl(rawUrl)?.let { return it }
        }
        if (depth > 2) return null
        val query = rawUrl.substringAfter('?', "")
        if (query.isBlank()) return null
        for (pair in query.split('&')) {
            val value = pair.substringAfter('=', "")
            if (value.isBlank()) continue
            val decoded = try {
                URLDecoder.decode(value, "UTF-8")
            } catch (_: Exception) {
                value
            }
            if (decoded.isBlank() || decoded == rawUrl) continue
            if (!decoded.startsWith("http", ignoreCase = true) && !decoded.startsWith("/")) continue
            val low = decoded.lowercase()
            val path = low.substringBefore('?').substringBefore('#')
            if (STREAMING_EXTENSIONS.any { path.endsWith(".$it") } ||
                path.endsWith("/manifest") ||
                path.contains("/manifest.") ||
                path.contains("/hls/")
            ) {
                return decoded
            }
            embeddedStreamingUrl(decoded, depth + 1)?.let { return it }
        }
        return null
    }

    /**
     * Strict adaptive-streaming manifest check.
     * Fixes the bug where a direct video file named "Manifest.S01E01.mp4" matched `low.contains("manifest")`.
     */
    fun isStreamingLink(rawUrl: String): Boolean {
        val low = rawUrl.trim().lowercase()
        val path = low.substringBefore('?').substringBefore('#')
        val ext = path.substringAfterLast('.', "")

        // If the path explicitly ends with a direct media file extension (.mp4, .mkv, etc.),
        // it is NOT a manifest unless the query string explicitly requests an HLS/DASH format.
        // Images and .ts keep falling through to the path/manifest heuristics below:
        // "/hls/master.jpg" style extension-obfuscated manifests must stay streaming.
        if (ext in DIRECT_MEDIA_EXTENSIONS && ext != "ts" && ext !in IMAGE_EXTENSIONS) {
            val query = low.substringAfter('?', "")
            return STREAMING_QUERY_REGEX.containsMatchIn(query) ||
                embeddedStreamingUrl(rawUrl) != null
        }

        if (ext in STREAMING_EXTENSIONS) return true
        if (path.endsWith("/manifest") || path.contains("/manifest.") || path.contains("/hls/") || path.contains(".m3u8")) {
            return true
        }
        if (DynamicRulesManager.isStreamingUrlMarker(rawUrl)) {
            return true
        }
        if (low.contains("kickassanime") || low.contains("playlist.php") ||
            low.contains("/api/orion/")
        ) {
            return true
        }
        // `stream-proxy` was hardcoded here (HLS) AND in LinkResolver
        // (provably-direct) until 2026-10-20. The two contradicted each other
        // and both were wrong: nsrplay's proxy is an opaque endpoint whose
        // BODY decides (a self-referential manifest when it is the decoy, a
        // direct MP4 byte-range when it is the real stream). Classification
        // is evidence-based now — see inspectTerminal() — so no URL-name
        // heuristic for it remains.
        if (embeddedStreamingUrl(rawUrl) != null) return true
        val query = low.substringAfter('?', "")
        return STREAMING_QUERY_REGEX.containsMatchIn(query)
    }

    // ---------------------------------------------------------------- evidence
    //
    // Terminal classification for the download router (2026-10-20). One
    // bounded probe decides what a URL actually IS:
    //   DIRECT_MEDIA     -> TurboDownloader / aria2c (byte-range file)
    //   HLS_PLAYLIST     -> yt-dlp (genuine multi-variant m3u8 / media playlist)
    //   SELF_REFERENTIAL -> reject + poison (a "master" whose every variant is
    //                       itself with a rotated token; nsrplay stream-proxy)
    //   STUB             -> reject + poison (1-byte / sub-1KiB mpegurl decoy)
    //   UNKNOWN          -> no structural verdict; caller keeps its fallback
    //
    // The body check runs ONLY for manifest-shaped responses (mpegurl
    // content-type or .m3u8/.mpd URL or no media extension), so a direct MP4
    // costs exactly the existing 1 KiB probe. Results are cached by
    // host+path (query/token rotates per request; the SHAPE does not), which
    // keeps RulesPipeline validation, LinkResolver acceptance and the
    // DownloadEngine backend decision from re-fetching the same terminal.

    enum class TerminalKind { DIRECT_MEDIA, HLS_PLAYLIST, SELF_REFERENTIAL, STUB, UNKNOWN }

    data class TerminalEvidence(
        val kind: TerminalKind,
        val code: Int = 0,
        val contentType: String = "",
        val totalBytes: Long? = null,
        val reason: String = ""
    ) {
        /** True only for a terminal that a downloader can actually consume. */
        val playable: Boolean
            get() = kind == TerminalKind.DIRECT_MEDIA || kind == TerminalKind.HLS_PLAYLIST
    }

    private const val EVIDENCE_TTL_MS = 5 * 60_000L
    private const val EVIDENCE_MAX_ENTRIES = 128
    private const val MANIFEST_BODY_MAX_BYTES = 32L * 1024L

    private data class EvidenceEntry(val evidence: TerminalEvidence, val expiresAtMs: Long)

    private val evidenceCache = java.util.concurrent.ConcurrentHashMap<String, EvidenceEntry>()

    /** Cache key: origin + path, query deliberately excluded (tokens rotate).
     *  Bridge URLs are the exception: the embedded `url=` IS the media plan,
     *  so different episodes on one bridge path must not share evidence. */
    internal fun evidenceKey(rawUrl: String): String {
        val parsed = rawUrl.trim().toHttpUrlOrNull() ?: return rawUrl.substringBefore('?').lowercase()
        val base = "${parsed.scheme}://${parsed.host}${parsed.port.let { if (it == 80 || it == 443) "" else ":$it" }}${parsed.encodedPath}"
        val embedded = embeddedStreamingUrl(rawUrl) ?: return base
        return "$base?embedded=${Integer.toHexString(embedded.hashCode())}"
    }

    fun cachedTerminalEvidence(rawUrl: String): TerminalEvidence? {
        val key = evidenceKey(rawUrl)
        val e = evidenceCache[key] ?: return null
        if (System.currentTimeMillis() >= e.expiresAtMs) {
            evidenceCache.remove(key, e)
            return null
        }
        return e.evidence
    }

    internal fun rememberTerminalEvidence(rawUrl: String, evidence: TerminalEvidence) {
        if (evidence.kind == TerminalKind.UNKNOWN) return
        if (evidenceCache.size >= EVIDENCE_MAX_ENTRIES) {
            val now = System.currentTimeMillis()
            evidenceCache.entries.removeIf { now >= it.value.expiresAtMs }
            if (evidenceCache.size >= EVIDENCE_MAX_ENTRIES) {
                evidenceCache.keys.take(evidenceCache.size / 2).forEach { evidenceCache.remove(it) }
            }
        }
        evidenceCache[evidenceKey(rawUrl)] = EvidenceEntry(
            evidence,
            System.currentTimeMillis() + EVIDENCE_TTL_MS
        )
    }

    /** Tests only. */
    internal fun clearEvidenceCacheForTests() = evidenceCache.clear()

    fun isManifestShaped(rawUrl: String, contentType: String = ""): Boolean {
        val ct = contentType.lowercase()
        if (ct.contains("mpegurl") || ct.contains("dash+xml")) return true
        if (embeddedStreamingUrl(rawUrl) != null) return true
        val path = rawUrl.substringBefore('?').substringBefore('#').lowercase()
        if (path.endsWith(".m3u8") || path.endsWith(".m3u") || path.endsWith(".mpd") || path.endsWith(".f4m")) return true
        return path.contains("/manifest") || path.contains("playlist")
    }

    fun isDirectByContentType(contentType: String): Boolean {
        val ct = contentType.lowercase()
        return ct.startsWith("video/") || ct.startsWith("audio/") ||
            ct.contains("application/octet-stream") || ct.contains("application/mp4")
    }

    /** True when the URL path itself proves a direct media file. */
    fun isDirectMediaPath(rawUrl: String): Boolean {
        val path = rawUrl.substringBefore('?').substringBefore('#').lowercase()
        val last = path.substringAfterLast('/')
        val ext = last.substringAfterLast('.', "")
        return ext in setOf("mp4", "mkv", "webm", "avi", "mov", "flv", "m4v", "mp3", "m4a", "aac", "flac", "opus", "ogg", "wav")
    }

    /**
     * Structural self-loop detector for a manifest body. Every variant /
     * segment URI that points back to the SAME host+path as the manifest
     * (query-only difference — the rotated token) proves the playlist can
     * never reach media. Comparison ignores the query because that is exactly
     * how the nsrplay proxy loops.
     */
    fun isSelfReferentialManifest(body: String, manifestUrl: String): Boolean {
        if (body.isBlank()) return false
        val uris = mutableListOf<String>()
        for (rawLine in body.lineSequence()) {
            val line = rawLine.trim()
            if (line.isBlank()) continue
            if (!line.startsWith("#")) {
                uris.add(line)
                continue
            }
            URI_VALUE.findAll(line).forEach { m ->
                val v = m.groupValues.getOrNull(1)?.trim().orEmpty()
                if (v.isNotBlank()) uris.add(v)
            }
        }
        if (uris.isEmpty()) return false
        val self = canonicalMediaPath(manifestUrl) ?: return false
        return uris.all { uri ->
            val resolved = HttpClient.safeResolveUri(manifestUrl, uri)
            canonicalMediaPath(resolved) == self
        }
    }

    /** host+path canonical form; null when unparseable. Query/hash dropped.
     *  When the URL is a streaming proxy worker (dash-hls-bridge / ?url=), canonicalizes
     *  the embedded target stream so proxy worker manifests are not falsely flagged
     *  as self-referential loops. */
    internal fun canonicalMediaPath(rawUrl: String): String? {
        val target = DynamicRulesManager.unwrapProxyUrl(rawUrl)
            ?: embeddedStreamingUrl(rawUrl)
            ?: rawUrl
        val parsed = target.trim().toHttpUrlOrNull() ?: return null
        val port = if (parsed.port == 80 || parsed.port == 443) "" else ":${parsed.port}"
        return "${parsed.host.lowercase()}$port${parsed.encodedPath}"
    }

    /**
     * Tiny mpegurl gate: a manifest under [HLS_STUB_MIN_BYTES] that carries
     * neither a variant tag nor a media segment is a decoy, never a playlist.
     */
    fun isTinyManifest(body: String, contentType: String, totalBytes: Long?): Boolean {
        val bytes = totalBytes ?: body.toByteArray(Charsets.UTF_8).size.toLong()
        if (bytes >= LinkResolver.HLS_STUB_MIN_BYTES) return false
        val ct = contentType.lowercase()
        val looksManifest = ct.contains("mpegurl") || body.trimStart().startsWith("#EXTM3U")
        if (!looksManifest) return false
        val hasVariant = body.contains("#EXT-X-STREAM-INF", ignoreCase = true)
        val hasSegment = body.contains("#EXTINF", ignoreCase = true)
        return !hasVariant && !hasSegment
    }

    /**
     * Bounded evidence probe. [referer] is attached to the body fetch (a
     * token-gated CDN may require it; classification must see the real body).
     * Never throws: any transport failure yields UNKNOWN.
     */
    suspend fun inspectTerminal(
        rawUrl: String,
        referer: String? = null,
        tag: String? = "terminal-evidence"
    ): TerminalEvidence {
        if (rawUrl.isBlank()) return TerminalEvidence(TerminalKind.UNKNOWN, reason = "blank")
        // Direct media path is proof enough; no network at all.
        if (isDirectMediaPath(rawUrl) && !isStreamingLink(rawUrl)) {
            return TerminalEvidence(TerminalKind.DIRECT_MEDIA, reason = "media path extension")
        }
        cachedTerminalEvidence(rawUrl)?.let { return it }

        val effectiveReferer = if (!referer.isNullOrBlank()) referer
        else ResolvedHints.refererFor(rawUrl) ?: com.anonrode.downloader.data.rules.DynamicRulesManager.resolveReferer(rawUrl)

        if (isManifestShaped(rawUrl)) {

            // and do one bounded GET (maxBytes = 32 KB) that follows redirects,
            // checks status/Content-Type/body, and caches the verdict.
            val body = try {
                com.anonrode.downloader.data.net.HttpClient.getText(
                    rawUrl, referer = effectiveReferer, tag = tag, maxBytes = MANIFEST_BODY_MAX_BYTES
                ).orEmpty()

                ""

            val bodyBytes = rawBytes.size.toLong()
            val isBinaryMedia = (rawBytes.size >= 8 && String(rawBytes, 4, 4, Charsets.US_ASCII).lowercase() in setOf("ftyp", "moov", "mdat", "styp")) ||
                (rawBytes.size >= 4 && rawBytes[0] == 0x1A.toByte() && rawBytes[1] == 0x45.toByte()) ||
                (rawBytes.isNotEmpty() && rawBytes[0] == 0x47.toByte())
            val ev = when {
                trimmed.isBlank() ->
                    TerminalEvidence(TerminalKind.UNKNOWN, 0, ct, null, "manifest body unreadable")
                isDash ->
                    TerminalEvidence(TerminalKind.HLS_PLAYLIST, 200, ct, bodyBytes, "genuine DASH manifest")
                isBinaryMedia ->
                    TerminalEvidence(TerminalKind.DIRECT_MEDIA, 200, "video/mp4", bodyBytes, "binary media stream")
                !isM3u ->
                    TerminalEvidence(TerminalKind.STUB, 200, ct, bodyBytes, "mpegurl body is not an M3U document")
                isTinyManifest(trimmed, ct, bodyBytes) ->
                    TerminalEvidence(TerminalKind.STUB, 200, ct, bodyBytes, "tiny mpegurl (${bodyBytes}B) with no variants/segments")
                isSelfReferentialManifest(trimmed, rawUrl) ->
                    TerminalEvidence(TerminalKind.SELF_REFERENTIAL, 200, ct, bodyBytes, "every playlist URI points back to the playlist itself")
                else ->
                    TerminalEvidence(TerminalKind.HLS_PLAYLIST, 200, ct, bodyBytes, "genuine playlist")
            }
            rememberTerminalEvidence(rawUrl, ev)
            return ev
        }

        val probe = try {
            com.anonrode.downloader.data.net.HttpClient.probeTerminal(
                rawUrl, referer = effectiveReferer, timeoutMs = 6_000L, tag = tag
            )
        } catch (_: Exception) {
            null
        } ?: return TerminalEvidence(TerminalKind.UNKNOWN, reason = "probe failed")

        val ct = probe.contentType
        val total = probe.totalBytes
        if (total == null) {
            val ev = TerminalEvidence(TerminalKind.UNKNOWN, probe.code, ct, null, "no size proof")
            return ev
        }
        val manifestShaped = isManifestShaped(rawUrl, ct)
        if (!manifestShaped) {
            val kind = when {
                isDirectByContentType(ct) -> TerminalKind.DIRECT_MEDIA
                isDirectMediaPath(rawUrl) -> TerminalKind.DIRECT_MEDIA
                else -> TerminalKind.UNKNOWN
            }
            val ev = TerminalEvidence(kind, probe.code, ct, total, "non-manifest ${ct.ifBlank { "unknown ct" }}")
            rememberTerminalEvidence(rawUrl, ev)
            return ev
        }
        // Manifest: read a bounded head. getText uses the shared client
        // (redirects followed) but the URL was just probe-validated and is
        // host-gated by the caller.
        val body = try {
            com.anonrode.downloader.data.net.HttpClient.getText(
                rawUrl, referer = effectiveReferer, tag = tag, maxBytes = MANIFEST_BODY_MAX_BYTES
            ).orEmpty()
        } catch (_: Exception) {
            ""
        }
        val trimmed = body.trimStart('\uFEFF', ' ', '\r', '\n', '\t')
        val isM3u = trimmed.startsWith("#EXTM3U")
        val isDash = trimmed.startsWith("<MPD") ||
            (trimmed.startsWith("<?xml") && trimmed.contains("<MPD", ignoreCase = true))
        val ev = when {
            trimmed.isBlank() ->
                TerminalEvidence(TerminalKind.UNKNOWN, probe.code, ct, total, "manifest body unreadable")
            isDash ->
                TerminalEvidence(TerminalKind.HLS_PLAYLIST, probe.code, ct, total, "genuine DASH manifest")
            !isM3u ->
                TerminalEvidence(TerminalKind.STUB, probe.code, ct, total, "mpegurl body is not an M3U document")
            isTinyManifest(trimmed, ct, total) ->
                TerminalEvidence(TerminalKind.STUB, probe.code, ct, total, "tiny mpegurl (${total}B) with no variants/segments")
            isSelfReferentialManifest(trimmed, rawUrl) ->
                TerminalEvidence(TerminalKind.SELF_REFERENTIAL, probe.code, ct, total, "every playlist URI points back to the playlist itself")
            else ->
                TerminalEvidence(TerminalKind.HLS_PLAYLIST, probe.code, ct, total, "genuine playlist")
        }
        rememberTerminalEvidence(rawUrl, ev)
        return ev
    }

    /**
     * Generic repair for a doubled scheme produced by a payload template
     * ("https://vidsrc.buzz" + a bound url that already starts with
     * "https://vidsrc.buzz" -> "https://vidsrc.buzzhttps://vidsrc.buzz/...").
     * Only repairs when the text before the second scheme is a BARE ORIGIN of
     * the same host — a legitimate `?url=https://...` parameter carries a
     * path/query before the embedded scheme and is left untouched.
     */
    fun repairConcatenatedUrl(rawUrl: String): String {
        val value = rawUrl.trim()
        val firstScheme = value.indexOf("://")
        if (firstScheme < 0) return value
        val authorityStart = firstScheme + 3
        val authorityEnd = value.indexOfAny(charArrayOf('/', '?', '#'), authorityStart)
            .let { if (it < 0) value.length else it }
        val authority = value.substring(authorityStart, authorityEnd)
        // Host-suffix concatenation: the device log produced
        // `vidsrc.buzzhttps:/…` and `vidsrc.buzzhttps://…`, where OkHttp
        // parsed the whole glued token as the HOST (`vidsrc.buzzhttps`).
        val embeddedInAuthority = authority.indexOf("http", ignoreCase = true)
        if (embeddedInAuthority > 0) {
            val prefixOrigin = value.substring(0, authorityStart) +
                authority.substring(0, embeddedInAuthority)
            val rest = authority.substring(embeddedInAuthority) + value.substring(authorityEnd)
            val normalizedRest = if (rest.startsWith("https:/") && !rest.startsWith("https://")) {
                "https://" + rest.removePrefix("https:/")
            } else if (rest.startsWith("http:/") && !rest.startsWith("http://")) {
                "http://" + rest.removePrefix("http:/")
            } else {
                rest
            }
            if ((normalizedRest.startsWith("http://", true) ||
                    normalizedRest.startsWith("https://", true)) &&
                extractHost(prefixOrigin).isNotBlank() &&
                extractHost(prefixOrigin) == extractHost(normalizedRest)
            ) {
                return normalizedRest
            }
        }
        val second = value.indexOf("://", firstScheme + 3)
        if (second < 0) return value
        val start = value.lastIndexOf("http", second)
        if (start <= 0) return value
        val prefix = value.substring(0, start)
        val rest = value.substring(start)
        if (!rest.startsWith("http://", true) && !rest.startsWith("https://", true)) return value
        val bareOrigin = prefix.trimEnd('/').lowercase()
        val originOk = bareOrigin.matches(Regex("""https?://[a-z0-9.-]+"""))
        if (!originOk) return value
        val prefixHost = bareOrigin.substringAfter("://").removePrefix("www.")
        val restHost = extractHost(rest).removePrefix("www.")
        return if (prefixHost.isNotBlank() && prefixHost == restHost) rest else value
    }
}

private val URI_VALUE = Regex("URI=\"([^\"]+)\"")
