            val anchorSet = java.util.Collections.newSetFromMap(java.util.IdentityHashMap<Element, Boolean>())
            kept.forEach { pair -> pair.first.ctx.element?.let { anchorSet.add(it) } }
            val markerRe = Regex("""(?i)^\s*SEASON\s*(\d{1,2})\s*$""")
            var currentSeason: Int? = null
            for (el in root.getAllElements()) {
                val txt = el.text().trim()
                if (txt.length in 6..28) {
                    val m = markerRe.find(txt)
                    if (m != null) {
                        m.groupValues.getOrNull(1)?.toIntOrNull()?.let { currentSeason = it }
                    }
                }
                if (currentSeason != null && el.tagName().equals("a", ignoreCase = true) &&
                    anchorSet.contains(el)
                ) {
                    markerByAnchor[el] = currentSeason!!
                }
            }
        }

        // Page declaration (3a): "Episode N Added/Fixed" => S(pin)E1..EN,
        // "Episode X-Y Added/Fixed" => S(pin)EX..EY. Only when the anchor
        // count matches the declared count - otherwise it is a changelog.
        val declaration = if (!grouped && pagePin != null) {
            val declRe = Regex("""(?i)episode\s+(\d{1,4})(?:\s*[-\u2013\u2014]\s*(\d{1,4}))?\s+(?:added|fixed)""")
            val m = declRe.find(pageTitleRaw)
            // "Episode N Added" declares 1..N (a count), NOT the single
            // episode N; "Episode X-Y Added" declares X..Y. Treating N as a
            // range start rejected the Ace page (2 anchors vs 1 expected).
            val declaredEnd = m?.groupValues?.getOrNull(2)?.toIntOrNull()
                ?: m?.groupValues?.getOrNull(1)?.toIntOrNull()
            val declaredStart = if (declaredEnd != null && !m?.groupValues?.getOrNull(2).isNullOrBlank()) {
                m?.groupValues?.getOrNull(1)?.toIntOrNull()
            } else 1
            if (declaredStart != null && declaredEnd != null && declaredEnd >= declaredStart) {
                declaredStart to declaredEnd
            } else null
        } else null
        val declarationMatches = declaration != null && kept.isNotEmpty() &&
            (declaration.second - declaration.first + 1) == kept.size

        fun seasonToken(href: String, text: String): SeasonToken {
            for (target in listOf(href, text)) {
                val m = SXX_EYY_TOKEN.find(target) ?: continue
                val raw = m.value
                val style = raw.any { it.isLowerCase() }.toString() + "|" +
                    raw.any { it.isUpperCase() }.toString() + "|" +
                    raw.filterNot { it.isLetterOrDigit() }
                return SeasonToken(
                    season = m.groupValues.getOrNull(1)?.toIntOrNull(),
                    episode = m.groupValues.getOrNull(2)?.toIntOrNull(),
                    raw = raw,
                    style = style
                )
            }
            val eRe = Regex("""(?i)(?:^|[^a-z0-9])e(?:p|pisode)?[\s._-]*(\d{1,4})(?![a-z0-9])""")
            for (target in listOf(href.substringAfterLast('/').substringBefore('?'), text)) {
                val m = eRe.find(target) ?: continue
                val ep = m.groupValues.getOrNull(1)?.toIntOrNull() ?: continue
                return SeasonToken(null, ep, m.value, "")
            }
            return SeasonToken(null, null, "", "")
        }

        val tokens = kept.map { seasonToken(it.first.ctx.href, it.first.ctx.text) }
        val pinSeasonEpisodes = tokens.asSequence()
            .filter { (it.season ?: pagePin) == pagePin && it.episode != null }
            .mapNotNull { it.episode }
            .toSet()
        val tokenSeasons = tokens.mapNotNull { it.season }
        val dominantSeason = tokenSeasons.groupingBy { it }.eachCount().entries
            .sortedWith(compareByDescending<Map.Entry<Int, Int>> { it.value }.thenByDescending { it.key == pagePin })
            .firstOrNull()?.key
        val majorityStyle = tokens.filter { it.season != null }
            .groupingBy { it.style }.eachCount().maxByOrNull { it.value }?.key
        val outlierIndices = tokens.indices.filter { idx ->
            val t = tokens[idx]
            pagePin != null && t.season != null && t.season != pagePin
        }
        val sparseOutliers = outlierIndices.sorted().zipWithNext().all { (a, b) -> b - a > 1 }
        val allowedOutlierCount = maxOf(2, kotlin.math.ceil(kept.size * 0.2).toInt())
        val outlierEpisodesMissing = outlierIndices.all { idx ->
            val ep = tokens[idx].episode
            ep != null && pinSeasonEpisodes.isNotEmpty() && ep !in pinSeasonEpisodes
        }
        val outlierStylesDiffer = outlierIndices.all { idx ->
            val style = tokens[idx].style
            style.isNotBlank() && majorityStyle != null && style != majorityStyle
        }
        // 3b fallback: pin wins a token outlier ONLY with all evidence present.
        val remapOutliers = !grouped && markerByAnchor.isEmpty() && titleRangeMatch == null &&
            !titleNamesOtherSeason && pagePin != null && dominantSeason == pagePin &&
            outlierIndices.isNotEmpty() && outlierIndices.size <= allowedOutlierCount &&
            sparseOutliers && outlierEpisodesMissing && outlierStylesDiffer

        fun nearestPrecedingSeason(index: Int): Int? {
            for (i in index - 1 downTo 0) tokens[i].season?.let { return it }
            return null
        }

        fun sameTitle(a: String, b: String): Boolean =
            a.trim().equals(b.trim(), ignoreCase = true)

        val builtList = mutableListOf<EpisodeItem>()
        val seasonPositions = HashMap<Int, Int>()
        // Specials such as TPN.S02E5.5 keep episode 5 (the identity the
        // season/episode codec can represent) but must not collide with the
        // plain E5 row: the fraction is appended to the title so the
        // duplicate-title net keeps both cards.
        val fractionRe = Regex("""(?i)\bS\d{1,2}E(\d{1,3})[.\-](\d{1,2})\b""")
        fun fractionOfAnchor(ctx: AnchorCtx, expectedEpisode: Int?): String? {
            for (target in listOf(ctx.href, ctx.text)) {
                val m = fractionRe.find(target) ?: continue
                val ep = m.groupValues.getOrNull(1)?.toIntOrNull() ?: continue
                if (expectedEpisode == null || ep == expectedEpisode) {
                    return m.groupValues.getOrNull(2)?.trim()?.takeIf { it.isNotBlank() }
                }
            }
            return null
        }
        kept.forEachIndexed { index, pair ->
            val ctx = pair.first.ctx
            val legacyNums = pair.second
            val token = tokens[index]
            val sectionSeason = pair.first.season
            var season = when {
                grouped -> sectionSeason ?: pagePin ?: 1
                markerByAnchor.containsKey(ctx.element) -> markerByAnchor[ctx.element]!!
                declarationMatches -> pagePin!!
                token.season != null && !(remapOutliers && index in outlierIndices) -> token.season
                else -> pagePin ?: nearestPrecedingSeason(index) ?: dominantSeason ?: 1
            }
            if (season <= 0) season = 1
            val position = (seasonPositions[season] ?: 0) + 1
            seasonPositions[season] = position

            // Combined posts (one anchor, several real episodes) expand from
            // the parsed legacy numbers; a single anchor uses its own token.
            val episodes: List<Int> = when {
                declarationMatches -> listOf(declaration!!.first + index)
                legacyNums.size > 1 -> legacyNums.map { n ->
                    when {
                        n >= 1000 -> n % 1000
                        n >= 100 -> n % 100
                        else -> n
                    }
                }.filter { it > 0 }
                else -> listOf(token.episode ?: deriveNum(ctx, position).coerceAtLeast(1))
            }
            val fraction = if (!grouped) fractionOfAnchor(ctx, token.episode) else null
            episodes.forEach { rawEpisode ->
                var episode = rawEpisode.coerceAtLeast(1)
                // Two anchors naming the same episode but carrying different
                // files are not the same card: an explicit "Episode 1 File"
                // after an already-identified E1 is a positional row (the
                // live nkiri shape). Fractional specials keep their episode.
                if (fraction == null && token.episode != null &&
                    builtList.any { it.season == season && it.episode == episode }
                ) {
                    var fallback = deriveNum(ctx, position).coerceAtLeast(1)
                    while (builtList.any { it.season == season && it.episode == fallback }) fallback++
                    episode = fallback
                }
                // A grouped page whose section header carries no parseable
                // season keeps its plain chain label (the season identity
                // still defaults to 1 for the codec).
                val labelSeason = if (grouped) sectionSeason else season
                var title = seasonLabel(ctx, episode, labelSeason, labelTemplate)
                if (urlSeasonTemplate.isNotBlank() && !grouped) {
                    title = fillSeasonTemplate(urlSeasonTemplate, season, episode, title)
                }
                val seasonScoped = (grouped && sectionSeason != null) || pagePin != null ||
                    markerByAnchor.isNotEmpty() || tokens.any { it.season != null }
                if (seasonScoped && !Regex("""(?i)s\d{1,2}\s*e\d{1,3}""").containsMatchIn(title)) {
                    title = "S%02d E%02d".format(season, episode)
                }
                if (fraction != null) title = "$title.$fraction"
                // Transparency: a remapped/overridden token keeps its raw text.
                val tokenContradicts = token.raw.isNotBlank() && (
                    (token.season != null && token.season != season) ||
                        (token.episode != null && token.episode != episode)
                )
                if (tokenContradicts && !title.contains(token.raw, ignoreCase = true)) {
                    title = "$title (file labeled ${token.raw})"
                }
                val duplicateTitle = builtList.any {
                    it.season == season && it.episode == episode && sameTitle(it.title, title)
                }
                if (duplicateTitle) return@forEach
                builtList.add(
                    EpisodeItem(
                        title = title,
                        url = ctx.href,
                        episodeNum = com.anonrode.downloader.util.SeasonEpisode.encode(season, episode),
                        site = site,
                        season = season,
                        episode = episode
                    )
                )
            }
        }
        var built: List<EpisodeItem> = builtList

        // ---- ordering
        val sortBy = items.optString("sortBy", "none")
        if (sortBy == "captures") {
            built = kept
                .mapIndexed { idx, pair -> idx to pair.first.ctx }
                .sortedWith(
                    compareBy(
                        { numericCapture(it.second.captures, 0) },
                        { numericCapture(it.second.captures, 1) },
                        { it.first }
                    )
                )
                .mapIndexed { newIdx, (_, ctx) ->
                    val episode = newIdx + 1
                    val season = effectiveUrlSeason ?: pagePin ?: 1
                    EpisodeItem(
                        title = if (urlSeasonTemplate.isNotBlank())
                            fillSeasonTemplate(urlSeasonTemplate, season, episode, labelFor(ctx, episode))
                        else if (pagePin != null) "S%02d E%02d".format(season, episode)
                        else labelFor(ctx, episode),
                        url = ctx.href,
                        episodeNum = com.anonrode.downloader.util.SeasonEpisode.encode(season, episode),
                        site = site,
                        season = season,
                        episode = episode
                    )
                }
        } else if (sortByNumber) {
            built = built.sortedBy { com.anonrode.downloader.util.SeasonEpisode.sortKey(it.season, it.episode) }
        }

        // ---- single-episode fallback
        var episodes = built
        if (episodes.isEmpty()) {
            val fb = items.optJSONObject("fallbackSingle")
            if (fb != null) {
                val condition = fb.optString("when", "always")
                val hit = condition == "always" ||
                    (condition.startsWith("hasElement:") && doc.selectFirst(condition.substringAfter(":")) != null)
                if (hit) {
                    episodes = listOf(
                        EpisodeItem(
                            title = fb.optString("title").ifBlank { "Episode 1" },
                            url = showUrl,
                            episodeNum = 1,
                            site = site,
                            season = 1,
                            episode = 1
                        )
                    )
                }
            }
        }

        // ---- optional meta (only when the rules carry a "meta" spec)
        val meta = items.optJSONObject("meta")
        var metaTitle: String? = null
        var metaPoster: String? = null
        var metaSynopsis: String? = null
        if (meta != null) {
            metaTitle = docField(meta.opt("title"), doc, vars)?.trim()?.let { applyTitleCleanup(it, meta.optJSONArray("titleCleanup")) }
            metaPoster = docField(meta.opt("poster"), doc, vars)?.trim()
            metaSynopsis = docField(meta.opt("synopsis"), doc, vars)?.trim()
        }
        // The shipped playbooks carry EMPTY meta blocks (nkiri/anitaku/dramakey/
        // nepu), so providers that trust the pipeline short-circuit with a blank
        // synopsis even though this same document holds the blurb the compiled
        // selector finds. Same-document fallback: zero extra network.
        if (metaSynopsis.isNullOrBlank()) metaSynopsis = fallbackSynopsis(doc)

        // A knownDead host must never reach a task/list: drop dead primary
        // links and dead mirrors here, before the drawer renders them. This is
        // the OTA-side counterpart to the compiled providers' filters.
        val usableEpisodes = episodes.mapNotNull { ep ->
            if (DynamicRulesManager.isKnownDead(ep.url)) return@mapNotNull null
            ep.copy(mirrorUrls = ep.mirrorUrls.filterNot { DynamicRulesManager.isKnownDead(it) })
        }
        return PipelineEpisodes(metaTitle, metaPoster, metaSynopsis, usableEpisodes)
    }

    /**
     * Synopsis from the document the pipeline already fetched. Selector order
     * mirrors the compiled providers (nkiri live-verified: the first
     * `.entry-content p` IS the blurb); meta descriptions rank last because WP
     * SEO plugins sometimes prepend site branding. Instructional paragraphs
     * ("How to download…") are skipped, and the text is capped so a comment
     * dump can never ride in as the story.
     */
    private fun fallbackSynopsis(doc: Document): String? {
        for (css in listOf(
            ".entry-content p", ".post-content p", ".description",
            ".info p", ".details p", ".synopsis",
            "meta[property=og:description]", "meta[name=description]"
        )) {
            val el = doc.selectFirst(css) ?: continue
            val text = (if (el.tagName() == "meta") el.attr("content") else el.text()).trim()
            if (text.length < 24) continue
            if (SYNOPSIS_JUNK.containsMatchIn(text.lowercase())) continue
            return text.take(2000)
        }
        return null
    }

    private val SYNOPSIS_JUNK = Regex("^(how to|download|click here|comment|copyright|tags?|added)\\b")

    private fun numericCapture(captures: List<String>, idx: Int): Int =
        captures.getOrNull(idx)?.toIntOrNull() ?: Int.MAX_VALUE

    /**
     * Episode numbers an anchor itself declares, in document order — the
     * nkiri-class list pages name their locker files "…E17…", "S01E19…", so
     * the number comes off the link instead of the link's position (the
     * Alchemy of Souls skips). Returns every distinct number found so a
     * combined post ("Episode 17 & 18" behind one anchor) expands into one
     * item per real episode; empty means "no self-declared number, fall back
     * to position". Patterns hit the URL first (locker filenames carry the
     * true number) and then the heading/anchor text. SxxEyy tokens with
     * season >= 2 encode season*100+ep when [allowTokenSeasons] says the
     * page's tokened anchors all name the same series (single-show page);
     * on cross-show list pages those tokens are skipped (they name a show
     * the page does not identify).
     */
    private val ANCHOR_NUM_PATTERNS = listOf(
        Regex("""(?i)\bs(\d+)e(\d+)\b"""),
        // no lookbehind — banned class, see NameSanitizer ENGINE RULE; group 1
        // stays the episode number because the prefix is non-capturing
        Regex("""(?i)(?:^|[^a-z0-9])e(?:p)?[\s._-]*(\d{1,4})(?![a-z0-9])""")
    )

    /** First SxxEyy token on a page claim — strict 1..2-digit seasons only so
     *  the season*100 code below can never overflow. */
    private val SXX_EYY_TOKEN = Regex("""(?i)\bs(\d{1,2})e(\d{1,3})\b""")

    /** (season, normalized series prefix) from the locker file's SxxEyy token
     *  ("…/The.Show.S02E01…" -> (2, "theshow")); null when the filename
     *  carries none. The prefix is the series name the file belongs to —
     *  equal prefixes across a page's anchors = one series, not a list page. */
    private fun fileSeasonToken(href: String): Pair<Int, String>? {
        val file = href.substringBefore('?').substringBefore('#').substringAfterLast('/')
        val m = SXX_EYY_TOKEN.find(file) ?: return null
        val s = m.groupValues.getOrNull(1)?.toIntOrNull() ?: return null
        return s to file.take(m.range.first).lowercase().filter { it.isLetterOrDigit() }
    }

    private fun anchorEpisodeNums(ctx: AnchorCtx, allowTokenSeasons: Boolean): List<Int> {
        val numbers = mutableListOf<Int>()
        for (target in listOf(ctx.href, ctx.text)) {
            if (target.isBlank()) continue
            for (re in ANCHOR_NUM_PATTERNS) {
                for (m in re.findAll(target)) {
                    val groups = m.groupValues.drop(1).filter { it.isNotBlank() }
                    val seasonEp = if (groups.size >= 2) {
                        val s = groups[0].toIntOrNull()
                        val e = groups[1].toIntOrNull()
                        when {
                            // Season 1 kept plain: every existing single-season
                            // page numbers 1..N today and the drawer decodes
                            // <100 as season 1 — no reason to renumber it.
                            s == 1 -> e
                            // Season 2+ = season*100 (the codebase drawer/
                            // engine convention) so both seasons of the same
                            // post get distinct chips; still capped by the
                            // same 1..2000 sanity bound below. Only when the
                            // single-series prefix guard passed — on cross-show
                            // list pages the season token names a DIFFERENT
                            // show than the page, so bail (old behavior).
                            s != null && s in 2..99 && allowTokenSeasons -> {
                                val ep = groups[1].toIntOrNull()
                                if (ep != null) com.anonrode.downloader.util.SeasonEpisode.encode(s, ep) else null
                            }
                            else -> null
                        }
                    } else {
                        groups.lastOrNull()?.toIntOrNull()
                    }
                    val n = seasonEp
                    // 1000-base season codes are legal up to season 99 x 999.
                    if (n != null && n in 1..99_999) numbers.add(n)
                }
            }
        }
        return numbers.distinct()
    }

    /** Evaluates one labelChain entry; null means "no hit, try next". */
    private fun evalLabelEntry(entry: Any?, ctx: AnchorCtx, num: Int): String? {
        return when {
            entry == null -> null
            entry == "counter" || entry == JSONObject.NULL -> "Episode $num"
            entry == "text" -> validAnchorText(ctx.text, maxLength = 40, skip = GENERIC_LINK_LABELS)
            entry is String && entry.startsWith("sibling:") -> siblingLabel(ctx.element, entry.substringAfter(":"))
            entry is JSONObject -> {
                when {
                    entry.has("text") -> {
                        val cfg = entry.optJSONObject("text")
                        validAnchorText(
                            ctx.text,
                            maxLength = cfg?.optInt("maxLength", 40) ?: 40,
                            skip = jsonStringList(cfg?.optJSONArray("skip")).ifEmpty { GENERIC_LINK_LABELS }
                        )
                    }
                    entry.optString("regexText").isNotBlank() -> {
                        val re = try { Regex(entry.optString("regexText")) } catch (_: Exception) { null }
                        re?.find(ctx.text)?.let { m ->
                            m.groupValues.getOrNull(1)?.takeIf { it.isNotBlank() } ?: m.value
                        }
                    }
                    entry.optString("regexUrl").isNotBlank() -> {
                        val re = try { Regex(entry.optString("regexUrl")) } catch (_: Exception) { null }
                        val m = re?.find(ctx.href)
                        if (m == null) null
                        else {
                            val tmpl = entry.optString("label")
                            if (tmpl.isNotBlank()) fillCaptureTemplate(tmpl, m.groupValues.drop(1))
                            else m.groupValues.getOrNull(1)?.takeIf { it.isNotBlank() } ?: m.value
                        }
                    }
                    entry.optString("label").isNotBlank() -> fillCaptureTemplate(entry.optString("label"), ctx.captures)
                    else -> null
                }
            }
            else -> null
        }
    }

    private val GENERIC_LINK_LABELS = listOf("Download", "Download Episode", "Download Movie")

    private fun validAnchorText(text: String, maxLength: Int, skip: List<String>): String? {
        val t = text.trim()
        if (t.isBlank()) return null
        if (maxLength > 0 && t.length > maxLength) return null
        if (skip.any { t.equals(it, ignoreCase = true) }) return null
        return t
    }

    /** Season grouping: parses the section's season number out of a field
     *  spec (e.g. `attr:.season-header:data-season` — dramakey declares it;
     *  `selector:.season-number` works where the text carries it). First
     *  integer in the value; 1..99 or null (null = "not season-scoped"). */
    private fun parseSeason(section: Element, seasonSpec: String, vars: Map<String, String>): Int? {
        if (seasonSpec.isBlank()) return null
        val raw = docField(seasonSpec, section, vars) ?: return null
        return Regex("""\d+""").find(raw)?.value?.toIntOrNull()?.takeIf { it in 1..99 }
    }

    /** Grouped-label template: {season}/{num} support the same %d format
     *  knobs as fillCaptureTemplate; {label} embeds the labelChain result.
     *  Without a season the template is ignored (chain label rides alone). */
    private fun fillSeasonTemplate(template: String, season: Int?, num: Int, label: String): String {
        if (season == null) return label
        return try {
            // BOTH braces escaped in every literal-brace pattern: the phone's
            // ICU-backed engine rejects a trailing unescaped `}` that the
            // desktop JVM happily reads as a literal (confirmed root cause of
            // the v3.1.x crash chain — anon_crash.txt). Before this, these
            // three catches ran on-device for every OTA site: renderTemplate
            // silently returned null for EVERY templated URL (playbook sites
            // dead), fillSeasonTemplate dropped its labels to bare, and
            // fillCaptureTemplate leaked "{1}" text into titles.
            Regex("""\{(season|num)(?::(%[^}]+))?\}|\{label\}""").replace(template) { m ->
                when (m.groupValues[1]) {
                    "season" -> formatInt(season, m.groupValues[2])
                    "num" -> formatInt(num, m.groupValues[2])
                    else -> label
                }
            }
        } catch (_: Exception) {
            label
        }
    }

    private fun formatInt(v: Int, fmt: String): String =
        if (fmt.isBlank()) v.toString()
        else try { String.format(Locale.US, fmt, v) } catch (_: Exception) { v.toString() }

    /** Nearest preceding h1-h6/p sibling (of the anchor or its parent) whose
     *  text contains [contains] — the "Episode 3" heading above a locker link. */
    private fun siblingLabel(anchor: Element?, contains: String): String? {        if (anchor == null) return null
        val candidates = listOfNotNull(anchor.previousElementSibling(), anchor.parent()?.previousElementSibling())
        for (el in candidates) {
            val tag = el.tagName().lowercase()
            val isHeading = tag == "p" || (tag.startsWith("h") && tag.length == 2 && tag[1].isDigit())
            val text = el.text().trim()
            if (isHeading && text.isNotBlank() && text.contains(contains, ignoreCase = true)) return text
        }
        return null
    }

    /** Fills {1}, {2}, ... from capture groups; {1:%02d} zero-pads numerics. */
    internal fun fillCaptureTemplate(template: String, captures: List<String>): String {
        return try {
            Regex("""\{(\d+)(?::(%[^}]+))?\}""").replace(template) { m ->
                val idx = (m.groupValues[1].toIntOrNull() ?: 0) - 1
                val value = captures.getOrNull(idx) ?: ""
                val fmt = m.groupValues[2]
                if (fmt.isNotBlank()) {
                    try { String.format(Locale.US, fmt, value.toIntOrNull() ?: 0) } catch (_: Exception) { value }
                } else value
            }
        } catch (_: Exception) {
            template
        }
    }

    private fun applyTitleCleanup(title: String, ops: JSONArray?): String {
        if (ops == null) return title
        var out = title
        for (i in 0 until ops.length()) {
            val op = ops.opt(i)
            out = when {
                op == "trim" -> out.trim()
                op is JSONObject && op.has("removePrefix") -> out.removePrefix(op.optString("removePrefix"))
                op is JSONObject && op.has("substringBefore") -> out.substringBefore(op.optString("substringBefore"))
                else -> out
            }
        }
        return out.trim()
    }

    /** Doc-scoped field specs for episode meta (selector:/attr:/literal:/template:). */
    private fun docField(spec: Any?, doc: Element, vars: Map<String, String>): String? {
        val candidates = when (spec) {
            is JSONArray -> (0 until spec.length()).map { spec.optString(it) }
            is String -> listOf(spec)
            else -> return null
        }
        for (raw in candidates) {
            if (raw.isBlank()) continue
            val v = when {
                raw.startsWith("literal:") -> raw.substringAfter(":")
                raw.startsWith("selector:") -> doc.selectFirst(raw.substringAfter(":"))?.text()
                raw.startsWith("attr:") -> {
                    val rest = raw.substringAfter(":")
                    val css = rest.substringBeforeLast(':')
                    val attr = rest.substringAfterLast(':')
                    doc.selectFirst(css)?.attrValue(attr)
                }
                raw.startsWith("template:") -> renderTemplate(raw.substringAfter(":"), vars) { name -> vars[name] }
                // vars: is doc-scoped-safe (the map is always in hand); self/
                // link:/field: need an anchor or JSON context that doc/section
                // scope does not have — the validator rejects them here.
                raw.startsWith("var:") -> vars[raw.substringAfter(":")]
                else -> null
            }
            if (!v.isNullOrBlank()) return v
        }
        return null
    }

    // ------------------------------------------------------------- primitives

    /**
     * Walks a JSON tree along a dot path. Segment grammar:
     *  - `name`   → object key
     *  - `name[]` → object key whose value is an array; emits each element
     *  - `*`      → every value of an object (dynamic top-level keys)
     * Arrays encountered mid-walk are descended into element-by-element, so
     * `*.all[]` walks {anyKey: [ {all: [items]} ] } — the anitaku shape.
     */
    internal fun walkJson(root: Any?, path: String): List<Any?> {
        if (path.isBlank()) return listOfNotNull(root)
        // Root-array item paths ("$[]" / "$" / "[]"): WordPress REST and the
        // NaijaVault search return a bare JSON array. Without this the first
        // segment looked for a "$" KEY on each element and yielded nothing
        // (the pipeline silently returned 0 cards).
        if (path == "$[]" || path == "$" || path == "[]") {
            return when (root) {
                is JSONArray -> (0 until root.length()).map { root.opt(it) }
                null -> emptyList()
                else -> listOf(root)
            }
        }
        var current = listOf(root)
        for (segment in path.split('.')) {
            if (segment.isBlank()) continue
            val iterate = segment.endsWith("[]")
            val key = if (iterate) segment.removeSuffix("[]") else segment
            val next = mutableListOf<Any?>()
            for (node in current) {
                if (next.size >= MAX_SEARCH_CONTEXTS) break
                val focus: List<Any?> = if (node is JSONArray) {
                    (0 until node.length()).map { node.opt(it) }
                } else listOf(node)
                for (f in focus) {
                    if (f !is JSONObject) continue
                    val targets: List<Any?> = if (key == "*") {
                        val ks = f.keys()
                        val acc = mutableListOf<Any?>()
                        while (ks.hasNext()) {
                            acc.add(f.opt(ks.next()))
                            if (acc.size >= MAX_SEARCH_CONTEXTS) break
                        }
                        acc
                    } else {
                        listOf(f.opt(key))
                    }
                    for (t in targets) {
                        if (t == null || t == JSONObject.NULL) continue
                        if (iterate && t is JSONArray) {
                            for (i in 0 until t.length()) {
                                if (next.size >= MAX_SEARCH_CONTEXTS) break
                                next.add(t.opt(i))
                            }
                        } else {
                            if (next.size < MAX_SEARCH_CONTEXTS) next.add(t)
                        }
                        if (next.size >= MAX_SEARCH_CONTEXTS) break
                    }
                    if (next.size >= MAX_SEARCH_CONTEXTS) break
                }
            }
            current = next
        }
        return current
    }

    /** Dot-path lookup inside one JSON item with `|` fallbacks and an optional
     *  `:before(<char>)` cut (e.g. `release_date|first_air_date:before(-)` → year). */
    internal fun jsonField(item: JSONObject, path: String): String? {
        // :before(<char>) applies to the WHOLE fallback chain, whichever
        // alternative hits — parsing it per-alt would leave early hits uncut.
        val cutIdx = path.indexOf(":before(")
        val cutChar = if (cutIdx >= 0) path.substring(cutIdx + 8).removeSuffix(")").takeIf { it.length == 1 } else null
        val chain = if (cutIdx >= 0) path.substring(0, cutIdx) else path
        for (alt in chain.split('|')) {
            var node: Any? = item
            for (seg in alt.split('.')) {
                // Array indexes in a path ("_embedded.wp:featuredmedia.0.source_url")
                // are how the WordPress REST response exposes the featured media.
                node = when (val current = node) {
                    is JSONObject -> current.opt(seg)
                    is JSONArray -> seg.toIntOrNull()?.let { idx -> current.opt(idx) }
                    else -> null
                }
            }
            if (node == null || node == JSONObject.NULL) continue
            var str = node.toString()
            if (cutChar != null) str = if (str.contains(cutChar)) str.substringBefore(cutChar) else ""
            if (str.isNotBlank()) return str
        }
        return null
    }

    private fun jsonToString(v: Any?): String? =
        if (v == null || v == JSONObject.NULL) null else v.toString()

    /** Pure substitution of {name}; a blank/missing required var fails the
     *  whole template (returns null) so spec arrays can fall through. */
    internal fun renderTemplate(template: String, vars: Map<String, String>, resolve: (String) -> String?): String? {
        return try {
            val sb = StringBuilder()
            var cursor = 0
            val re = Regex("""\{([^{}]+)\}""")
            var matched = false
            for (m in re.findAll(template)) {
                matched = true
                sb.append(template, cursor, m.range.first)
                val value = resolve(m.groupValues[1])
                // TRIAGE (C) tightened to the documented contract: a BLANK
                // bound var must fail the whole render exactly like a missing
                // one — otherwise a multi-var terminal template silently
                // ships a partial URL (host without its path) to the probe.
                if (value.isNullOrBlank() || value == "null") return null
                sb.append(value)
                cursor = m.range.last + 1
            }
            if (!matched) template else sb.append(template, cursor, template.length).toString()
        } catch (_: Exception) {
            null
        }
    }

    private fun stringMapOf(obj: JSONObject?): Map<String, String> {
        if (obj == null) return emptyMap()
        val out = mutableMapOf<String, String>()
        val keys = obj.keys()
        while (keys.hasNext()) {
            val k = keys.next()
            val v = obj.optString(k)
            if (v.isNotBlank()) out[k] = v
        }
        return out
    }
}

                alloc[id] = min
                remaining -= min

            while (remaining > 0) {
                val eligible = entries.filter { (id, g) ->
                    val cap = if (g.hls) g.lanes else g.cap

                val share = maxOf(1, remaining / eligible.size)
                var added = false

                    if (remaining <= 0) break

                    val room = cap - (alloc[id] ?: 0)
                    val add = minOf(share, room, remaining)
                    if (add > 0) {

    fun effectiveHlsLanesForUrl(masterUrl: String, segmentUrl: String?, requested: Int): Int {
        val want = requested.coerceIn(1, LaneBudget.HLS_MAX_LANES)
        fun capFor(url: String): Int {
            if (url.isBlank()) return LaneBudget.HLS_MAX_LANES
            val host = UrlClassifier.extractHost(url)
            // Reuse the OTA overlay + built-in locker caps, then apply the
            // HLS-specific CDN rules (which may be lower).
            val socketCap = effectiveSocketsForUrl(url, LaneBudget.HLS_MAX_LANES)
            val builtIn = HLS_HOST_CAP_RULES.firstOrNull { (domain, _) ->
                host == domain || host.endsWith(".$domain") || host.contains(domain)
            }?.second ?: LaneBudget.HLS_MAX_LANES
            return minOf(socketCap, builtIn).coerceIn(1, LaneBudget.HLS_MAX_LANES)
        }
        return minOf(want, capFor(masterUrl), capFor(segmentUrl ?: masterUrl))
    }

    fun effectiveSocketsForUrl(url: String, requestedSockets: Int): Int {

        // overlay can retune any host (including the capped ones) without an
        // APK; removing the section restores these compiled caps. Same
        // read-through precedence style as DynamicRulesManager.resolveReferer.

            .getContentPolicy().socketCaps.entries
            .firstOrNull { (domain, _) -> host == domain || host.endsWith(".$domain") }
            ?.value
            ?.coerceIn(1, 16)

            .firstOrNull { (domain, _) -> host == domain || host.endsWith(".$domain") }
            ?.value

     * with right now", per process session:

     *  - FAST multiplicative backoff on 429/403/503 (halve immediately; a
     *    rejected request pattern must not be repeated at the old width),
     *  - SLOW additive recovery with hysteresis: +1 only after
     *    [RECOVERY_CONFIRMATIONS] consecutive improving goodput samples.
     *    This is the two-sample rule 188aa09 added for lane SHRINK, applied
     *    symmetrically here so one noisy sample can neither grow nor shrink;
     *  - clamp 1..hostCap at every entry point.
     *

     * the NEXT task on that host at 8 instead of re-tripping, then climbs back
     * only while goodput keeps improving. Keyed by host, so one hot CDN never
     * inherits another host's penalty.
     */
    object HostSocketOccupancy {
        const val MIN_SOCKETS = 1
        const val RECOVERY_CONFIRMATIONS = 2
        const val RECOVERY_IMPROVE_RATIO = 1.05

        private data class State(
            var sockets: Int,
            var lastBps: Double = 0.0,
            var improvingSamples: Int = 0,
            /** Last sample per task, 15s window. Multiple tasks on one host
             *  must not overwrite each other's recovery signal. */
            val latestByTask: MutableMap<String, TaskSample> = mutableMapOf()
        )

        private data class TaskSample(var bps: Double, var atMs: Long)

        private val hosts = LinkedHashMap<String, State>()

        private fun keyFor(url: String): String {
            val host = UrlClassifier.extractHost(url)
            return host.ifBlank { url.take(120) }
        }

        private fun stateFor(url: String, hostCap: Int): Pair<State, Int> {
            val cap = hostCap.coerceIn(MIN_SOCKETS, 16)
            val key = keyFor(url)
            val state = hosts.getOrPut(key) { State(sockets = cap) }
            if (state.sockets !in MIN_SOCKETS..cap) {
                state.sockets = state.sockets.coerceIn(MIN_SOCKETS, cap)
            }
            return state to cap
        }

        /** Occupancy a new task on this host should start at (session memory;
         *  first use of a host starts at its cap). */
        @Synchronized
        fun currentForUrl(url: String, hostCap: Int): Int = stateFor(url, hostCap).first.sockets

        /** 429/403/503: halve NOW, forget any recovery progress. */
        @Synchronized
        fun recordBackoff(url: String, hostCap: Int): Int {
            val (state, _) = stateFor(url, hostCap)
            state.sockets = maxOf(MIN_SOCKETS, state.sockets / 2)
            state.improvingSamples = 0
            state.lastBps = 0.0
            return state.sockets
        }

        /**
         * Goodput sample (aggregate bytes/s). Sockets grow by ONE only after
         * two consecutive samples improve by [RECOVERY_IMPROVE_RATIO]; a flat
         * or regressing sample resets the run (hysteresis). Returns the
         * occupancy the caller should run at.
         */
        @Synchronized
        fun recordGoodput(url: String, hostCap: Int, bps: Double, taskId: String = ""): Int {
            val (state, cap) = stateFor(url, hostCap)
            if (!bps.isFinite() || bps <= 0.0) {
                state.improvingSamples = 0
                return state.sockets
            }
            // Aggregate the latest sample per live task (15s window). With one
            // task this is exactly the old behavior; with two tasks on the
            // same host, alternating 1.2/2.5 MB/s samples no longer reset the
            // other's improvingSamples forever.
            val nowMs = System.currentTimeMillis()
            state.latestByTask[taskId] = TaskSample(bps, nowMs)
            state.latestByTask.entries.removeAll { nowMs - it.value.atMs > 15_000L }
            val aggregate = state.latestByTask.values.sumOf { it.bps }
            val improving = state.lastBps > 0.0 && aggregate >= state.lastBps * RECOVERY_IMPROVE_RATIO
            state.lastBps = aggregate
            if (state.sockets >= cap) {
                state.improvingSamples = 0
                return state.sockets
            }
            if (improving) {
                state.improvingSamples++
                if (state.improvingSamples >= RECOVERY_CONFIRMATIONS) {
                    state.sockets = minOf(cap, state.sockets + 1)
                    state.improvingSamples = 0
                }
            } else {
                state.improvingSamples = 0
            }
            return state.sockets
        }

        @Synchronized
        fun clearForTest() {
            hosts.clear()
        }

        /**
         * In-run recovery of the post-throttle worker cap. The throttle
         * ladder halves the live cap; it may only be restored to [target]
         * when the host's occupancy ACTUALLY GREW in this sample. Without
         * the growth gate a flat sample would silently undo the rate-limit
         * backoff; without this helper the cap would never be restored at
         * all (active workers were not lowered by the throttle).
         */
        fun recoveryMaxWorkers(currentMax: Int, target: Int, occupancyGrew: Boolean): Int =
            if (occupancyGrew && target > currentMax) target else currentMax
    }

    fun allowsPermissiveTlsFallback(url: String): Boolean {
        val host = UrlClassifier.extractHost(url).removePrefix("www.").trimEnd('.')
        if (host.isBlank()) return false
        return com.anonrode.downloader.data.rules.DynamicRulesManager.isPermissiveTls(host) ||
            BROKEN_TLS_INTERMEDIATE_HOSTS.any { domain ->
                val d = domain.lowercase().removePrefix("www.").trimEnd('.')
                host == d || host.endsWith(".$d")
            }
    }
}

package com.anonrode.downloader.pipeline

import android.content.Context
import com.anonrode.downloader.data.rules.DynamicRulesManager
import org.json.JSONObject
import java.io.File

/**
 * Persistent per-host health ledger.
 *
 * The app used to rediscover dead hosts from scratch every session (the
 * jisooido/jiminido lesson) and hammered sites that had already refused us.
 * This ledger remembers success rates per host with an exponential backoff
 * window, seeded by the playbook's knownDead list so fresh installs skip
 * known corpses instantly. Data stays on-device — nothing is uploaded.
 */
object HostHealth {

    private data class Rec(
        var ok: Long = 0,
        var fail: Long = 0,
        var consecutiveFails: Int = 0,
        var lastOkMs: Long = 0,
        var lastFailMs: Long = 0,
        var rate429: Int = 0,
        var lastRate429Ms: Long = 0,
        var lastReason: String? = null,
        // Millisecond timestamps cannot order two events in the same tick;
        // this flag records which one happened LAST (persisted so a restart
        // does not resurrect a rejection the host already answered).
        var lastEventOk: Boolean = false
    ) {
        fun toJson(): JSONObject = JSONObject()
            .put("ok", ok).put("fail", fail)
            .put("consecFail", consecutiveFails)
            .put("lastOk", lastOkMs).put("lastFail", lastFailMs)
            .put("rate429", rate429)
            .put("lastRate429", lastRate429Ms)
            .put("lastEventOk", lastEventOk)
            .apply { if (lastReason != null) put("lastReason", lastReason) }

        companion object {
            fun from(o: JSONObject) = Rec(
                ok = o.optLong("ok"), fail = o.optLong("fail"),
                consecutiveFails = o.optInt("consecFail"),
                lastOkMs = o.optLong("lastOk"), lastFailMs = o.optLong("lastFail"),
                rate429 = o.optInt("rate429"),
                lastRate429Ms = o.optLong("lastRate429"),
                lastReason = o.optString("lastReason").takeIf { it.isNotBlank() },
                // Legacy records carry only the timestamps.
                lastEventOk = o.optBoolean("lastEventOk", o.optLong("lastOk") > o.optLong("lastFail"))
            )
        }
    }

    private const val FILE_NAME = "host_health.json"
    private val records = java.util.concurrent.ConcurrentHashMap<String, Rec>()

    @Volatile
    private var file: File? = null

    fun init(context: Context) {
        file = File(context.filesDir, FILE_NAME)
        try {
            val f = file ?: return
            if (!f.exists()) return
            val obj = JSONObject(f.readText())
            val keys = obj.keys()
            while (keys.hasNext()) {
                val k = keys.next()
                records[k] = Rec.from(obj.optJSONObject(k) ?: continue)
            }
        } catch (_: Exception) {
            // Corrupt ledger -> start empty; health rebuilds as downloads run.
            records.clear()
        }
    }

    private fun hostOf(urlOrHost: String): String = try {
        val u = urlOrHost.trim()
        if (u.contains("://"))
            java.net.URI(u.substringBefore('#')).host?.lowercase() ?: u.lowercase()
        else u.lowercase()
    } catch (_: Exception) {
        urlOrHost.lowercase().substringBefore('/')
    }

    private val EXEMPT_HOST_SUFFIXES = listOf(
        "x.com", "twitter.com", "instagram.com", "tiktok.com",
        "youtube.com", "youtu.be", "facebook.com", "fb.watch",
        "reddit.com", "googlevideo.com", "google.com"
    )

    private fun isExemptHost(host: String): Boolean {
        val h = host.lowercase().removePrefix("www.")
        return EXEMPT_HOST_SUFFIXES.any { h == it || h.endsWith(".$it") }
    }

    /** Compiled dead seeds: hosts confirmed dead from the field (dated
     *  evidence) and skipped WITHOUT burning a request. Distinct from the
     *  OTA knownDead list: the cold-start data.vidsrcme.ru wave
     *  (2026-10-18 activity-log audit §3.3 — ~30 ConnectExceptions per cold
     *  start on every fleet device, 213 failures logged) cannot wait for a
     *  payload rev, so the evidence ships in the APK. A seed stays for the
     *  life of this build by design — the host is TCP-refused fleet-wide and
     *  from desktop networks; removal takes a build. */
    private val COMPILED_DEAD_SEEDS = listOf(
        "data.vidsrcme.ru" // 2026-10-18 — dead since 10-17; host probes must never fire
    )

    private fun isCompiledDeadSeed(host: String): Boolean {
        val h = host.lowercase().removePrefix("www.")
        return COMPILED_DEAD_SEEDS.any { h == it || h.endsWith(".$it") }
    }

    /** Exponential backoff window after consecutive failures:
     *  30s, 1m, 2m — capped at 2m.
     *
     *  The old 1h cap was a disaster with a queue (the 2026-09-02 Suits
     *  batch): 18 staggered tasks all resolve through the SAME locker host,
     *  every real request timeout bumped consecutiveFails again, and the
     *  window ratcheted 15m → 31m → 59m while tasks retried every 10s. To
     *  the user a 1h park is indistinguishable from a dead host. Two minutes
     *  still rides out a transient outage and lets a parked batch visibly
     *  recover. */
    private fun backoffWindowMs(consecutiveFails: Int): Long =
        if (consecutiveFails <= 0) 0L
        else minOf(30_000L shl (consecutiveFails - 1).coerceAtMost(2), 120_000L)

    fun recordOk(hostOrUrl: String, latencyMs: Long = 0) {
        val h = hostOf(hostOrUrl)
        if (h.isBlank()) return
        records.compute(h) { _, v -> (v ?: Rec()).apply {
            ok++; consecutiveFails = 0; lastRate429Ms = 0L
            lastOkMs = System.currentTimeMillis()
            lastEventOk = true
        } }
        persist()
    }

    /**
     * Auto-clears a host's "dead" state on the first sign of life. Distinct
     * from [recordOk] so it can be called BEFORE the response is read (just
     * a 2xx status code is enough — the 50%+ false positive rate on hosts
     * like vdl.np-downloader.com, where the prior 60s backoff blocked the
     * next attempt that would have succeeded, all came from skipping this
     * clear-on-2xx path). The 2xx must be on a request that actually reached
     * the host's response handler — connection-timeout and DNS failures do
     * not produce a 2xx and so do not qualify.
     *
     * Concurrent recordOk() calls are still safe: this method only shortens
     * consecutiveFails and updates lastOkMs; recordOk is the canonical writer
     * for the full Rec state.
     */
    fun clearIfAlive(hostOrUrl: String) {
        val h = hostOf(hostOrUrl)
        if (h.isBlank()) return
        var changed = false
        records.compute(h) { _, v -> (v ?: return@compute v).apply {
            if (consecutiveFails > 0 || lastRate429Ms > 0L || !lastEventOk) {
                consecutiveFails = 0
                lastRate429Ms = 0L
                lastEventOk = true
                changed = true
            }
            lastOkMs = System.currentTimeMillis()
        } }
        if (changed) persist()
    }

    /**
     * Rules-rev state invalidation (Firefox Remote Settings semantics —
     * scratch/ota_rule_engine_design.md §3.7): a new OTA rules version
     * republishes known-dead lists and pipelines, so every parked/dead
     * backoff verdict in this ledger was formed against a DIFFERENT payload
     * than the one about to run. Such verdicts are stale by construction —
     * the share-31 massacre (2,189 fans-out pre-skipped by backoffs earned
     * under old rules) is the live proof. Drops only the backoff JUDGMENT;
     * ok/fail history (and [hasProvenLocker] credentials) and 429 cooldowns
     * are fresh evidence, not stale, so they stay. Called by
     * DynamicRulesManager on an actual version change at activation.
     *
     * @return count of hosts that had an active verdict cleared.
     */
    fun clearBackoffsOnNewRules(): Int {
        var cleared = 0
        for (h in records.keys) {
            records.compute(h) { _, v ->
                if (v == null) return@compute null
                if (v.consecutiveFails > 0) {
                    cleared++
                    v.consecutiveFails = 0
                    v.lastFailMs = 0L
                }
                v
            }
        }
        if (cleared > 0) persist()
        return cleared
    }

    /**
     * P2-7 — diff-based state invalidation (plan slice 7; the scoped
     * refinement of [clearBackoffsOnNewRules]). Clears the backoff JUDGMENT
     * only for hosts covered by [changedTargets] — the set of knownDead /
     * lockerHosts / hostPolicy / pipeline targets whose policy CHANGED or was
     * REMOVED between the previously active payload and the new one. A truly
     * dead host whose policy did not change keeps its live backoff, so an
     * unrelated update never re-hammers it; hosts REMOVED from knownDead /
     * lockerHosts are inside the changed set by construction, which is
     * exactly the confirmed "remembers-dead-after-fix" bug this fixes.
     *
     * Matching is deliberately shard-based (contains in either direction):
     * the playbook addresses hosts by fragments ("jisooido", "megap.")
     * everywhere else in this file's consumers, so a ledger record
     * "cdn.jisooido.net" must match the changed fragment "jisooido". Only
     * the judgment clears — ok/fail history and 429 cooldowns stay, and the
     * exempt-host rule does not apply (this is playbook-scoped, not a
     * failure recording path).
     *
     * @return count of hosts that had an active verdict cleared.
     */
    fun clearBackoffsFor(changedTargets: Set<String>): Int {
        if (changedTargets.isEmpty()) return 0
        val targets = changedTargets.map { it.lowercase().trim().removePrefix("*.") }.filter { it.isNotBlank() }
        if (targets.isEmpty()) return 0
        var cleared = 0
        for (h in records.keys) {
            val hit = targets.any { t -> h.contains(t) || t.contains(h) }
            if (!hit) continue
            records.compute(h) { _, v ->
                if (v == null) return@compute null
                if (v.consecutiveFails > 0) {
                    cleared++
                    v.consecutiveFails = 0
                    v.lastFailMs = 0L
                }
                v
            }
        }
        if (cleared > 0) persist()
        return cleared
    }

    fun recordFail(hostOrUrl: String, rateLimited: Boolean = false, reason: String? = null) {
        val h = hostOf(hostOrUrl)
        if (h.isBlank() || isExemptHost(h)) return
        // A USER-INITIATED cancellation (search typing, task pause) surfaces
        // as an IOException: Canceled. That is NOT a host failure — recording
        // it poisoned nepu.gd with a 60s backoff every time the user typed
        // fast in search (live-verified). The reason comes from the CALLER
        // (the resolver's per-attempt failure), never the global
        // HttpClient.lastFailure, which is stale for resolvers with their own
        // OkHttp clients and would misattribute both ways.
        val failure = reason ?: ""
        if (failure.contains("Canceled", ignoreCase = true) ||
            failure.contains("CancellationException", ignoreCase = true) ||
            failure.contains("abort", ignoreCase = true)) {
            return
        }
        // A TIMEOUT is not proof of death: a loaded locker under a burst of 18
        // queued tasks will time out one request while serving the next one
        // fine (the 2026-09-02 Suits disaster — loadedfiles.net completed
        // downloads minutes before and after the "dead" verdict). If the host
        // has served us within the last 10 minutes, a timeout only PAUSES the
        // backoff clock; it must never ratchet consecutiveFails up, or one
        // busy period flags the whole host dead and mass-parks the queue.
        val isTimeout = failure.contains("timeout", ignoreCase = true) ||
            failure.contains("timed out", ignoreCase = true)
        records.compute(h) { _, v -> (v ?: Rec()).apply {
            fail++
            if (rateLimited) {
                rate429++
                lastRate429Ms = System.currentTimeMillis()
            }
            if (reason != null && reason.isNotBlank()) {
                lastReason = reason
            }
            val provenRecently = lastOkMs > 0 &&
                System.currentTimeMillis() - lastOkMs < 10 * 60_000L
            if (!(isTimeout && provenRecently)) {
                consecutiveFails = (consecutiveFails + 1).coerceAtMost(20)
            }
            lastFailMs = System.currentTimeMillis()
            lastEventOk = false
        } }
        persist()
    }

    /** Last recorded failure reason for this host, if any. */
    fun lastReason(urlOrHost: String): String? = records[hostOf(urlOrHost)]?.lastReason

    /** False when this URL's host is playbook-known-dead or currently inside
     *  its backoff window. Callers skip the host WITHOUT burning a request. */
    fun isUsable(urlOrHost: String): Boolean {
        val h = hostOf(urlOrHost)
        if (isExemptHost(h)) return true
        if (isCompiledDeadSeed(h)) return false
        if (DynamicRulesManager.isKnownDead(urlOrHost)) return false
        val r = records[h] ?: return true
        val sinceLastFail = System.currentTimeMillis() - r.lastFailMs
        val sinceLast429 = System.currentTimeMillis() - r.lastRate429Ms
        // If the host explicitly returned HTTP 429 (Rate Limited), honor a minimum
        // 30s cooldown immediately so we do not hammer the server into a hard ban.
        if (r.lastRate429Ms > 0L && sinceLast429 < 30_000L) return false
        // Backoff only after >= 3 CONSECUTIVE hard failures: a single hiccup
        // (one 404, one timeout) must not gate a host for 30s+ — search
        // cancellations and flaky single requests used to kill hosts
        // (live-verified: nepu.gd backoff after fast search typing).
        if (r.consecutiveFails < 3) return true
        return sinceLastFail >= backoffWindowMs(r.consecutiveFails)
    }

    /** Milliseconds until [isUsable] becomes true again — 0 when the host is
     *  usable or has no record. Powers the cooldown-parking message and its
     *  auto-retry loop (the engine parks a task while this is > 0). */
    fun remainingBackoffMs(urlOrHost: String): Long {
        val h = hostOf(urlOrHost)
        if (isExemptHost(h)) return 0L
        val r = records[h] ?: return 0L
        val elapsed = System.currentTimeMillis() - r.lastFailMs
        val sinceLast429 = System.currentTimeMillis() - r.lastRate429Ms
        if (r.lastRate429Ms > 0L && sinceLast429 < 30_000L) {
            return maxOf(0L, 30_000L - sinceLast429)
        }
        if (r.consecutiveFails < 3) return 0L
        val window = backoffWindowMs(r.consecutiveFails)
        return maxOf(0L, window - elapsed)
    }

    /** True when this host has successfully served at least one stream —
     *  evidence-based proof it is a working locker. The playbook seeds known
     *  hosts, but any host that proves itself in the field is treated as
     *  known from then on (LockerRegistry.classify), no OTA needed. */
    fun hasProvenLocker(hostOrUrl: String): Boolean =
        (records[hostOf(hostOrUrl)]?.ok ?: 0L) >= 1L

    /**
     * Session hard block (investigation 11 R1 / fix row 10): the host's most
     * recent transport verdict was a NAMED edge rejection — HTTP 403 or 436
     * (Cloudflare-style bot walls; recorded by HttpClient's
     * HttpStatusCodeException branch as reason "HTTP <code> ...", and equally
     * by resolvers whose failure text embeds the code). Distinct from
     * [isUsable]'s consecutive-fails backoff (which a single failure cannot
     * trigger): one 436 must skip the host for the session window NOW, or the
     * resolver chain re-fights the same rejection until the task dies
     * ("resolver chain EMPTY", mayonaka-punch 5× 436 in one resolve).
     *
     * TTL-bounded (15 min, persisted via the same lastFailMs field so the
     * ledger needs no new schema) and overruled by any later success:
     * recordOk/clearIfAlive move lastOkMs past lastFailMs. Exempt hosts
     * (social/video app hosts) never block.
     */
    fun hardBlockActive(hostOrUrl: String): Boolean {
        val h = hostOf(hostOrUrl)
        if (h.isBlank() || isExemptHost(h)) return false
        val r = records[h] ?: return false
        val reason = r.lastReason?.lowercase() ?: return false
        if (HARD_BLOCK_REASONS.none { reason.contains(it) }) return false
        val sinceFail = System.currentTimeMillis() - r.lastFailMs
        if (sinceFail < 0L || sinceFail >= HARD_BLOCK_TTL_MS) return false
        // A proven sign of life AFTER the rejection lifts the block. The
        // boolean (not lastOkMs <= lastFailMs) keeps same-millisecond
        // ordering correct in both directions.
        return !r.lastEventOk
    }

    private const val HARD_BLOCK_TTL_MS = 15 * 60_000L
    private val HARD_BLOCK_REASONS = listOf("http 403", "http 436")

    /** Debug summary for the activity log (bounded to the hottest entries). */
    fun snapshotForLog(limit: Int = 12): String {
        return records.entries.take(limit).joinToString(", ") { (k, v) ->
            "$k(ok=${v.ok},fail=${v.fail},429=${v.rate429})"
        }
    }

    private val persistLock = Any()

    private fun persist() {
        synchronized(persistLock) {
            try {
                val f = file ?: return
                val obj = JSONObject()
                records.entries.take(500).forEach { (k, v) -> obj.put(k, v.toJson()) }
                val tmp = File(f.parentFile, f.name + ".tmp")
                tmp.writeText(obj.toString())
                if (!tmp.renameTo(f)) {
                    f.delete()
                    tmp.renameTo(f)
                }
            } catch (_: Exception) {}
        }
    }
}
